chapters.name: Arjuna Visada Yoga
chapters.summary: Arjuna sees his own family on the other side of the battlefield and completely breaks down. Full anxiety spiral. The whole Gita starts here.

chapters.name: Sankhya Yoga
chapters.summary: Krishna's crash course: you're more than your body, do the work without obsessing over results, keep your mind steady. Read one chapter? Read this.

chapters.name: Karma Yoga
chapters.summary: Running from responsibility isn't peace. Do your part, do it for something bigger than yourself, and don't make it all about you.

chapters.name: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
chapters.meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
chapters.summary: This wisdom is ancient, and Krishna returns whenever the world needs a reset. Work without ego and let wisdom burn away your past.

chapters.name: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
chapters.summary: Quitting versus doing? Doing your work without attachment wins. Find joy inside and outside pleasures lose their grip.

chapters.name: Dhyana Yoga
chapters.summary: The meditation chapter. Your mind can be your best friend or worst enemy. Balance, practice and patience train it.

chapters.name: Gyaan Vigyana Yoga
chapters.summary: Krishna is the thread running through everything: the taste of water, the light of the sun. Look closer and you'll see him everywhere.

chapters.name: Akshara Brahma Yoga
chapters.summary: What you think about most is where you end up. Remember the divine always, even at the very end.

chapters.name: Raja Vidya Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through the King of Sciences
chapters.summary: The royal secret: a leaf, a flower or some water offered with love is enough. Turn your whole life into an offering.

chapters.name: Vibhooti Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God
chapters.summary: Wherever you see brilliance, beauty or power, that's a spark of the divine. Krishna lists his best appearances.

chapters.name: Vishwaroopa Darshana Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God
chapters.summary: The big reveal. Arjuna sees Krishna's cosmic form, as bright as a thousand suns, and learns he's just the instrument.

chapters.name: Bhakti Yoga
chapters.summary: The love chapter. Can't focus? Practise. Can't practise? Serve. Can't serve? Let go of results. There's a path for everyone.

chapters.name: Ksetra Ksetrajna Vibhaaga Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field
chapters.summary: Your body is the field, your soul is the knower. Learn the difference and you see the same divine in everyone.

chapters.name: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
chapters.summary: Three energies run your moods: clarity, hustle and laziness. Notice which is in charge, then rise above all three.

chapters.name: Purushottama Yoga
chapters.meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
chapters.summary: Life is an upside-down tree rooted in the divine. Cut through attachment and find the Supreme Person beyond it all.

chapters.name: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
chapters.summary: Green flags versus red flags of the soul. Lust, anger and greed are the three exits to avoid.

chapters.name: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
chapters.summary: You are what you believe. Food, discipline and giving each come in pure, hyped and lazy versions.

chapters.name: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
chapters.summary: The finale. Do your own work, let go of results, trust the divine completely. Arjuna's confusion is gone. Glow-up complete.

verses.en: Dhritarashtra said: Sanjaya, on the holy field of Kurukshetra, my sons and the sons of Pandu gathered, eager to fight. What did they do?
verses.hi: धृतराष्ट्र ने कहा: संजय, धर्मभूमि कुरुक्षेत्र में युद्ध के लिए इकट्ठा हुए मेरे पुत्रों और पांडु के पुत्रों ने क्या किया?
verses.short: Blind King Dhritarashtra asks: "What's happening on the battlefield?" The whole Gita is the answer to this one anxious question.
verses.notes: Why does the Gita start with Dhritarashtra's question? The blind king can't see the battlefield, so he asks Sanjaya what is happening. The whole Gita is Sanjaya's answer. Why call Kurukshetra a 'holy field'? It was a sacred place long before the war. The war of duty is fought on a field of dharma.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Seeing the Pandava army lined up for battle, King Duryodhana went to his teacher Drona and spoke.
verses.hi: संजय ने कहा: पांडवों की सेना को व्यूह में खड़ा देखकर राजा दुर्योधन अपने गुरु द्रोणाचार्य के पास गया और बोला।
verses.short: Duryodhana sees the other army lined up and runs straight to his teacher. Nervous energy, trying to look confident.
verses.notes: Why does Duryodhana go to Drona first? Seeing the Pandava army lined up, he feels uneasy and goes to his teacher, looking for reassurance. What does this tell us about Duryodhana? Despite his large army, he is anxious. Outer strength doesn't remove inner fear.

verses.en: Teacher, look at this huge army of Pandu's sons, arranged by your own clever student, Drupada's son.
verses.hi: गुरुदेव, पांडु-पुत्रों की इस विशाल सेना को देखिए, जिसे आपके ही बुद्धिमान शिष्य, द्रुपद के पुत्र ने सजाया है।
verses.short: "Look, teacher, your own student is leading their army." Duryodhana throwing subtle shade at Drona.
verses.notes: Who is the 'son of Drupada'? Dhrishtadyumna, the commander of the Pandava army, who was once Drona's own student. Why does Duryodhana point this out? To needle Drona: his own student is now leading the army against him.

verses.en: Here are heroes and great archers, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata and the mighty warrior Drupada.
verses.hi: इसमें भीम और अर्जुन जैसे बड़े धनुर्धारी वीर हैं: युयुधान, विराट और महारथी द्रुपद।
verses.short: Duryodhana lists the legends on the other side: Bhima, Arjuna, and big names. He's lowkey scared.
verses.notes: Who are the heroes named here? Great archers like Bhima and Arjuna, and warriors Yuyudhana (Satyaki), Virata and Drupada on the Pandava side. Why does Duryodhana list enemy heroes? He is sizing up the threat, and his worry shows in how he names them first.

verses.en: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the brave king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, Shaibya the best of men, the bold Yudhamanyu and the strong Uttamauja,
verses.hi: धृष्टकेतु, चेकितान, पराक्रमी काशीराज, पुरुजित, कुंतिभोज, श्रेष्ठ पुरुष शैब्य, साहसी युधामन्यु और बलवान उत्तमौजा,
verses.short: More heavy hitters on the Pandava side. Duryodhana keeps counting threats instead of trusting his own team.
verses.notes: Who are Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana and the others? Kings and warriors allied with the Pandavas, including the king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaibya. What does this list show? The Pandavas had strong allies from many kingdoms, which worried Duryodhana.

verses.en: Subhadra's son and the sons of Draupadi: all of them great chariot warriors.
verses.hi: सुभद्रा का पुत्र और द्रौपदी के पुत्र: ये सभी महारथी हैं।
verses.short: Young warriors too, including Abhimanyu and Draupadi's sons. Every name makes Duryodhana more anxious.
verses.notes: Who is the son of Subhadra? Abhimanyu, Arjuna's young and brave son, famous for entering the chakravyuha formation. Who are the sons of Draupadi? The five sons Draupadi had with the five Pandava brothers, all skilled warriors.

verses.en: Now hear, best of the twice-born, about the leaders of my own army. I name them for you.
verses.hi: हे द्विजश्रेष्ठ, अब हमारी सेना के प्रमुख नायकों को भी जान लीजिए। मैं आपको उनके नाम बताता हूँ।
verses.short: Now he hypes his own side: "Let me remind you of our commanders." Classic pep talk to calm himself down.
verses.notes: Why does Duryodhana now name his own commanders? After listing the enemy, he turns to his own side to reassure himself and Drona. Why call Drona 'best of Brahmanas'? It is a respectful title, but Duryodhana uses it to flatter Drona and keep him loyal.

verses.en: You yourself, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa who wins every fight, Ashvatthama, Vikarna and Somadatta's son.
verses.hi: आप स्वयं, भीष्म, कर्ण, युद्ध जीतने वाले कृपाचार्य, अश्वत्थामा, विकर्ण और सोमदत्त का पुत्र।
verses.short: Drona, Bhishma, Karna and more. Duryodhana flexing his roster like a fantasy team.
verses.notes: Who are the Kaurava leaders named here? Drona himself, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna and Jayadratha, also called the son of Somadatta in some readings. Why does he name Drona first? He is speaking to Drona, so naming him first is both courtesy and flattery.

verses.en: And many other heroes, ready to give their lives for me, armed with all kinds of weapons and skilled in war.
verses.hi: और भी बहुत से वीर हैं जो मेरे लिए जान देने को तैयार हैं, तरह-तरह के शस्त्रों से लैस और युद्ध में निपुण।
verses.short: "So many heroes ready to die for me." When your confidence depends on others, it's shaky.
verses.notes: Who are the 'many other heroes'? Countless warriors ready to give their lives for Duryodhana, skilled with many weapons. What does 'for my sake' reveal? Duryodhana sees the war as his personal cause, showing his ego.

verses.en: Our strength, guarded by Bhishma, seems hard to measure; their strength, guarded by Bhima, seems limited.
verses.hi: भीष्म से रक्षित हमारी सेना अपार है, और भीम से रक्षित उनकी सेना सीमित है।
verses.short: "Our army feels weak, theirs feels strong." Comparing yourself to others always messes with your head.
verses.notes: What does Duryodhana mean by 'inadequate' and 'adequate'? Readings differ: either his army is unlimited and theirs limited, or he secretly fears his own force falls short. Both show his inner unease. Why contrast Bhishma and Bhima? Bhishma guards the Kauravas and Bhima the Pandavas. He is comparing the two pillars of each side.

verses.en: So all of you, holding your posts at every entrance, must above all protect Bhishma.
verses.hi: इसलिए आप सब अपने-अपने मोर्चों पर डटे रहकर हर तरह से भीष्म की रक्षा करें।
verses.short: "Everyone, protect Bhishma at all costs!" Duryodhana's whole plan rests on one person. Risky strategy.
verses.notes: Why must everyone guard Bhishma? Bhishma is the Kauravas' chief strength. If he falls, their army loses its backbone. What does this order show? Duryodhana's plan depends heavily on one man, revealing his insecurity.

verses.en: To cheer Duryodhana, the grand old Bhishma, eldest of the Kurus, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly.
verses.hi: दुर्योधन का उत्साह बढ़ाने के लिए कुरुवंश के वृद्ध पितामह भीष्म ने सिंह जैसी गर्जना की और ज़ोर से शंख बजाया।
verses.short: Bhishma roars and blows his conch to boost Duryodhana's mood. The grandpa hype man moment.
verses.notes: Why does Bhishma blow his conch? To cheer up the worried Duryodhana and signal that the battle is about to begin. What does 'roared like a lion' suggest? Bhishma's power and courage, even in old age.

verses.en: Then conches, kettledrums, tabors, drums and horns all sounded at once, and the noise was deafening.
verses.hi: फिर शंख, नगाड़े, ढोल, मृदंग और नरसिंघे एक साथ बज उठे, और बहुत भयंकर शोर हुआ।
verses.short: Conches, drums, horns all at once. The noise is insane. Battle soundtrack: on.
verses.notes: What happens after Bhishma's conch? The whole Kaurava army joins in with conchs, drums and horns, creating a huge uproar. Why describe the noise? It sets the scene: the war is no longer a threat but about to begin.

verses.en: Then Krishna and Arjuna, standing in a great chariot drawn by white horses, blew their divine conches.
verses.hi: तब सफ़ेद घोड़ों वाले विशाल रथ पर बैठे श्रीकृष्ण और अर्जुन ने अपने दिव्य शंख बजाए।
verses.short: Krishna and Arjuna, on a chariot with white horses, blow their divine conches. Main characters have entered.
verses.notes: Why mention the white horses? White symbolises purity and goodness, marking Krishna and Arjuna's chariot as special. Why are their conchs called divine? They were gifts from the gods, showing that divine support is with the Pandavas.

verses.en: Krishna blew Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and Bhima, the doer of mighty deeds, blew the great conch Paundra.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने पांचजन्य, अर्जुन ने देवदत्त, और भयंकर कर्म करने वाले भीम ने पौण्ड्र नाम का महाशंख बजाया।
verses.short: Every hero has a named conch, like a signature sound. Krishna's is Panchajanya. Iconic.
verses.notes: What are the names of the conchs? Krishna's is Panchajanya, Arjuna's is Devadatta and Bhima's is Paundra. Why do conchs have names? Like famous weapons, they carried identity and history, and their sounds were recognised on the battlefield.

verses.en: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
verses.hi: कुंती-पुत्र राजा युधिष्ठिर ने अनंतविजय, और नकुल-सहदेव ने सुघोष और मणिपुष्पक शंख बजाए।
verses.short: Yudhishthira, Nakula and Sahadeva join in. The Pandava brothers are fully in sync.
verses.notes: Which conchs do the other Pandavas blow? Yudhishthira blows Anantavijaya, Nakula blows Sughosha and Sahadeva blows Manipushpaka. Why list each brother? It shows the Pandavas standing united, each ready to play his part.

verses.en: The great archer king of Kashi, the mighty Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata and the unbeaten Satyaki,
verses.hi: श्रेष्ठ धनुर्धर काशीराज, महारथी शिखंडी, धृष्टद्युम्न, विराट और अजेय सात्यकि,
verses.short: More warriors answer the call. The Pandava side is loud, united and ready.
verses.notes: Who joins the Pandavas in blowing conchs? The king of Kashi, Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata and the unbeaten Satyaki. Who is Shikhandi? A warrior who later plays a key role in Bhishma's fall.

verses.en: Drupada, the sons of Draupadi and the strong-armed son of Subhadra, O King, each blew his own conch.
verses.hi: हे राजन, द्रुपद, द्रौपदी के पुत्र और महाबाहु सुभद्रा-पुत्र, सभी ने अलग-अलग अपने शंख बजाए।
verses.short: Everyone blows their conch again and again. It's a full squad roll call.
verses.notes: Who else blows their conchs? Drupada, Draupadi's sons and Abhimanyu, again and again. What is the effect of so many conchs? A wave of sound that shows the Pandavas' confidence and unity.

verses.en: That roar filled the sky and the earth and tore at the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.
verses.hi: उस भयंकर आवाज़ ने आकाश और धरती को गुंजा दिया और धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों के दिल दहला दिए।
verses.short: The sound shakes earth and sky, and the Kauravas feel it in their hearts. Unity is loud.
verses.notes: Why did the sound shake the Kauravas? The roar echoed through earth and sky and pierced their hearts, a sign of fear on the side that started the wrong. Why doesn't the Pandava side feel the same? Those who stand for what is right carry less inner fear.

verses.en: Then Arjuna, whose flag bears Hanuman, saw Dhritarashtra's sons in position. As weapons were about to fly, he raised his bow and spoke these words to Krishna, O King.
verses.hi: हे राजन, तब हनुमान के ध्वज वाले अर्जुन ने धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को मोर्चे पर खड़ा देखा। जब शस्त्र चलने ही वाले थे, उसने धनुष उठाया और श्रीकृष्ण से ये वचन कहे।
verses.short: Arjuna, Hanuman on his flag, picks up his bow. The fight is about to begin.
verses.notes: What is on Arjuna's flag? Hanuman, the great devotee, who is said to protect the chariot. What is Arjuna doing at this moment? He lifts his bow as arrows are about to fly, ready to fight.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Achyuta, place my chariot between the two armies,
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे अच्युत, मेरा रथ दोनों सेनाओं के बीच खड़ा कीजिए,
verses.short: Arjuna: "Krishna, take my chariot to the middle." He wants a clear look before the battle.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask Krishna? To drive the chariot between the two armies so he can see who he will fight. Why is Krishna driving? Krishna chose to be Arjuna's charioteer and not fight. He guides rather than commands.

verses.en: so I can look at those standing here eager for war, and see whom I must fight in this battle.
verses.hi: ताकि मैं देख सकूँ कि युद्ध की इच्छा से कौन-कौन खड़े हैं और इस लड़ाई में मुझे किन-किन से लड़ना है।
verses.short: "Let me see who I'm actually up against." Smart move. Know what you're facing.
verses.notes: Why does Arjuna want to see his opponents? To know exactly who stands against him before the battle starts. What happens because of this request? Seeing their faces up close is what triggers Arjuna's crisis.

verses.en: I want to see those who have come here to fight, wanting to please Duryodhana, the wicked-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
verses.hi: मैं उन्हें देखना चाहता हूँ जो दुष्ट बुद्धि वाले दुर्योधन को खुश करने के लिए यहाँ लड़ने आए हैं।
verses.short: Arjuna wants to see who showed up to support Duryodhana's bad choices.
verses.notes: Who is the 'evil-minded son'? Duryodhana, whose greed and scheming caused this war. What is Arjuna's mood here? Still confident and ready to fight those siding with wrongdoing.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: O King, asked this by Arjuna, Krishna drove the fine chariot between the two armies,
verses.hi: संजय ने कहा: हे भारत, अर्जुन के ऐसा कहने पर श्रीकृष्ण ने उस उत्तम रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के बीच खड़ा किया,
verses.short: Krishna parks the chariot right in front of Bhishma and Drona and says: "Look at them." Plot twist loading.
verses.notes: Where does Krishna place the chariot? Between the two armies, right in front of Bhishma and Drona. Why stop in front of Bhishma and Drona? They are the people Arjuna loves and respects most, which brings his inner conflict into focus.

verses.en: facing Bhishma, Drona and all the kings, and said: Arjuna, look at all these Kurus gathered here.
verses.hi: भीष्म, द्रोण और सभी राजाओं के सामने, और कहा: हे पार्थ, यहाँ इकट्ठे हुए इन कौरवों को देखो।
verses.short: Krishna's "look at them" is deliberate. He knows exactly what Arjuna is about to feel.
verses.notes: What does Krishna say? 'Arjuna, behold these assembled Kurus.' Just a few words, but they open Arjuna's eyes to who is there. Why might Krishna say only this? He lets Arjuna face the situation himself, so his real doubts come out.

verses.en: There Arjuna saw, in both armies, fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends,
verses.hi: वहाँ अर्जुन ने दोनों सेनाओं में पिता, दादा, गुरु, मामा, भाई, पुत्र, पोते और मित्रों को खड़ा देखा,
verses.short: Arjuna sees grandfathers, teachers, cousins, friends. The enemy is literally family.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna see? Fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends on the battlefield. Why is this hard for him? The enemy is not strangers. It is his own family.

verses.en: and fathers-in-law and well-wishers. Seeing all his own people lined up, Arjuna was overcome with pity and spoke in sorrow.
verses.hi: ससुर और शुभचिंतक भी। अपने सभी सगे-संबंधियों को सामने देखकर अर्जुन करुणा से भर गया और दुखी होकर बोला।
verses.short: In-laws and close friends on both sides. Suddenly this isn't a war. It's a family breakup.
verses.notes: Who else does Arjuna notice? Fathers-in-law and close friends in both armies. What is building in Arjuna? A growing sense that this war means fighting everyone he cares about.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, seeing my own people standing here ready to fight,
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे कृष्ण, युद्ध के लिए खड़े अपने ही लोगों को देखकर,
verses.short: Arjuna gets hit by a wave of emotion and starts to break down.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna feel? Deep compassion mixed with despair as he sees his kinsmen ready to fight. Is this compassion good? Compassion is good, but here it is mixed with attachment and confusion, which Krishna will address.

verses.en: my legs give way, my mouth is dry, my body shakes and my hair stands on end.
verses.hi: मेरे अंग ढीले पड़ रहे हैं, मुँह सूख रहा है, शरीर काँप रहा है और रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं।
verses.short: Legs weak, mouth dry, body shaking, goosebumps. That's a full panic attack, described thousands of years ago.
verses.notes: What physical signs does Arjuna show? Weak limbs, dry mouth, a trembling body and hair standing on end. Why describe his body? To show how deeply the emotional shock has hit him. Grief shows up in the body.

verses.en: My bow Gandiva is slipping from my hand, my skin is burning, I cannot stand steady and my mind is spinning.
verses.hi: गांडीव धनुष हाथ से फिसल रहा है, त्वचा जल रही है, मैं खड़ा नहीं रह पा रहा और मेरा मन चकरा रहा है।
verses.short: His bow slips, his skin burns, his head spins. Even the greatest warrior can hit a wall.
verses.notes: Why does Gandiva slip from his hand? Arjuna's famous bow falls because his strength and will are collapsing. What does 'my mind is reeling' mean? He can't think clearly. Emotion has taken over his judgment.

verses.en: I see bad omens, Krishna, and I see no good in killing my own people in battle.
verses.hi: हे केशव, मुझे बुरे संकेत दिख रहे हैं, और युद्ध में अपनों को मारने में मुझे कोई भलाई नहीं दिखती।
verses.short: "I only see bad signs. Nothing good comes from killing my own people."
verses.notes: What are the 'bad omens'? Arjuna senses that nothing good will come of this war. His mind sees only loss. What is his main argument here? Killing his own kin can't lead to any good.

verses.en: I don't want victory, Krishna, or a kingdom or pleasures. What use is a kingdom, or enjoyment, or even life?
verses.hi: हे कृष्ण, मुझे न जीत चाहिए, न राज्य, न सुख। हे गोविंद, ऐसे राज्य, भोग या जीवन से क्या लाभ?
verses.short: "I don't want the win, the throne or the luxury. What's the point of any of it?" Total burnout energy.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna no longer want? Victory, kingdom, pleasures, even life itself. Is this true renunciation? Not yet. It comes from grief, not wisdom. Krishna will show the difference.

verses.en: The very people for whom we wanted a kingdom, comforts and pleasures stand here in battle, ready to give up their lives and wealth.
verses.hi: जिनके लिए हम राज्य, भोग और सुख चाहते थे, वही लोग जान और धन की परवाह छोड़कर युद्ध में खड़े हैं।
verses.short: "The people I'd want to share the success with are the ones standing here to fight."
verses.notes: What is Arjuna's point here? The people he'd want to share the kingdom with are the ones about to die. Why does that make victory pointless to him? Joy shared with no one, won by killing loved ones, feels empty.

verses.en: My teachers, uncles, sons, grandfathers, my mother's brothers, my wife's father, grandsons, my wife's brothers and other in-laws.
verses.hi: गुरु, पिता, पुत्र, दादा, मामा, ससुर, पोते, साले और दूसरे रिश्तेदार।
verses.short: Teachers, fathers, sons, uncles, in-laws: Arjuna sees them all as his own people. That's the pain.
verses.notes: Who does Arjuna list? Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons and brothers-in-law. Why repeat these relations? Each name adds weight to his grief. He keeps seeing family, not enemies.

verses.en: I don't want to kill them, Krishna, even if they kill me, not even for rule over the three worlds, let alone this earth.
verses.hi: हे मधुसूदन, वे मुझे मार भी दें, तब भी मैं उन्हें मारना नहीं चाहता, तीनों लोकों के राज्य के लिए भी नहीं, फिर धरती के लिए तो क्या।
verses.short: "Even for all three worlds I wouldn't kill them, let alone for this earth."
verses.notes: Would Arjuna fight even to save himself? No. He says he wouldn't kill them even if they killed him, not even for all three worlds. What does this show about Arjuna? He has a gentle heart, but he is letting emotion decide his duty.

verses.en: What joy could we get from killing Dhritarashtra's sons? Even though they are aggressors, killing them would only bring us sin.
verses.hi: हे जनार्दन, धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्रों को मारकर हमें क्या खुशी मिलेगी? वे अत्याचारी हैं, फिर भी उन्हें मारकर हमें पाप ही लगेगा।
verses.short: "Even if they're wrong, what joy is there in destroying them? It'll only leave guilt."
verses.notes: Why does Arjuna fear sin? Even though the Kauravas are wrongdoers, he feels killing them would bring sin on himself. Who are the 'felons' he mentions? The Kauravas, who tried to burn the Pandavas, poisoned Bhima and seized their kingdom.

verses.en: So it is not right for us to kill our own cousins and their families. How could we be happy after killing our own people, Krishna?
verses.hi: इसलिए अपने ही भाइयों और उनके परिवार को मारना हमें शोभा नहीं देता। हे माधव, अपनों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी रहेंगे?
verses.short: "How could we ever be happy after killing our own family?" Arjuna's heart is overruling everything.
verses.notes: What question does Arjuna ask? How can we ever be happy if we kill our own people? Is happiness the right test for duty? Krishna will show that duty is not decided by personal happiness alone.

verses.en: Even if they, blinded by greed, see no wrong in destroying a family or betraying friends,
verses.hi: भले ही लालच से अंधे हुए वे लोग कुल के नाश और मित्रों से धोखे में कोई दोष न देखें,
verses.short: "They're blinded by greed and don't see the damage. But we can see it."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna say about the Kauravas? Their greed blinds them, so they see nothing wrong in destroying families or betraying friends. Why bring this up? He argues that even if they can't see the harm, he can.

verses.en: why shouldn't we, who clearly see the harm in destroying a family, know to turn away from this sin, Krishna?
verses.hi: पर हे जनार्दन, हम तो कुल के नाश का दोष साफ़ देख रहे हैं, फिर हम इस पाप से बचना क्यों न जानें?
verses.short: "If we know this is wrong, why shouldn't we walk away?" Arjuna building his case to quit.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna propose? Since they understand the evil of destroying a family, they should turn away from it. Is his reasoning sound? It sounds moral, but it is shaped by attachment. Krishna will reframe it.

verses.en: When a family is destroyed, its age-old traditions die. When those values are lost, disorder takes over the whole family.
verses.hi: कुल का नाश होने पर उसकी पुरानी परंपराएँ मिट जाती हैं, और धर्म मिटने पर पूरे कुल में अधर्म फैल जाता है।
verses.short: "When families fall apart, traditions and values go with them, and chaos follows."
verses.notes: What happens when a family is destroyed? Its traditions are lost, and without them, disorder takes over. Why does Arjuna care about traditions? They hold families and society together across generations.

verses.en: When disorder spreads, Krishna, the women of the family are led astray, and from that comes confusion in society.
verses.hi: हे कृष्ण, अधर्म फैलने पर कुल की स्त्रियाँ भटक जाती हैं, और इससे समाज में मिलावट और अव्यवस्था पैदा होती है।
verses.short: Arjuna worries society will lose its moral compass if this war happens. Big-picture fear.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna fear will follow? With order gone, family values decline and social confusion grows. How should we read this today? As Arjuna's worry about society breaking down after war, a fear common to every age.

verses.en: This confusion drags both the family and its destroyers to ruin, and their ancestors fall too, deprived of their offerings.
verses.hi: यह अव्यवस्था कुल और उसके नाश करने वालों को नरक की ओर ले जाती है, और पिंडदान-जल न मिलने से उनके पूर्वज भी गिर जाते हैं।
verses.short: He fears the damage will hit generations, even the ancestors. His anxiety is now going full worst-case.
verses.notes: What are the 'offerings' to ancestors? Rituals of food and water that families perform for those who have passed away. Why does Arjuna mention ancestors? He fears the war will break the chain linking generations.

verses.en: Through these wrongs of the family destroyers, which cause social confusion, the lasting duties of community and family are wiped out.
verses.hi: कुल का नाश करने वालों के इन दोषों से, जो समाज में अव्यवस्था लाते हैं, जाति और कुल के सनातन धर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं।
verses.short: "Those who break families destroy traditions that took ages to build."
verses.notes: Who does Arjuna blame? Those who destroy families, because their actions wipe out long-held traditions. Is Arjuna blaming himself too? Yes. He fears he would become one of them by fighting.

verses.en: Krishna, we have heard that people whose family values are destroyed live in hell for a long time.
verses.hi: हे जनार्दन, हमने सुना है कि जिनके कुल-धर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं, वे लंबे समय तक नरक में रहते हैं।
verses.short: "We've heard that people who destroy family values suffer badly." Fear is doing the talking now.
verses.notes: Where does Arjuna get this belief? He says 'so we have heard', meaning it comes from tradition and teachers. Why does that matter? He is quoting what he was taught, not yet seeing the deeper truth Krishna will share.

verses.en: Alas, we are set on doing a great sin, ready to kill our own people out of greed for a kingdom and its pleasures.
verses.hi: हाय, कितने दुख की बात है कि राज्य-सुख के लालच में हम अपने ही लोगों को मारने और बड़ा पाप करने पर तुले हैं।
verses.short: "We're about to do something terrible just for power and comfort." Guilt hits hard.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna regret? That they were about to commit a great sin, killing kin out of greed for a kingdom. Is greed really his motive? Not really. His grief makes him see his duty as greed.

verses.en: It would be better for me if Dhritarashtra's armed sons killed me in battle while I stood unarmed and did not fight back.
verses.hi: अगर मैं बिना शस्त्र और बिना विरोध के रहूँ और धृतराष्ट्र के शस्त्रधारी पुत्र मुझे युद्ध में मार दें, तो वह मेरे लिए ज़्यादा अच्छा होगा।
verses.short: "I'd rather let them kill me, unarmed, than fight." Arjuna is ready to give up completely.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna prefer? To be killed unarmed and without resisting, rather than fight. What does this reveal? He has reached total despair, ready to give up even his life.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Having said this on the battlefield, Arjuna threw down his bow and arrows and sank onto the chariot seat, his mind torn with grief.
verses.hi: संजय ने कहा: युद्धभूमि में ऐसा कहकर, शोक से व्याकुल मन वाला अर्जुन धनुष-बाण छोड़कर रथ के पिछले हिस्से में बैठ गया।
verses.short: Arjuna drops his bow, sits down, and breaks. Rock bottom. And this is exactly where the Gita begins.
verses.notes: How does Chapter 1 end? Arjuna throws down his bow and arrows and sinks into his chariot, overwhelmed with grief. Why is this called the 'yoga of despair'? Because this despair, faced honestly, becomes the doorway to Krishna's teaching.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Seeing Arjuna overcome with pity, his eyes full of tears and his heart sinking, Krishna spoke these words.
verses.hi: संजय ने कहा: करुणा से भरे, आँसुओं से डबडबाई आँखों वाले और दुखी अर्जुन से श्रीकृष्ण ने ये वचन कहे।
verses.short: Arjuna's crying, overwhelmed, frozen. Krishna sees it all and steps in. Big talk incoming.
verses.notes: What state is Arjuna in here? He is overwhelmed: full of pity, eyes filled with tears, and confused about what to do. This is the moment Krishna begins to teach. Why does the narrator describe his tears? To show that Arjuna's refusal comes from emotion, not clear thinking. The rest of the chapter moves him from feeling to understanding.

verses.en: Krishna said: Arjuna, where has this weakness come from at such a critical moment? It doesn't suit a noble person. It leads neither to heaven nor to honour.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे अर्जुन, इस संकट के समय यह कमज़ोरी तुम्हें कहाँ से आ गई? यह श्रेष्ठ लोगों को शोभा नहीं देती, न स्वर्ग दिलाती है, न यश।
verses.short: Krishna: "Bro, why are you breaking down right now? This isn't you, and it won't get you anywhere."
verses.notes: Why does Krishna start by scolding Arjuna? To jolt him out of despair. Krishna calls this weakness unworthy of a noble person, because it neither brings honour nor leads anywhere good. Is Krishna against feeling sad? No. He is against sadness that freezes you at the very moment you need to act. The problem is the paralysis, not the feeling.

verses.en: Don't give in to cowardice, Arjuna. It isn't who you are. Shake off this petty weakness of heart and stand up, you who burn your enemies.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, कायरता में मत पड़ो, यह तुम्हें शोभा नहीं देती। दिल की इस छोटी-सी कमज़ोरी को छोड़कर उठ खड़े हो, हे परंतप।
verses.short: This isn't you. Stop doom-spiralling, get up, and handle it. You're bigger than this moment.
verses.notes: What does 'faint-heartedness' mean here? A small, weak state of heart that doesn't match who Arjuna really is. Krishna urges him to shake it off and stand up. What is the lesson for daily life? When fear makes you shrink, remember your strength and rise to the task. Krishna's 'arise' is a call to courage.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, how can I shoot arrows in battle at Bhishma and Drona, who deserve my worship?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे मधुसूदन, मैं युद्ध में भीष्म और द्रोण पर बाण कैसे चलाऊँ? वे तो मेरे लिए पूजनीय हैं।
verses.short: Arjuna: "How do I fight people I literally look up to?" Real dilemma, real pain.
verses.notes: Why can't Arjuna fight Bhishma and Drona? Bhishma is his grandfather and Drona his teacher. Both deserve his worship, so shooting arrows at them feels unthinkable to him. Is Arjuna's argument wrong? His respect is real, but he is mixing personal feelings with his duty. Krishna will show him a deeper way to see the situation.

verses.en: It would be better to live on alms in this world than to kill these great teachers. If I kill them, even the pleasures I enjoy would be stained with blood.
verses.hi: इन महान गुरुओं को मारने से अच्छा है कि इस दुनिया में भीख माँगकर जी लूँ। उन्हें मारकर जो सुख भोगूँगा, वह भी खून से सना होगा।
verses.short: Arjuna would rather be broke than hurt his teachers. Any win built on that feels toxic to him.
verses.notes: Why would Arjuna rather beg? He feels that a kingdom won by killing his teachers would be stained with blood, so even a beggar's life seems better. What does 'blood-stained pleasures' show? That Arjuna is judging the war only by what he would gain or lose. Krishna will shift his focus from results to duty.

verses.en: We don't even know which is better, that we win or that they win. Dhritarashtra's sons stand before us, and after killing them we wouldn't even want to live.
verses.hi: हम यह भी नहीं जानते कि हमारे लिए क्या बेहतर है, हम जीतें या वे जीतें। सामने धृतराष्ट्र के पुत्र खड़े हैं, जिन्हें मारकर हम जीना भी नहीं चाहेंगे।
verses.short: Arjuna doesn't even know what winning means anymore. Win or lose, someone he loves gets hurt.
verses.notes: What is Arjuna unsure about? Whether winning or losing would be better. Either way, he would lose people he loves, so neither outcome feels right. Why is this confusion important? When every option looks wrong, we need a deeper principle to decide. That is exactly what Krishna is about to give.

verses.en: My nature is overwhelmed by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me clearly what is best for me. I am your student. I surrender to you; guide me.
verses.hi: कमज़ोरी ने मेरे स्वभाव को दबा दिया है और मैं समझ नहीं पा रहा कि धर्म क्या है। मैं आपसे पूछता हूँ, मुझे साफ़ बताइए कि मेरे लिए क्या अच्छा है। मैं आपका शिष्य हूँ, आपकी शरण में हूँ, मुझे राह दिखाइए।
verses.short: Arjuna finally admits: "I'm confused. I need help. Guide me." Asking for help is the first real step.
verses.notes: Why is this verse a turning point? Arjuna stops arguing and asks for guidance. He says, 'I am your disciple, teach me.' Real learning begins here. What can we learn from Arjuna's request? Admitting you are confused and asking for help is a strength, not a weakness. It opens the door to wisdom.

verses.en: I can't see anything that would remove this grief that dries up my senses, not even an unrivalled, rich kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
verses.hi: मुझे ऐसा कुछ नहीं दिखता जो मेरी इंद्रियों को सुखा देने वाले इस शोक को दूर कर दे, चाहे धरती का निष्कंटक समृद्ध राज्य मिले या देवताओं पर राज।
verses.short: Even owning the whole world wouldn't fix this pain. Money and power can't heal a confused mind.
verses.notes: Why wouldn't even a kingdom help Arjuna? His grief is inside him. No outer gain, not even rule over the gods, can remove a sorrow that comes from within. What does this teach about success? Outer achievements can't heal inner pain. Peace needs a change in understanding, which is what the Gita offers.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Having said this to Krishna, Arjuna declared, "I will not fight," and fell silent.
verses.hi: संजय ने कहा: श्रीकृष्ण से ऐसा कहकर अर्जुन बोला, "मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा," और चुप हो गया।
verses.short: Arjuna says "I won't fight" and goes silent. Full shutdown mode.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna finally decide? He tells Krishna, 'I will not fight,' and falls silent. He has run out of answers. Why is Arjuna called the 'conqueror of sleep' here? It reminds us of his great discipline and strength, which makes his collapse into despair all the more striking.

verses.en: Then, O King, between the two armies, Krishna smiled slightly and spoke these words to the grieving Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे भारत, तब दोनों सेनाओं के बीच दुखी बैठे अर्जुन से श्रीकृष्ण ने मुस्कुराते हुए ये वचन कहे।
verses.short: Krishna smiles. Not mocking, just calm. He knows this crisis is where the growth starts.
verses.notes: Why does Krishna smile? Not to mock him, but because he sees the confusion is temporary and can be cleared. His calm contrasts with Arjuna's distress. Why is the setting 'between the two armies' mentioned? Arjuna is literally and mentally caught in the middle. The teaching happens right where the conflict is.

verses.en: Krishna said: You grieve for those who don't need grieving for, yet you speak words that sound wise. The truly wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: तुम उनके लिए शोक कर रहे हो जिनके लिए शोक करना ठीक नहीं, और बातें ज्ञानियों जैसी करते हो। ज्ञानी लोग न मरे हुओं का शोक करते हैं, न जीवितों का।
verses.short: You're overthinking things that don't deserve your grief. Wise people don't spiral over life or death.
verses.notes: What does Krishna mean by grieving for those who shouldn't be grieved for? Arjuna talks wisely but misses the basic truth: the real Self doesn't die. The wise don't mourn the living or the dead. Does this mean we shouldn't feel loss? It means grief comes from mistaking the body for the person. With understanding, loss doesn't crush us.

verses.en: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings. And none of us will ever stop existing in the future.
verses.hi: ऐसा कभी नहीं था कि मैं नहीं था, या तुम नहीं थे, या ये राजा नहीं थे। और आगे भी ऐसा कभी नहीं होगा कि हम सब न रहें।
verses.short: You, me, everyone here: we always existed and always will. You're not as temporary as you think.
verses.notes: What is Krishna saying about existence? There was never a time when Krishna, Arjuna or these kings did not exist, and there never will be. The Self has no beginning or end. Why does Krishna start with this idea? Arjuna's grief is about death. Showing that the Self is eternal removes the root of that grief.

verses.en: Just as the soul in this body passes through childhood, youth and old age, it also passes into another body. The steady person is not shaken by this.
verses.hi: जैसे इस शरीर में आत्मा बचपन, जवानी और बुढ़ापे से गुज़रती है, वैसे ही वह दूसरा शरीर पाती है। धीर व्यक्ति इससे विचलित नहीं होता।
verses.short: Childhood, teen years, old age, then a new body. You keep upgrading; the real you stays.
verses.notes: How is death like growing up? We pass from childhood to youth to old age and remain the same person. Death is just one more change of body. Who is 'not deluded' by this? The wise person, who sees that the one living in the body stays the same through every change.

verses.en: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go; they don't last. Learn to bear them patiently, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, इंद्रियों का विषयों से संपर्क ही सर्दी-गर्मी और सुख-दुख देता है। ये आते-जाते रहते हैं, टिकते नहीं। हे भारत, इन्हें धैर्य से सहना सीखो।
verses.short: Feelings come and go like weather. One bad day isn't your whole story. Let it pass and keep going.
verses.notes: Why should we endure pleasure and pain? Because they come from the senses meeting the world, and they don't last. Like hot and cold weather, they come and go. Does 'endure' mean suppress feelings? No. It means not being swept away. You notice them, knowing they will pass.

verses.en: The person who isn't disturbed by these, who stays the same in pain and pleasure and remains steady, is ready for immortality.
verses.hi: हे पुरुषश्रेष्ठ, जो व्यक्ति इनसे परेशान नहीं होता, सुख-दुख में एक जैसा और धीर रहता है, वही अमरता के योग्य है।
verses.short: Stay the same whether it's pain or pleasure. That steady person can't be shaken by anything.
verses.notes: Who is fit for immortality? The steady person who stays the same in pleasure and pain and isn't shaken by them. What does 'immortality' mean here? Freedom from the cycle of birth and death, the lasting peace of knowing the Self.

verses.en: The unreal never truly exists, and the real never stops existing. Those who see the truth have understood the nature of both.
verses.hi: असत् का कोई अस्तित्व नहीं होता और सत् का कभी अभाव नहीं होता। सत्य को देखने वालों ने इन दोनों का सार समझ लिया है।
verses.short: What's fake never really exists. What's real never disappears. Learn to tell the difference.
verses.notes: What are the 'real' and the 'unreal'? The unreal is what changes and passes, like the body. The real is what never stops being, the Self. Who sees this truth? Seers who look past appearances. They know what lasts and what doesn't.

verses.en: Know that what pervades this whole universe can never be destroyed. No one can destroy the imperishable.
verses.hi: जिससे यह पूरा संसार व्याप्त है, उसे अविनाशी जानो। उस अविनाशी का नाश कोई नहीं कर सकता।
verses.short: The thing that runs through everything can't be destroyed. Nobody can delete the real you.
verses.notes: What pervades 'all this'? The Self, the awareness behind everything. It fills all that exists. Why can no one destroy it? Because it doesn't change. Only things that change can be destroyed.

verses.en: These bodies come to an end, but the soul living in them is eternal, indestructible and beyond measure. So fight, Arjuna.
verses.hi: ये शरीर नाशवान हैं, पर इनमें रहने वाली आत्मा नित्य, अविनाशी और अपार है। इसलिए हे भारत, युद्ध करो।
verses.short: Bodies have an expiry date. The soul doesn't. So do what you have to do.
verses.notes: What ends and what doesn't? Bodies end. The one living in them is eternal and can't be destroyed. Why does Krishna say 'therefore fight'? Since the Self can't be killed, Arjuna's fear of killing is misplaced. He should do his duty.

verses.en: Whoever thinks the soul kills, and whoever thinks it is killed, both fail to understand. It neither kills nor is killed.
verses.hi: जो आत्मा को मारने वाला मानता है और जो इसे मरा हुआ मानता है, दोनों ही नहीं जानते। आत्मा न मारती है, न मारी जाती है।
verses.short: Thinking the soul kills or gets killed? Both takes are wrong. It's untouchable.
verses.notes: Why are both the 'slayer' and the 'slain' ignorant? Both think the Self can kill or be killed. In truth, it does neither. Does this make violence acceptable? No. Krishna is talking about the eternal nature of the Self in the context of a just duty, not giving permission to harm.

verses.en: The soul is never born and never dies. It did not come into being and will not cease to be. Unborn, eternal, ever-lasting and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.
verses.hi: आत्मा न कभी जन्म लेती है, न कभी मरती है। यह न पैदा होकर फिर होने वाली है। यह अजन्मा, नित्य, शाश्वत और पुरातन है। शरीर के मारे जाने पर भी यह नहीं मरती।
verses.short: The real you was never born and can't die. Bodies change, but the one watching it all stays.
verses.notes: What is the Self like? It is never born and never dies. Unborn, eternal and ancient, it isn't destroyed when the body is. Why is this verse so famous? It sums up the Gita's answer to the fear of death in a few lines, and is often recited at funerals.

verses.en: Arjuna, if someone knows the soul to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and unchanging, how can that person kill anyone or cause anyone to be killed?
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, जो आत्मा को अविनाशी, नित्य, अजन्मा और अपरिवर्तनीय जानता है, वह किसी को कैसे मारेगा या मरवाएगा?
verses.short: Once you know the soul can't be destroyed, the whole fear of killing and dying changes.
verses.notes: What question does Krishna ask? If someone knows the Self is indestructible and unborn, how can they think they kill anyone, or cause anyone to be killed? What is the point of this question? To shift Arjuna from 'I am the killer' to seeing the deeper truth about who he and others really are.

verses.en: Just as a person throws away worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the soul leaves worn-out bodies and takes on new ones.
verses.hi: जैसे इंसान पुराने कपड़े उतारकर नए पहन लेता है, वैसे ही आत्मा पुराने शरीर छोड़कर नए शरीर धारण करती है।
verses.short: Changing bodies is like changing clothes. Old fit off, new fit on. Same you inside.
verses.notes: What does the clothes example mean? Just as we throw away worn-out clothes and put on new ones, the Self leaves an old body and takes a new one. Is this about rebirth? Yes. It is one of the Gita's clearest pictures of rebirth, showing death as a change, not an end.

verses.en: Weapons cannot cut the soul, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it and wind cannot dry it.
verses.hi: आत्मा को न शस्त्र काट सकते हैं, न आग जला सकती है, न पानी गीला कर सकता है और न हवा सुखा सकती है।
verses.short: Weapons can't cut it, fire can't burn it, water can't wet it, wind can't dry it. Built different.
verses.notes: Why can't weapons or fire harm the Self? Because the Self is not physical. Weapons, fire, water and wind only work on matter. Why use these four examples? They are the forces that destroy physical things. None of them can touch the Self.

verses.en: It cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried. It is eternal, present everywhere, stable, unmoving and timeless.
verses.hi: यह न कटती है, न जलती है, न भीगती है, न सूखती है। यह नित्य, सर्वव्यापी, स्थिर, अचल और सनातन है।
verses.short: The soul can't be cut, burned, soaked or dried. It's everywhere, steady, and forever.
verses.notes: What qualities of the Self are listed? Eternal, all-pervading, stable, unmoving and ancient. It can't be cut, burnt, wetted or dried. Why repeat the idea again? Repetition helps a grieving mind absorb a truth it finds hard to accept.

verses.en: The soul is called unseen, beyond thought and unchanging. Knowing it to be so, you should not grieve.
verses.hi: आत्मा को अदृश्य, सोच से परे और अपरिवर्तनीय कहा जाता है। इसे ऐसा जानकर तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.short: You can't see it or fully figure it out, and it never changes. So stop grieving.
verses.notes: What does 'unmanifest' mean? The Self can't be seen by the eyes or grasped by the mind. It doesn't change. What should knowing this do? It should end grief, because what you are mourning was never lost.

verses.en: And even if you think the soul is always being born and always dying, mighty Arjuna, you still should not grieve.
verses.hi: हे महाबाहु, और अगर तुम मानो कि आत्मा बार-बार जन्म लेती और मरती है, तब भी तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.short: Even if you think the soul dies every time, grieving still doesn't help. Stay strong.
verses.notes: What if someone doesn't believe the Self is eternal? Krishna argues that even if the Self were constantly born and dying, grief still wouldn't make sense. Why does Krishna make this second argument? To meet Arjuna where he is. Whatever view he holds, grief is not the answer.

verses.en: Death is certain for whoever is born, and birth is certain for whoever dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
verses.hi: जो जन्मा है उसकी मृत्यु निश्चित है, और जो मरा है उसका जन्म निश्चित है। इसलिए जो टल नहीं सकता, उस पर शोक मत करो।
verses.short: Whoever's born will die, and whoever dies comes back. Don't stress over what can't be avoided.
verses.notes: Why not grieve what is inevitable? Whoever is born will die, and whoever dies will be born. Grieving over the certain doesn't change it. How can this help in real life? Accepting what can't be changed frees your energy for what can.

verses.en: Beings are unseen before birth, seen in between, and unseen again after death. So why mourn, Arjuna?
verses.hi: हे भारत, सभी प्राणी जन्म से पहले अदृश्य, बीच में दिखाई देने वाले और मृत्यु के बाद फिर अदृश्य हो जाते हैं। फिर इसमें रोना कैसा?
verses.short: We come from the unknown and go back to it. We only see the middle part. Why panic?
verses.notes: What does 'unknown beginning and end' mean? We don't see where beings come from before birth or where they go after death. We only see the middle. Why does that remove grief? If we only ever see a small part of the story, mourning its end as total loss makes little sense.

verses.en: Some see the soul as a wonder, some speak of it as a wonder, some hear of it as a wonder, and even after hearing, no one truly knows it.
verses.hi: कोई आत्मा को आश्चर्य की तरह देखता है, कोई आश्चर्य की तरह इसका वर्णन करता है, कोई आश्चर्य की तरह सुनता है, और सुनकर भी कोई इसे पूरी तरह नहीं जानता।
verses.short: Some see the soul as a miracle, some talk about it, some hear about it. Few actually get it.
verses.notes: Why is the Self called a wonder? It is so unlike anything we know that people see it, speak of it and hear of it with amazement. Why do many still not know it? Hearing about the Self isn't the same as realising it. That takes direct experience.

verses.en: The soul that lives in every body can never be killed, Arjuna. So you should not grieve for any living being.
verses.hi: हे भारत, हर शरीर में रहने वाली आत्मा कभी मारी नहीं जा सकती। इसलिए तुम्हें किसी भी प्राणी के लिए शोक नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.short: The soul in every body is eternal. Nobody is ever truly lost. Don't drown in grief.
verses.notes: What is the conclusion of Krishna's first argument? The Self in every body is eternal and can't be killed, so Arjuna shouldn't grieve for anyone. Does this apply to everyone? Yes. Krishna says it is true of all beings, not just Arjuna's family.

verses.en: Looking at your own duty too, you should not waver. For a warrior, nothing is better than a fight for what is right.
verses.hi: अपने धर्म को देखकर भी तुम्हें डगमगाना नहीं चाहिए। एक क्षत्रिय के लिए धर्म के युद्ध से बढ़कर कुछ नहीं।
verses.short: This is literally your role. Backing out of the right fight doesn't suit you.
verses.notes: What is 'svadharma'? Your own duty, based on your role and nature. For Arjuna, a warrior, it is to fight for what is right. Why does Krishna now talk about duty? He moves from spiritual truth to practical reason: even by the standards of his own role, Arjuna shouldn't hesitate.

verses.en: Happy are the warriors, Arjuna, who get such a battle by chance. It is like an open door to heaven.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, वे क्षत्रिय भाग्यशाली हैं जिन्हें अपने आप ऐसा युद्ध मिलता है। यह स्वर्ग के खुले दरवाज़े जैसा है।
verses.short: A real chance to stand up for what's right is rare. Lucky are those who get one.
verses.notes: Why does Krishna call such a war fortunate? For a warrior, a righteous battle that comes on its own is a rare chance to fulfil his purpose. What is the broader lesson? When the right challenge arrives, see it as an opportunity, not a burden.

verses.en: But if you refuse to fight this righteous war, you will give up your duty and your honour, and you will gain sin.
verses.hi: पर अगर तुम यह धर्मयुद्ध नहीं करोगे, तो अपना धर्म और यश दोनों खोकर पाप के भागी बनोगे।
verses.short: Skip this fight and you lose your purpose, your respect, and your peace.
verses.notes: What happens if Arjuna refuses? He would abandon his duty and honour and incur sin, because walking away from a just cause is itself wrong. Can avoiding action be a mistake? Yes. Krishna shows that not acting when duty calls has consequences too.

verses.en: People will talk about your disgrace forever. For someone respected, dishonour is worse than death.
verses.hi: लोग हमेशा तुम्हारी बदनामी की बातें करेंगे। सम्मानित व्यक्ति के लिए अपयश मृत्यु से भी बुरा है।
verses.short: Run away and people will talk about it forever. For someone respected, that hurts more than anything.
verses.notes: Why does Krishna mention reputation? People will speak of Arjuna's retreat forever, and for an honoured person, disgrace is worse than death. Is Krishna saying reputation matters most? No. It is one of several practical arguments, alongside the deeper spiritual one.

verses.en: The great warriors will think you ran from battle out of fear. Those who held you in high regard will think little of you.
verses.hi: महारथी सोचेंगे कि तुम डर के मारे युद्ध से भाग गए। जो तुम्हें बहुत मानते थे, उनकी नज़रों में तुम छोटे हो जाओगे।
verses.short: The legends will think you got scared. The ones who hyped you up will lose respect.
verses.notes: How would other warriors see Arjuna? They would think he fled out of fear, and those who once respected him would look down on him. What does this teach? Our choices shape how others understand us, especially in moments that matter.

verses.en: Your enemies will say many cruel things and mock your strength. What could be more painful than that?
verses.hi: तुम्हारे दुश्मन तुम्हारी ताकत का मज़ाक उड़ाते हुए बहुत सी न कहने लायक बातें कहेंगे। इससे बड़ा दुख क्या होगा?
verses.short: Haters will roast you nonstop. What's more painful than that?
verses.notes: What would Arjuna's enemies do? They would mock his strength with insulting words, which Krishna calls the most painful thing of all. Why list these consequences? To show Arjuna that running away won't bring the peace he hopes for.

verses.en: If you are killed, you will reach heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the earth. So stand up, Arjuna, determined to fight.
verses.hi: मारे गए तो स्वर्ग पाओगे, जीत गए तो धरती का सुख भोगोगे। इसलिए हे कौन्तेय, युद्ध का निश्चय करके उठो।
verses.short: Lose and you still win something. Win and you get it all. So get up and fight.
verses.notes: Why is it a win either way? If Arjuna dies, he gains heaven. If he wins, he enjoys the earth. Doing his duty has no losing outcome. What is the call here? Get up and fight with a firm mind, instead of staying stuck in doubt.

verses.en: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, and then get ready to fight. That way you will not incur sin.
verses.hi: सुख-दुख, लाभ-हानि और जीत-हार को एक समान मानकर युद्ध के लिए तैयार हो जाओ। ऐसा करने से तुम्हें पाप नहीं लगेगा।
verses.short: Pleasure or pain, gain or loss, win or fail: treat them the same and just do your duty.
verses.notes: What does it mean to treat gain and loss alike? Do your duty without being pulled by hopes of winning or fears of losing. Stay even-minded. How does this free one from sin? Action done without selfish attachment doesn't bind you. That is the seed of Karma Yoga.

verses.en: So far I have explained this to you through knowledge. Now hear it through the path of yoga. With this understanding, Arjuna, you will break free from the bondage of action.
verses.hi: अब तक मैंने तुम्हें यह ज्ञान के नज़रिए से समझाया। अब इसे योग के नज़रिए से सुनो। इस समझ से जुड़कर, हे पार्थ, तुम कर्म के बंधन से छूट जाओगे।
verses.short: Theory done. Now the practical: how to work without getting trapped by your actions.
verses.notes: What shift happens in this verse? Krishna moves from knowledge of the Self (Sankhya) to the practice of action (Yoga). What does this Yoga promise? Freedom from the bondage of karma through the right attitude to work.

verses.en: On this path, no effort is wasted and there is no harm in trying. Even a little of this practice protects you from great fear.
verses.hi: इस मार्ग में की गई कोई कोशिश बेकार नहीं जाती और कोई नुकसान नहीं होता। इसका थोड़ा-सा पालन भी बड़े डर से बचा लेता है।
verses.short: On this path no effort is ever wasted. Even a little practice protects you from big fears.
verses.notes: Why is no effort wasted here? On this path, even a small step counts. Nothing is lost, and there is no harm in trying. What is the 'great fear'? The fear of repeated birth and death. Even a little of this practice protects you from it.

verses.en: Here the determined mind is focused on one aim, Arjuna. But the minds of the undecided branch out endlessly in many directions.
verses.hi: हे कुरुनंदन, इस मार्ग में निश्चय वाली बुद्धि एक ही लक्ष्य पर टिकी रहती है। पर अनिश्चित लोगों की बुद्धि अनगिनत दिशाओं में बँट जाती है।
verses.short: Focused mind = one clear goal. Scattered mind = a hundred tabs open and nothing done.
verses.notes: What is a resolute mind? A mind focused on one clear goal. It doesn't scatter in many directions. What happens to the irresolute? Their thoughts branch out endlessly, chasing many desires and never settling.

verses.en: Unwise people delight in the flowery words of the Vedas, Arjuna, and claim there is nothing beyond them.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, अविवेकी लोग वेदों की लुभावनी बातों में मगन रहते हैं और कहते हैं कि इसके आगे कुछ नहीं है।
verses.short: Some people use religion just to chase rewards and luxury. That noise kills real focus.
verses.notes: Who are the 'unwise' Krishna describes? People who treat scripture only as a way to get pleasure and power, and say there is nothing higher. What does 'flowery words' mean? Attractive promises of rewards that pull the mind toward desire instead of clarity.

verses.en: Full of desires and set on heaven, they praise many rituals that promise a good birth, rewards, pleasure and power.
verses.hi: इच्छाओं से भरे और स्वर्ग को ही लक्ष्य मानने वाले वे लोग ऐसे कर्मकांडों का गुणगान करते हैं जो अच्छे जन्म, फल, भोग और ऐश्वर्य का वादा करते हैं।
verses.short: Chasing heaven, perks and power as the goal? Your mind stays scattered and never settles.
verses.notes: Why does chasing rewards scatter the mind? When the goal is pleasure and power, the mind keeps jumping between desires and can't settle. Is Krishna against rituals? He is against using them only for selfish gain. Their deeper purpose is purification.

verses.en: Those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away by such talk, cannot develop the firm focus needed for deep meditation.
verses.hi: जो भोग और ऐश्वर्य में फँसे हैं और जिनका मन ऐसी बातों से भटक गया है, उनकी बुद्धि ध्यान में स्थिर नहीं हो पाती।
verses.short: Hooked on pleasure and power? You'll never build the deep focus that actually matters.
verses.notes: What happens to those attached to pleasure and power? Their minds are carried away and can't develop the steady focus needed for wisdom. What is the takeaway? Craving rewards keeps the mind restless. Steadiness comes when you let that pull go.

verses.en: The Vedas deal with the three qualities of nature. Rise above them, Arjuna. Be free from opposites, stay grounded in truth, don't worry about getting and keeping, and be centred in yourself.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, वेद तीनों गुणों की बात करते हैं। तुम इन गुणों से ऊपर उठो। द्वंद्वों से मुक्त रहो, सत्य में टिके रहो, पाने-बचाने की चिंता छोड़ो और आत्मा में स्थित रहो।
verses.short: Rise above the push and pull of moods. Stop obsessing over getting and keeping stuff. Stay centered.
verses.notes: What does it mean to go beyond the three gunas? To rise above the forces of nature that drive our moods and desires, and rest in the Self. What does 'free from the pairs of opposites' mean? Not being tossed between heat and cold, praise and blame, gain and loss.

verses.en: For someone who knows the truth, the Vedas are as useful as a small well is when water floods everywhere.
verses.hi: जब चारों ओर पानी ही पानी भरा हो, तब छोटे कुएँ का जितना काम होता है, सत्य को जानने वाले के लिए वेदों का उतना ही काम है।
verses.short: When you've found the ocean, you don't need the well. Real wisdom covers everything the rituals promise.
verses.notes: What does the flood example mean? When there is water everywhere, a small reservoir is of little use. For one who knows the Self, rituals have the same small use. Is Krishna dismissing the Vedas? No. He means that the goal of all scripture is reached in knowing the Self.

verses.en: Your right is to the work alone, never to its results. Don't let results be your motive, and don't get attached to doing nothing.
verses.hi: तुम्हारा अधिकार केवल कर्म करने पर है, उसके फल पर कभी नहीं। फल को अपने कर्म का कारण मत बनाओ, और कर्म न करने से भी मत चिपको।
verses.short: You control the effort, not the outcome. Grades, likes, promotions aren't your department. Do the work, drop the result anxiety.
verses.notes: Does this verse mean I shouldn't care about results? It means don't let results be your motive or your anxiety. Plan well and work hard, but your control ends at the effort. Why does Krishna also warn against inaction? Because letting go of results is not an excuse to stop working. Detachment and laziness are different things.

verses.en: Do your work steady in yoga, Arjuna, letting go of attachment and staying the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
verses.hi: हे धनंजय, आसक्ति छोड़कर और सफलता-असफलता में एक समान रहकर, योग में स्थित होकर कर्म करो। यही समता योग कहलाती है।
verses.short: Do your thing with a steady mind. Win or lose, stay balanced. That calm focus is real yoga.
verses.notes: What is Yoga according to this verse? Evenness of mind: staying balanced in success and failure while you do your work. How do I practise this? Give your best, then accept the outcome calmly, without being lifted by success or crushed by failure.

verses.en: Work done for results is far lower than work done with this steady understanding, Arjuna. Take refuge in that understanding. Those who work only for results are to be pitied.
verses.hi: हे धनंजय, फल के लिए किया गया कर्म समझ के साथ किए गए कर्म से बहुत नीचे है। इसी समझ की शरण लो। जो केवल फल के लिए काम करते हैं, वे दया के पात्र हैं।
verses.short: Working only for rewards keeps you stressed. Working with a calm mind keeps you free.
verses.notes: Why is work done for results inferior? It ties your happiness to things outside your control, which makes you anxious and miserable. What should we take refuge in? An even, steady mind. It makes work lighter and life calmer.

verses.en: A person with this understanding lets go of both good and bad deeds here and now. So commit to yoga. Yoga is skill in action.
verses.hi: समझ से जुड़ा व्यक्ति यहीं अच्छे-बुरे दोनों कर्मों के बंधन से छूट जाता है। इसलिए योग से जुड़ो। योग ही कर्म में कुशलता है।
verses.short: A balanced mind is the real skill. Yoga is basically being great at what you do, without stress.
verses.notes: What does 'Yoga is skill in action' mean? Acting well while staying unattached, so that work doesn't bind you. That balance is the real skill. How does one cast off good and evil? By acting without selfish attachment, actions stop leaving marks that bind you.

verses.en: The wise, joined with this understanding, give up the fruits of action, become free from the cycle of birth, and reach a state beyond all suffering.
verses.hi: इस समझ से जुड़े ज्ञानी लोग कर्म के फल को छोड़कर जन्म के बंधन से मुक्त हो जाते हैं और दुखों से परे पद को पाते हैं।
verses.short: Wise people work hard but don't cling to the results. That's how they escape the endless cycle.
verses.notes: What do the wise give up? The fruits of their actions. They work fully but don't cling to rewards. Where does this lead? Beyond the cycle of birth, to a state free of all suffering.

verses.en: When your mind crosses the swamp of confusion, you will become indifferent to all you have heard and all you are yet to hear.
verses.hi: जब तुम्हारी बुद्धि मोह के दलदल को पार कर लेगी, तब तुम जो सुन चुके हो और जो सुनना बाकी है, उन सबसे उदासीन हो जाओगे।
verses.short: Once you see through the confusion, all the hype and noise around you stops mattering.
verses.notes: What is the 'tangle of delusion'? The confusion that makes us identify with the body and chase outcomes. Crossing it brings clarity. Why become indifferent to what you've heard? Once you see clearly, promises of rewards and opinions stop pulling you around.

verses.en: When your mind, no longer confused by conflicting teachings, stands firm and steady in meditation, you will reach yoga.
verses.hi: जब तरह-तरह की बातें सुनकर भटकी तुम्हारी बुद्धि ध्यान में अचल और स्थिर हो जाएगी, तब तुम योग को पा लोगे।
verses.short: When your mind stops getting pulled around by every opinion and stays steady, that's the real breakthrough.
verses.notes: When does the mind become steady? When it is no longer confused by conflicting ideas and rests firmly in focus. What is attained then? Yoga, the direct vision of the Self.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, how do you describe a person of steady wisdom, settled in meditation? How does such a person speak, sit and move?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे केशव, स्थिर बुद्धि वाले और ध्यान में टिके व्यक्ति की क्या पहचान है? वह कैसे बोलता, बैठता और चलता है?
verses.short: Arjuna asks: "What does a truly steady person look like? How do they talk, sit, move?"
verses.notes: What does Arjuna want to know? How a person of steady wisdom speaks, sits and moves. He wants to see the teaching in real life. Why is this question useful? It turns big ideas into a practical picture we can learn from.

verses.en: Krishna said: When someone lets go of all the desires of the mind and is content in the self, by the self, that person is said to have steady wisdom.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे पार्थ, जब कोई मन की सारी इच्छाएँ छोड़ देता है और अपने भीतर ही संतुष्ट रहता है, तब उसे स्थिर बुद्धि वाला कहा जाता है।
verses.short: When you stop needing outside stuff to be happy and feel complete inside, you're truly steady.
verses.notes: What is the first sign of steady wisdom? Giving up desires that come from the mind and being content in the Self. Does contentment mean having no goals? No. It means your happiness doesn't depend on getting what you want.

verses.en: Someone who isn't shaken by sorrow, doesn't crave pleasure, and is free from attachment, fear and anger is called a sage of steady mind.
verses.hi: जो दुख में घबराता नहीं, सुख की लालसा नहीं रखता, और राग, डर व क्रोध से मुक्त है, वह स्थिर बुद्धि वाला मुनि कहलाता है।
verses.short: Not shaken by pain, not chasing pleasure, free from fear and anger. That's peak calm.
verses.notes: How does a steady sage handle pain and pleasure? Pain doesn't shake them, pleasure doesn't hook them, and they are free of craving, fear and anger. Is this possible for ordinary people? It's a direction to grow in. Every time you stay calm instead of reacting, you move closer.

verses.en: Someone who is attached to nothing, and who neither rejoices at good nor hates bad when it comes, has firm wisdom.
verses.hi: जो किसी चीज़ से चिपका नहीं है, और अच्छा मिलने पर न खुशी से उछलता है न बुरा मिलने पर नफ़रत करता है, उसकी बुद्धि स्थिर है।
verses.short: Good news or bad news, they don't overreact either way. That's real stability.
verses.notes: What does 'no love on any side' mean? Not being clingy toward anything. The person isn't thrilled by good or bitter about bad. Doesn't this sound cold? It isn't coldness. It is a calm heart that cares without being controlled by attachment.

verses.en: When someone can pull the senses back from their objects completely, like a tortoise pulls in its limbs, that person's wisdom is firm.
verses.hi: जैसे कछुआ अपने अंगों को अंदर समेट लेता है, वैसे ही जो इंद्रियों को विषयों से पूरी तरह हटा लेता है, उसकी बुद्धि स्थिर है।
verses.short: Like a tortoise pulling in its limbs, pull your senses back from distractions. That's focus.
verses.notes: What does the tortoise example mean? Like a tortoise pulling in its limbs, the wise can withdraw their senses from distractions when needed. How can I apply this today? Notice when your senses are being pulled, like by your phone, and choose to step back.

verses.en: When a person stops feeding the senses, the objects fall away, but the craving for them remains. Even the craving disappears once the Supreme is seen.
verses.hi: इंद्रियों को विषय न देने से विषय तो छूट जाते हैं, पर उनका स्वाद बना रहता है। परमात्मा का अनुभव होने पर वह स्वाद भी मिट जाता है।
verses.short: You can avoid temptations, but the craving stays. It only fades when you find something higher.
verses.notes: Why does fasting not end desire? Staying away from objects stops the action, but the taste for them remains inside. When does the taste itself go? When one sees the Supreme. A higher joy naturally replaces the lower craving.

verses.en: Arjuna, the restless senses can forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is trying hard.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, बेचैन इंद्रियाँ कोशिश कर रहे समझदार व्यक्ति के मन को भी ज़बरदस्ती खींच ले जाती हैं।
verses.short: Your senses are strong enough to drag even a smart person off track. Stay alert.
verses.notes: Can even a wise person be carried away by the senses? Yes. Krishna admits the senses are powerful enough to sweep away the mind of someone who is trying hard. Why is this honesty helpful? It means struggling with distraction is normal. It calls for steady practice, not guilt.

verses.en: Bringing them all under control, one should sit focused, with me as the highest goal. Whoever has the senses under control has steady wisdom.
verses.hi: इन सबको वश में करके मुझमें मन लगाकर स्थिर बैठना चाहिए। जिसकी इंद्रियाँ वश में हैं, उसकी बुद्धि स्थिर है।
verses.short: Control your senses and stay focused on the Divine. That's where steady wisdom comes from.
verses.notes: How do we control the senses? By restraining them and keeping the mind fixed on the Divine as the highest goal. Why does focus on the Divine help? A higher focus gives the mind something to hold, so it isn't dragged around by every distraction.

verses.en: When you keep thinking about sense objects, attachment to them grows. From attachment comes desire, and from desire comes anger.
verses.hi: विषयों के बारे में सोचते रहने से उनसे लगाव हो जाता है। लगाव से इच्छा पैदा होती है, और इच्छा से क्रोध।
verses.short: Keep thinking about something and you get attached. Attachment becomes wanting. Blocked wanting becomes anger. Sound familiar?
verses.notes: How does anger begin? It starts with dwelling on objects. Thinking about them creates attachment, attachment creates desire, and blocked desire becomes anger. Where can this chain be stopped? At the first link, by noticing where your thoughts keep going and redirecting them.

verses.en: Anger leads to confusion, confusion to loss of memory, loss of memory to loss of judgement, and with lost judgement a person is ruined.
verses.hi: क्रोध से भ्रम होता है, भ्रम से याददाश्त बिगड़ती है, याददाश्त बिगड़ने से बुद्धि नष्ट होती है, और बुद्धि नष्ट होने से इंसान का पतन हो जाता है।
verses.short: Anger fogs your head, you forget who you are, you make choices you regret. Catch the spiral early.
verses.notes: What happens after anger? Anger clouds judgment, we forget what we know, our sense of right and wrong breaks down, and we fall. Why is this verse so relevant today? It perfectly describes how a heated moment can lead to decisions we regret.

verses.en: But a self-disciplined person who moves among sense objects with senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, reaches inner peace.
verses.hi: पर जो अपने मन को वश में रखकर, राग और द्वेष से मुक्त इंद्रियों के साथ विषयों के बीच रहता है, वह मन की शांति पाता है।
verses.short: Enjoy the world without love-hate drama and with your senses in check. That's how you find peace.
verses.notes: Can we enjoy the world and still be free? Yes. Someone who moves among things with senses under control, free of attraction and aversion, finds peace. What is the key word here? Self-control. It's not about avoiding the world but not being ruled by it.

verses.en: In that peace, all sorrows end. The mind of a peaceful person quickly becomes steady.
verses.hi: उस शांति में सारे दुख मिट जाते हैं। शांत मन वाले की बुद्धि जल्दी ही स्थिर हो जाती है।
verses.short: With a peaceful mind all sadness fades, and your thinking gets clear fast.
verses.notes: What does serenity do? It ends all sorrow, and in a calm mind, understanding quickly becomes steady. Why is calm linked to wisdom? A peaceful mind sees clearly, the way still water reflects clearly.

verses.en: Someone who is not disciplined has no clear understanding and no focus. Without focus there is no peace, and without peace, how can there be happiness?
verses.hi: जो अनुशासित नहीं है, उसमें न सही समझ होती है न एकाग्रता। एकाग्रता के बिना शांति नहीं, और शांति के बिना सुख कहाँ?
verses.short: No focus, no peace. No peace, no real happiness. It all starts with a steady mind.
verses.notes: Why can't an uncontrolled person find happiness? Without self-control there is no clear understanding, without that no meditation, without meditation no peace, and without peace no happiness. What does this chain show? Happiness is the end result of inner discipline, not of getting more things.

verses.en: When the mind follows the wandering senses, it carries away one's wisdom, like wind carries away a boat on water.
verses.hi: जब मन भटकती इंद्रियों के पीछे चलता है, तो वह बुद्धि को ऐसे बहा ले जाता है जैसे हवा पानी में नाव को।
verses.short: Let your senses run wild and they'll drag your mind like wind pushing a boat off course.
verses.notes: What does the ship example mean? Like wind blowing a boat off course, a mind following the senses gets its judgment carried away. How do we keep our course? By not letting the mind run after every sense that pulls it.

verses.en: So, mighty Arjuna, whoever has fully pulled the senses back from their objects has steady wisdom.
verses.hi: इसलिए हे महाबाहु, जिसने अपनी इंद्रियों को विषयों से पूरी तरह रोक लिया है, उसकी बुद्धि स्थिर है।
verses.short: When your senses don't control you, your wisdom becomes rock solid.
verses.notes: What is Krishna concluding here? The one whose senses are fully restrained from their objects has steady wisdom. Why does Krishna repeat this? Sense control is the practical foundation of everything else he is teaching.

verses.en: What is night for all beings is when the self-controlled person is awake. And what others are awake to is night for the sage who truly sees.
verses.hi: जो सब प्राणियों के लिए रात है, उसमें संयमी व्यक्ति जागता है। और जिसमें सब प्राणी जागते हैं, वह सच देखने वाले मुनि के लिए रात है।
verses.short: What the world hypes, the wise ignore. What the world ignores, the wise see clearly. Different vision.
verses.notes: What does 'night for all beings' mean? What others are blind to, the Self, the sage is awake to. What others chase, the sage sees as darkness. Is this literal sleep? No. It is about awareness: the wise and the worldly are awake to different things.

verses.en: Like the ocean that stays full and still while rivers keep flowing in, a person into whom all desires flow without disturbing them finds peace, not the one who chases desires.
verses.hi: जैसे नदियाँ बहकर समुद्र में मिलती हैं पर वह भरा और शांत रहता है, वैसे ही जिसमें सारी इच्छाएँ समा जाती हैं पर उसे हिला नहीं पातीं, वही शांति पाता है, इच्छाओं के पीछे भागने वाला नहीं।
verses.short: Rivers keep flowing in, but the ocean stays calm. Let desires come and go. That's peace.
verses.notes: What does the ocean example mean? Rivers pour into the ocean but it stays calm and full. Desires enter the wise person's mind without disturbing it. Who doesn't find peace? The one who keeps chasing desires, always needing more.

verses.en: Whoever gives up all desires and lives free from craving, without "mine" and without ego, reaches peace.
verses.hi: जो सारी इच्छाएँ छोड़कर, लालसा, "मेरा" और अहंकार के बिना जीता है, वह शांति पाता है।
verses.short: Drop the cravings, the ego and the "mine, mine, mine" mindset. That's when you find real peace.
verses.notes: What brings peace? Giving up desires and living without craving, possessiveness or ego, the sense of 'I' and 'mine'. Does this mean owning nothing? It means not being owned by what you have. You can use things without clinging.

verses.en: This is the divine state, Arjuna. Having reached it, one is never confused again. Staying in it even at the time of death, one attains liberation in the Supreme.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, यही ब्रह्म की अवस्था है। इसे पाकर कोई फिर भ्रम में नहीं पड़ता। अंत समय में भी इसमें टिके रहकर व्यक्ति ब्रह्म-निर्वाण पाता है।
verses.short: This is the ultimate state: total clarity and calm. Reach it, even at the very end, and you're free.
verses.notes: What is the 'Brahmic state'? The state of being established in the Supreme. Once reached, confusion doesn't return. Why mention the hour of death? Even reaching this state at the very end is enough to attain liberation.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, if you think understanding is better than action, then why are you pushing me into this terrible action?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे जनार्दन, अगर आप ज्ञान को कर्म से श्रेष्ठ मानते हैं, तो हे केशव, मुझे इस भयानक कर्म में क्यों लगा रहे हैं?
verses.short: Arjuna: "If knowledge is better than action, why push me into this fight?" Fair question.
verses.notes: What confuses Arjuna here? Krishna praised wisdom, yet he urges Arjuna to fight. Arjuna asks why act at all if knowledge is higher. Is this a fair question? Yes. Many people wonder whether spiritual life means stepping back from the world. Chapter 3 answers this.

verses.en: Your mixed-up words seem to confuse my mind. Tell me one thing for sure, by which I can reach what is best.
verses.hi: आपकी मिली-जुली बातों से मेरी बुद्धि उलझ रही है। मुझे पक्का एक बात बताइए जिससे मेरा भला हो।
verses.short: "Your advice feels contradictory. Just give me one clear path." We've all wanted this.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask for? One clear path to the highest good, because Krishna's words seem to point both ways. What can we learn from this? When advice feels mixed, it's okay to ask for clarity directly.

verses.en: Krishna said: Sinless Arjuna, long ago I taught two paths in this world: the path of knowledge for thinkers, and the path of action for those who work.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे निष्पाप अर्जुन, इस संसार में मैंने पहले दो मार्ग बताए थे: विचार करने वालों के लिए ज्ञान का मार्ग, और कर्म करने वालों के लिए कर्म का मार्ग।
verses.short: Two paths: the path of knowledge for thinkers, the path of action for doers. Both are valid.
verses.notes: What are the two paths Krishna mentions? The path of knowledge (Jnana Yoga) for the contemplative, and the path of action (Karma Yoga) for the active. Is one path better? Both are valid. Krishna shows they suit different natures.

verses.en: No one becomes free from action just by not starting any work, and no one reaches perfection just by renouncing.
verses.hi: कर्म शुरू न करने से कोई कर्म के बंधन से मुक्त नहीं होता, और केवल त्याग करने से कोई सिद्धि नहीं पाता।
verses.short: Just quitting work doesn't make you free. Escaping isn't the same as growing.
verses.notes: Can we reach freedom by not working? No. Simply stopping action doesn't bring freedom from action's effects. Is giving up work enough? No. Renunciation without inner purity doesn't lead to perfection.

verses.en: No one can stay without doing anything even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act by the qualities born of nature.
verses.hi: कोई भी एक पल के लिए भी बिना कर्म किए नहीं रह सकता। प्रकृति से पैदा हुए गुण हर किसी को कर्म करने पर मजबूर करते हैं।
verses.short: Nobody can do nothing, even for a second. Your nature keeps you moving. So move with purpose.
