verses.notes: Can anyone stop acting completely? No one can stay without action even for a moment. Nature keeps us acting. What does this mean for daily life? Since action is unavoidable, the real question is how to act well.

verses.en: Someone who holds back the organs of action but keeps thinking about sense objects is fooling themselves and is called a pretender.
verses.hi: जो कर्म-इंद्रियों को रोककर मन में विषयों के बारे में सोचता रहता है, वह खुद को धोखा देता है और पाखंडी कहलाता है।
verses.short: Sitting still while your mind binges on cravings? That's just pretending. Fake discipline.
verses.notes: Who is a hypocrite in this verse? Someone who sits still on the outside but keeps dwelling on pleasures in their mind. What is the lesson? Outer show doesn't matter if the mind is still chasing desires.

verses.en: But someone who controls the senses with the mind and, without attachment, uses the organs of action for selfless work, stands out, Arjuna.
verses.hi: पर हे अर्जुन, जो मन से इंद्रियों को वश में करके, बिना आसक्ति के कर्म-इंद्रियों से कर्मयोग करता है, वही श्रेष्ठ है।
verses.short: Control your mind, then act without clinging to results. That person really stands out.
verses.notes: Who excels according to Krishna? The one who controls the senses with the mind and works without attachment. How is this different from the hypocrite? The hypocrite fakes stillness. This person acts fully but with inner control.

verses.en: Do the work you are meant to do, because action is better than inaction. Without action you couldn't even keep your body going.
verses.hi: अपना तय कर्म करो, क्योंकि कर्म करना कर्म न करने से बेहतर है। बिना कर्म के तो तुम्हारा शरीर भी नहीं चल पाएगा।
verses.short: Doing something beats doing nothing. Even staying alive takes action. Stop waiting for the perfect moment.
verses.notes: Why is action better than inaction? Without action you can't even keep your body alive. Doing your duty is better than doing nothing. What is 'obligatory action'? The work that is yours to do because of your role and responsibilities.

verses.en: Work binds people unless it is done as an offering. So, Arjuna, do your work as an offering, free from attachment.
verses.hi: यज्ञ के लिए किए गए कर्म के अलावा हर कर्म इंसान को बाँधता है। इसलिए हे कौन्तेय, आसक्ति छोड़कर यज्ञ भाव से कर्म करो।
verses.short: Work done only for yourself traps you. Work done as an offering sets you free.
verses.notes: When does work bind us? When it's done only for ourselves. Work done as an offering doesn't bind. What does 'work as sacrifice' mean today? Doing your job with care for others and a larger purpose, not just personal gain.

verses.en: In the beginning, the Creator made beings along with sacrifice and said: "Grow through this. Let it give you all you wish for."
verses.hi: शुरुआत में सृष्टिकर्ता ने यज्ञ के साथ प्राणियों को बनाया और कहा: "इसी से फलो-फूलो, यह तुम्हारी सब इच्छाएँ पूरी करे।"
verses.short: From the start, life was designed around giving. Give, and the universe gives back.
verses.notes: What did the Creator say at the beginning? That humans would prosper through sacrifice, and that it would fulfil their needs like a wish-granting cow. What is the idea behind this story? Giving and contributing is built into the design of life.

verses.en: "Nourish the gods with this, and let the gods nourish you. By caring for each other, you will reach the highest good."
verses.hi: "इससे देवताओं को संतुष्ट करो, और देवता तुम्हें संतुष्ट करें। एक-दूसरे का ख्याल रखकर तुम परम कल्याण पाओगे।"
verses.short: Support each other, and everyone wins. Life works best as a team sport.
verses.notes: What does 'nourishing each other' mean? Humans honour the forces of nature, and nature supports humans. Both thrive together. How can we apply this? Take care of the world that takes care of you.

verses.en: "Pleased by sacrifice, the gods will give you the things you want. Whoever enjoys their gifts without giving anything back is simply a thief."
verses.hi: "यज्ञ से प्रसन्न देवता तुम्हें मनचाही चीज़ें देंगे। जो उनकी दी चीज़ें बिना कुछ लौटाए भोगता है, वह चोर ही है।"
verses.short: Taking from the world without giving anything back? That's basically stealing.
verses.notes: Why is someone who only takes called a thief? Because they enjoy what life gives without giving anything back. What is the message? Gratitude should turn into giving, not just receiving.

verses.en: Good people who eat what remains after the offering are freed from all wrongs. But those who cook only for themselves eat sin.
verses.hi: जो सज्जन यज्ञ के बाद बचा हुआ खाते हैं, वे सब पापों से छूट जाते हैं। पर जो केवल अपने लिए पकाते हैं, वे पाप ही खाते हैं।
verses.short: Share first, then enjoy. Living only for yourself leaves you empty.
verses.notes: What does 'eating the remnants of sacrifice' mean? Enjoying what remains after you've shared and offered first. Why is cooking only for yourself a sin? Pure selfishness, even in daily things, closes the heart.

verses.en: Living beings come from food, food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice comes from action.
verses.hi: प्राणी अन्न से होते हैं, अन्न बारिश से, बारिश यज्ञ से, और यज्ञ कर्म से होता है।
verses.short: Food comes from rain, rain from nature's cycle, and that cycle runs on everyone's effort. It's all connected.
verses.notes: What is the cycle described here? Beings come from food, food from rain, rain from sacrifice, and sacrifice from action. What does it teach? Everything is connected. Our actions keep the cycle of life going.

verses.en: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas come from the Imperishable. So the all-pervading Supreme is always present in sacrifice.
verses.hi: जानो कि कर्म वेद से पैदा होता है और वेद अविनाशी परमात्मा से। इसलिए सर्वव्यापी ब्रह्म हमेशा यज्ञ में स्थित है।
verses.short: Every action traces back to something bigger. The divine is present in every act of giving.
verses.notes: Where does action come from? Action arises from the body and nature, which ultimately rest on the Imperishable. Why is Brahman 'established in sacrifice'? The Divine is present wherever work is offered selflessly.

verses.en: Arjuna, whoever doesn't keep this wheel turning, living only for sense pleasure, lives a sinful and wasted life.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, जो इस चक्र को आगे नहीं बढ़ाता और केवल इंद्रियों के सुख में जीता है, उसका पापी जीवन बेकार है।
verses.short: Living just for your own pleasure, ignoring the cycle? That's a wasted life.
verses.notes: What is 'the wheel set in motion'? The cycle of give and take that sustains life. What happens to someone who ignores it? Living only for sense pleasure, they waste their life.

verses.en: But for someone who delights in the self, is satisfied in the self and content in the self alone, there is no duty left to do.
verses.hi: पर जो आत्मा में ही रमता है, आत्मा में ही तृप्त है और आत्मा में ही संतुष्ट है, उसके लिए कोई कर्तव्य बाकी नहीं रहता।
verses.short: When you're truly at peace with yourself, you don't need anything to prove.
verses.notes: Who has nothing left to do? The one who delights in the Self and is fully content within. Does this mean they stop working? They no longer work out of need, but may still act for others' good.

verses.en: Such a person has nothing to gain by acting or by not acting, and doesn't depend on any being for anything.
verses.hi: ऐसे व्यक्ति को न कर्म करने से कुछ पाना है, न कर्म न करने से। उसे किसी भी प्राणी से कोई मतलब नहीं रहता।
verses.short: Someone fully content has nothing to gain or lose from doing or not doing. Total freedom.
verses.notes: Why does the Self-realised person need nothing? They gain nothing by acting and lose nothing by not acting. They depend on no one. Is this state common? No, it's rare. Most of us still need to work, which is why Krishna urges action.

verses.en: So always do the work that needs doing, without attachment. By working without attachment, a person reaches the Supreme.
verses.hi: इसलिए आसक्ति छोड़कर हमेशा अपना कर्तव्य करते रहो। बिना आसक्ति के कर्म करके इंसान परमात्मा को पाता है।
verses.short: So do what needs to be done, without attachment. That's the path to the highest.
verses.notes: How should we work? Do what needs doing, without attachment to the outcome. Where does this lead? To the Supreme. Detached work itself becomes a spiritual path.

verses.en: King Janaka and others reached perfection through action alone. Even just to set an example for the world, you should act.
verses.hi: जनक जैसे राजाओं ने कर्म से ही सिद्धि पाई। दुनिया को राह दिखाने के लिए भी तुम्हें कर्म करना चाहिए।
verses.short: King Janaka reached the top while working. And you set an example for others too.
verses.notes: Who is King Janaka? A wise king who reached perfection while ruling, proving action and wisdom can go together. What is 'welfare of the world' here? Setting a good example and keeping society on track.

verses.en: Whatever a great person does, others copy. Whatever standard they set, the world follows.
verses.hi: श्रेष्ठ व्यक्ति जो करता है, दूसरे भी वही करते हैं। वह जो मिसाल कायम करता है, दुनिया उसी पर चलती है।
verses.short: People copy what leaders do. Whatever standard you set, others will follow. Be a good influence.
verses.notes: Why do people copy great people? Leaders set the standard. Whatever they do, others follow. What responsibility does this bring? If you are looked up to, your actions teach more than your words.

verses.en: Arjuna, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, and nothing I lack or need to gain. Still, I keep working.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, तीनों लोकों में मेरे लिए कुछ करना ज़रूरी नहीं, न कुछ पाना बाकी है। फिर भी मैं कर्म करता रहता हूँ।
verses.short: Krishna: "I have nothing left to achieve, and I still keep working." Ultimate role model.
verses.notes: Why does Krishna work if he needs nothing? There is nothing he must gain, yet he keeps acting to set an example. What does this teach? Even when you don't need to, working for others' sake is noble.

verses.en: If I ever stopped working tirelessly, Arjuna, people everywhere would follow my path.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, अगर मैं कभी सावधानी से कर्म करना छोड़ दूँ, तो लोग हर तरह से मेरे ही रास्ते पर चलेंगे।
verses.short: "If I stopped working, everyone would copy me and stop too."
verses.notes: What would happen if Krishna stopped working? People would follow him and stop working too. What is the point? Those who lead must stay active, because others are watching.

verses.en: If I stopped working, these worlds would fall apart. I would be the cause of chaos and would ruin all these people.
verses.hi: अगर मैं कर्म न करूँ, तो ये लोक नष्ट हो जाएँगे। मैं अव्यवस्था का कारण बनूँगा और इन सब लोगों को बर्बाद कर दूँगा।
verses.short: "If I quit, the world falls into chaos." When people look up to you, your actions matter.
verses.notes: Why would the world fall into chaos? If the one who sustains order stopped acting, everything would fall apart. How does this apply to us? Our roles hold up others. Dropping them affects more than ourselves.

verses.en: Just as the unwise work with attachment, Arjuna, the wise should work without attachment, wanting the good of the world.
verses.hi: हे भारत, जैसे अज्ञानी लोग आसक्ति से कर्म करते हैं, वैसे ही ज्ञानी को दुनिया की भलाई के लिए बिना आसक्ति के कर्म करना चाहिए।
verses.short: Others work for personal gain. The wise work just as hard, but for the good of everyone.
verses.notes: How should the wise work compared to the ignorant? With the same energy, but without attachment and for the good of all. What changes is the motive? Yes. The work looks the same, but the intention is selfless.

verses.en: The wise should not unsettle the minds of the unwise who are attached to work. Instead, working with focus themselves, they should inspire others to work well.
verses.hi: ज्ञानी को कर्म में लगे अज्ञानी लोगों की बुद्धि में भ्रम पैदा नहीं करना चाहिए। बल्कि खुद लगन से कर्म करते हुए उन्हें भी अच्छे कर्म के लिए प्रेरित करना चाहिए।
verses.short: Don't confuse people who are still learning. Lead by doing, not by lecturing.
verses.notes: Why shouldn't the wise confuse others? Telling people to drop their work before they're ready only unsettles them. What should the wise do instead? Work well themselves and inspire others by example.

verses.en: All actions are carried out by the qualities of nature. But a person confused by ego thinks, "I am the doer."
verses.hi: सारे कर्म प्रकृति के गुणों से होते हैं। पर अहंकार से भ्रमित व्यक्ति सोचता है, "करने वाला मैं हूँ।"
verses.short: Nature is doing most of the work. Ego just jumps in and says "I did this."
verses.notes: Who is really doing all actions? The forces of nature, the gunas. Ego makes us think 'I am the doer.' Why does this matter? Seeing this loosens pride in success and guilt in failure.

verses.en: But someone who knows the truth about qualities and actions, mighty Arjuna, sees that it is just qualities acting on qualities, and doesn't get attached.
verses.hi: पर हे महाबाहु, जो गुणों और कर्मों का सच जानता है, वह समझता है कि गुण ही गुणों में बरत रहे हैं, और इसलिए आसक्त नहीं होता।
verses.short: Understand how nature works, and you stop taking everything personally. No attachment.
verses.notes: How does the wise person see action? As the gunas interacting with each other, so they don't get attached. Is this a way to avoid responsibility? No. It's a way to act fully without ego taking over.

verses.en: People deluded by nature's qualities get attached to their actions. The one who knows the whole truth should not unsettle those who know only part.
verses.hi: प्रकृति के गुणों से भ्रमित लोग गुणों और कर्मों में आसक्त रहते हैं। पूरा सच जानने वाले को अधूरा जानने वालों को विचलित नहीं करना चाहिए।
verses.short: People stuck in their patterns need patience, not judgement. Don't shake them up unnecessarily.
verses.notes: What should the wise avoid doing? Unsettling those who are still attached to their work and not ready for deeper truths. Why? Truth shared too early can confuse rather than help.

verses.en: Offering all your actions to me, with your mind fixed on the self, free from hopes and from "mine", fight without inner fever.
verses.hi: अपने सारे कर्म मुझे अर्पण करके, मन को आत्मा में लगाकर, आशा और "मेरेपन" से मुक्त होकर, बिना बेचैनी के युद्ध करो।
verses.short: Hand over your actions to me, drop the ego and anxiety, and do what needs doing. Calmly.
verses.notes: What does Krishna ask of Arjuna here? To offer every action to him, free of desire and 'mine', and fight without inner fever. What is 'fever' here? Anxiety and agitation. Act with a calm mind.

verses.en: Those who always follow this teaching of mine with faith and without finding fault are also freed from the bondage of action.
verses.hi: जो लोग श्रद्धा से और बिना दोष निकाले हमेशा मेरे इस मत का पालन करते हैं, वे भी कर्म के बंधन से छूट जाते हैं।
verses.short: Those who live this with trust and without overthinking it are set free.
verses.notes: Who is freed by this teaching? Those who follow it with faith and without finding fault. Do you need to be perfect? No. Sincere practice and faith are enough to begin.

verses.en: But know that those who find fault with this teaching and don't follow it are confused about all knowledge, lost and thoughtless.
verses.hi: पर जो इस मत में दोष निकालते हैं और इसका पालन नहीं करते, उन्हें सारे ज्ञान से भ्रमित, नष्ट और विवेकहीन जानो।
verses.short: Those who mock it and ignore it miss out completely. Their loss.
verses.notes: What happens to those who reject this teaching? Krishna says they lose their way, confused about what is truly good. Is this a threat? It's a warning: ignoring wisdom leaves you lost.

verses.en: Even a wise person acts according to their own nature. All beings follow their nature. What can forcing it achieve?
verses.hi: ज्ञानी भी अपने स्वभाव के अनुसार ही काम करता है। सभी प्राणी अपनी प्रकृति के पीछे चलते हैं। ज़बरदस्ती रोकने से क्या होगा?
verses.short: Everyone acts according to their nature, even smart people. Suppressing it doesn't work. Channel it instead.
verses.notes: Why can't we just suppress our nature? Everyone acts according to their nature. Forcing it down doesn't work for long. So what should we do? Work with your nature and guide it, instead of fighting it.

verses.en: Attraction and aversion sit in every sense towards its objects. Don't fall under their control. They are roadblocks on your path.
verses.hi: हर इंद्रिय के विषय में राग और द्वेष छिपे रहते हैं। उनके वश में मत आओ। वे तुम्हारे रास्ते के लुटेरे हैं।
verses.short: Likes and dislikes are built into your senses. Don't let them boss you around. They're your enemies.
verses.notes: What are attraction and aversion? Each sense naturally likes some things and dislikes others. Why call them enemies? If they control you, they pull you off course.

verses.en: It is better to do your own duty, even imperfectly, than someone else's duty well. Even dying while doing your own duty is better. Another's duty is full of danger.
verses.hi: दूसरे का धर्म अच्छी तरह निभाने से अपना धर्म अधूरे ढंग से निभाना भी बेहतर है। अपने धर्म में मरना भी अच्छा है, दूसरे का धर्म डर से भरा है।
verses.short: Your own path done imperfectly beats someone else's done perfectly. Stop copy-pasting lives off your feed.
verses.notes: Why is your own duty better, even done poorly? It fits who you are. Living someone else's path, however well, brings fear. How does this apply to careers? Follow what suits your nature, not what looks impressive in someone else's life.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, then what pushes a person to do wrong, even against their will, as if forced?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे वार्ष्णेय, फिर वह क्या है जो इंसान को उसकी इच्छा के खिलाफ़ भी, जैसे ज़बरदस्ती, पाप करने पर मजबूर करता है?
verses.short: Arjuna: "Why do we do wrong things even when we don't want to?" Most relatable question ever.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask? What pushes people to do wrong, even against their will? Why is this question relatable? We all know moments of acting against our better judgment.

verses.en: Krishna said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion. It is never satisfied and leads to great sin. Know it as the enemy here.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: यह काम है, यही क्रोध है, जो रजोगुण से पैदा होता है। यह कभी तृप्त नहीं होता और बड़ा पापी है। इसे ही यहाँ दुश्मन जानो।
verses.short: Krishna: "It's desire, and the anger that follows it. That's the real enemy."
verses.notes: What is the enemy Krishna names? Desire, which turns into anger. Both come from rajas, the restless quality. Why is desire 'a great devourer'? It is never satisfied. The more you feed it, the more it wants.

verses.en: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an unborn baby by the womb, so knowledge is covered by desire.
verses.hi: जैसे आग धुएँ से, आईना धूल से और गर्भ झिल्ली से ढका रहता है, वैसे ही ज्ञान इच्छा से ढका रहता है।
verses.short: Like smoke over fire or dust on a mirror, desire covers up your clarity.
verses.notes: What do the three examples mean? Desire covers wisdom lightly like smoke over fire, more like dust on a mirror, or completely like a womb covering an embryo. What is the takeaway? Desire hides clarity in different degrees, but the light is always beneath.

verses.en: Arjuna, knowledge is covered by this constant enemy of the wise, desire, which is like a fire that can never be filled.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, ज्ञानियों के इस हमेशा के दुश्मन, इच्छा ने ज्ञान को ढक रखा है। यह ऐसी आग है जो कभी नहीं भरती।
verses.short: Desire is never satisfied. Feed it and it just wants more. It blocks your wisdom.
verses.notes: Why is desire called the constant enemy of the wise? It keeps covering wisdom and is never satisfied, like a fire that always wants more fuel. Even the wise struggle? Yes. That's why constant awareness matters.

verses.en: The senses, the mind and the intellect are said to be its home. Through them it hides knowledge and confuses the soul.
verses.hi: इंद्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि इसके ठिकाने कहे जाते हैं। इन्हीं के ज़रिए यह ज्ञान को ढककर आत्मा को भ्रमित करता है।
verses.short: Desire hides in your senses, mind and thinking. That's how it takes over.
verses.notes: Where does desire hide? In the senses, the mind and the intellect. Why does knowing its hiding place help? You can guard those places and catch desire early.

verses.en: So, best of the Bharatas, first control your senses and destroy this evil that ruins knowledge and wisdom.
verses.hi: इसलिए हे भरतश्रेष्ठ, पहले अपनी इंद्रियों को वश में करो और ज्ञान-विज्ञान को नष्ट करने वाले इस पापी को मार डालो।
verses.short: So start with your senses. Get them in check and take down desire early.
verses.notes: Where should we start controlling desire? With the senses, right from the beginning. Why the senses first? They are the entry point. Control them and desire loses its grip.

verses.en: The senses are said to be higher than the body, the mind is higher than the senses, the intellect is higher than the mind, and the self is higher still than the intellect.
verses.hi: कहते हैं कि इंद्रियाँ शरीर से ऊपर हैं, मन इंद्रियों से ऊपर है, बुद्धि मन से ऊपर है, और आत्मा बुद्धि से भी ऊपर है।
verses.short: Senses are strong, the mind is stronger, the intellect stronger still. The real you is above it all.
verses.notes: What is the ladder Krishna describes? The senses are powerful, the mind is higher, the intellect higher still, and the Self is highest of all. Why does this ladder matter? Knowing what is highest in you helps you rule what is lower.

verses.en: So, knowing the self to be higher than the intellect, steady yourself from within and destroy this hard-to-defeat enemy called desire, mighty Arjuna.
verses.hi: इसलिए हे महाबाहु, आत्मा को बुद्धि से ऊपर जानकर, अपने भीतर से खुद को स्थिर करके, इच्छा रूपी इस कठिन दुश्मन को मार डालो।
verses.short: Know who you really are, steady your mind, and defeat desire. Tough enemy, but beatable.
verses.notes: How do we defeat desire? By knowing the Self, which is beyond the intellect, and steadying the mind with that knowledge. Is it easy? Krishna admits desire is hard to beat, but says it can be done.

verses.en: Krishna said: I taught this timeless yoga to Vivasvan, the sun god. Vivasvan passed it to Manu, and Manu passed it to King Ikshvaku.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: यह अविनाशी योग मैंने सूर्यदेव विवस्वान को सिखाया था। विवस्वान ने इसे मनु को बताया, और मनु ने राजा इक्ष्वाकु को।
verses.short: Krishna: "I taught this wisdom ages ago to the Sun god, who passed it down." This isn't new content. It's timeless.
verses.notes: Who first received this teaching? Krishna taught it to Vivasvan, the sun god, who passed it to Manu, who passed it to King Ikshvaku. Why mention this lineage? To show the teaching is ancient and has been passed down carefully, not invented for the moment.

verses.en: Handed down like this, the royal sages knew it. But over a long time, Arjuna, this yoga was lost in the world.
verses.hi: इस तरह परंपरा से मिले इस योग को राजर्षि जानते थे। पर हे परंतप, बहुत समय बीतने से यह योग दुनिया से लुप्त हो गया।
verses.short: Wise kings passed it down for generations, but over time it got lost. Even great wisdom fades if nobody lives it.
verses.notes: How was this Yoga lost? Over a long time, the chain of teachers broke and the knowledge faded. What does this teach about wisdom? Wisdom needs living teachers and practice, or it slowly disappears.

verses.en: Today I have taught you this same ancient yoga, because you are my devotee and my friend. It is the deepest secret.
verses.hi: आज मैंने तुम्हें वही पुराना योग बताया है, क्योंकि तुम मेरे भक्त और मित्र हो। यह सबसे उत्तम रहस्य है।
verses.short: "I'm sharing this secret with you because you're my friend and you're open to it."
verses.notes: Why does Krishna teach Arjuna? Because Arjuna is his devotee and friend. The teaching is shared out of love. Why is it called a 'supreme mystery'? It's deep and not easily grasped without trust and openness.

verses.en: Arjuna said: You were born recently, and Vivasvan was born long ago. How am I to understand that you taught it to him in the beginning?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: आपका जन्म तो अभी हुआ है और विवस्वान का बहुत पहले। मैं कैसे समझूँ कि आपने उन्हें शुरुआत में यह सिखाया?
verses.short: Arjuna: "Wait, you were born way after the Sun god. How did you teach him?" Fair plot-hole check.
verses.notes: What puzzles Arjuna? Krishna was born recently, but Vivasvan lived long ago. How could Krishna have taught him? What does this question set up? Krishna's explanation of his divine nature and repeated births.

verses.en: Krishna said: Arjuna, you and I have both had many births. I know them all, but you don't remember yours.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे अर्जुन, मेरे और तुम्हारे बहुत से जन्म हो चुके हैं। मैं उन सबको जानता हूँ, पर हे परंतप, तुम नहीं जानते।
verses.short: Krishna: "We've both lived many lives. I remember all of mine. You don't remember yours."
verses.notes: What is the difference between Krishna and Arjuna here? Both have had many births, but Krishna remembers them all and Arjuna doesn't. What does this reveal about Krishna? His awareness is unbroken across time.

verses.en: Though I am unborn and unchanging, and the Lord of all beings, I take birth by my own power, through my own nature.
verses.hi: मैं अजन्मा और अविनाशी हूँ, सब प्राणियों का ईश्वर हूँ, फिर भी अपनी प्रकृति को वश में करके अपनी माया से जन्म लेता हूँ।
verses.short: "I'm never truly born and I never change, but I choose to appear in the world through my own power."
verses.notes: How can the unborn be born? Krishna takes birth by his own will, using his power, while remaining unchanged. How is his birth different from ours? We are born because of karma. He chooses to come.

verses.en: Whenever goodness declines and wrongdoing rises, Arjuna, I bring myself forth.
verses.hi: हे भारत, जब-जब धर्म कमज़ोर पड़ता है और अधर्म बढ़ता है, तब-तब मैं खुद को प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.short: Whenever the world gets really messed up and goodness is losing, I show up. Hope is always loading.
verses.notes: When does the Divine appear? Whenever goodness declines and wrongdoing rises. Why is this verse so loved? It promises that the world is never abandoned. Help comes when it's most needed.

verses.en: To protect the good, to destroy evil and to re-establish what is right, I appear age after age.
verses.hi: सज्जनों की रक्षा, दुष्टों के नाश और धर्म की फिर से स्थापना के लिए मैं हर युग में प्रकट होता हूँ।
verses.short: "I come back in every age to protect good people, stop the harmful ones, and reset what's right."
verses.notes: What are the three purposes of the Divine's coming? To protect the good, to end the harm done by the wicked, and to re-establish dharma. What does 'age after age' mean? This happens again and again, whenever the world needs it.

verses.en: Whoever truly understands my divine birth and actions is not born again after leaving the body, Arjuna. They come to me.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, जो मेरे दिव्य जन्म और कर्म को सच में समझ लेता है, वह शरीर छोड़ने के बाद फिर जन्म नहीं लेता, बल्कि मुझे पाता है।
verses.short: Truly understand who Krishna is, and you won't be stuck in the cycle again. You'll reach him.
verses.notes: What happens to one who truly understands Krishna's birth and deeds? They are not reborn and come to him after leaving the body. Why does understanding matter so much? Truly knowing the Divine changes how you live, which frees you.

verses.en: Free from attachment, fear and anger, absorbed in me and relying on me, many, purified by the fire of knowledge, have reached my state of being.
verses.hi: राग, डर और क्रोध से मुक्त, मुझमें लीन और मेरी शरण में रहने वाले बहुत से लोग ज्ञान के तप से शुद्ध होकर मेरे स्वरूप को पा चुके हैं।
verses.short: Free from craving, fear and anger, fully focused on the Divine, many people have already made it. You can too.
verses.notes: What did those who reached Krishna let go of? Desire, fear and anger. What purified them? The discipline of knowledge, along with complete trust in the Divine.

verses.en: However people come to me, I respond to them in the same way. Everyone, Arjuna, follows my path in every way.
verses.hi: जो जिस भाव से मेरी शरण में आता है, मैं उसे उसी तरह अपनाता हूँ। हे पार्थ, सभी लोग हर तरह से मेरे ही मार्ग पर चलते हैं।
verses.short: However you come to me, I meet you there. Every path people take leads to me in the end.
verses.notes: How does Krishna respond to people? In the same way they approach him. As you come to him, he meets you. Does this mean all paths lead to him? Krishna says people follow his path in many ways. Every sincere approach is answered.

verses.en: Wanting success in their work, people here worship the gods, because in the human world, success from action comes quickly.
verses.hi: कर्मों में सफलता चाहने वाले लोग यहाँ देवताओं की पूजा करते हैं, क्योंकि इंसानी दुनिया में कर्म का फल जल्दी मिलता है।
verses.short: People who want quick results pray for quick rewards, and they often get them. But quick isn't lasting.
verses.notes: Why do people worship lesser gods? For quick results. Rewards from rituals come fast in this world. Is that wrong? Not wrong, but limited. The results are temporary.

verses.en: I created the four social orders based on qualities and work. Though I am their creator, know me as the unchanging non-doer.
verses.hi: गुणों और कर्मों के आधार पर चार वर्ण मैंने बनाए हैं। उनका रचयिता होकर भी मुझे अविनाशी और अकर्ता जानो।
verses.short: People have different natures and strengths, so they do different work. Your role comes from who you are, not your label.
verses.notes: What does Krishna say about the four classes? They were set up according to people's qualities and work, not by birth alone. Why is Krishna called a non-doer here? Though he created this order, he isn't bound by it or changed by it.

verses.en: Actions don't stain me, and I have no desire for their results. Whoever understands me this way is not bound by actions.
verses.hi: कर्म मुझे नहीं बाँधते और मुझे कर्म के फल की चाह नहीं। जो मुझे इस तरह जानता है, वह कर्मों से नहीं बँधता।
verses.short: "Actions don't stick to me because I don't crave results." Get this and your work stops weighing you down.
verses.notes: Why don't actions touch Krishna? He has no desire for their results. What does this mean for us? If we also act without craving results, we aren't bound either.

verses.en: Knowing this, seekers of freedom in ancient times did their work. So you too should act, as the ancients did long ago.
verses.hi: यह जानकर पुराने समय के मुक्ति चाहने वालों ने भी कर्म किए। इसलिए तुम भी वैसे ही कर्म करो जैसे पूर्वजों ने किए थे।
verses.short: Wise people before you worked this way and found freedom. So follow their lead and do your work.
verses.notes: What did earlier seekers of liberation do? They kept working, knowing this truth. What does Krishna ask of Arjuna? To do his work the same way the ancients did.

verses.en: What is action and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. I will explain action to you, and knowing it, you will be free from harm.
verses.hi: कर्म क्या है और अकर्म क्या है, इस बारे में ज्ञानी भी उलझ जाते हैं। मैं तुम्हें कर्म समझाता हूँ, जिसे जानकर तुम अशुभ से मुक्त हो जाओगे।
verses.short: What counts as action? What counts as doing nothing? Even smart people get confused. Krishna's about to explain.
verses.notes: Why are even the wise confused about action? Because what counts as action and non-action is subtle and not obvious. What does Krishna promise to explain? The kind of action that, once understood, frees you from harm.

verses.en: You need to understand action, wrong action and inaction. The way of action is hard to grasp.
verses.hi: कर्म को भी समझना ज़रूरी है, विकर्म को भी और अकर्म को भी। कर्म की गति बहुत गहरी है।
verses.short: Right action, wrong action, and no action all need to be understood. The way of action is deep.
verses.notes: What three things must be understood? Right action, wrong action and inaction. Why is the path of action 'mysterious'? The same outer act can bind or free, depending on the intention behind it.

verses.en: Whoever sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people. Such a person is in yoga, even while doing all kinds of work.
verses.hi: जो कर्म में अकर्म और अकर्म में कर्म देखता है, वह इंसानों में बुद्धिमान है। सारे कर्म करते हुए भी वह योग में स्थित है।
verses.short: Being busy isn't always action, and being still isn't always idle. See through that and you're wise.
verses.notes: What is 'action in inaction'? Seeing that a busy person can be inwardly free, and an idle person can be bound by desire. Who is truly wise? The one who sees this difference and acts from inner freedom.

verses.en: When all of someone's efforts are free from selfish desire and scheming, and their actions are burned up in the fire of knowledge, the wise call that person learned.
verses.hi: जिसके सारे काम स्वार्थी इच्छा और योजना से मुक्त हैं, और जिसके कर्म ज्ञान की आग में जल चुके हैं, उसे ज्ञानी लोग पंडित कहते हैं।
verses.short: Someone whose work has no selfish agenda, whose actions are cleansed by understanding, is truly wise.
verses.notes: Who do the wise call a sage? Someone whose actions are free from selfish desire, burned clean by knowledge. What does 'burned in the fire of knowledge' mean? Wisdom removes the binding effect of actions.

verses.en: Letting go of attachment to results, always content and depending on nothing, such a person does nothing at all, even while fully engaged in action.
verses.hi: कर्म-फल की आसक्ति छोड़कर, हमेशा संतुष्ट और किसी पर निर्भर न रहने वाला व्यक्ति कर्म में पूरी तरह लगा रहकर भी कुछ नहीं करता।
verses.short: Drop the obsession with results, feel complete within, depend on no one. You're working, but it doesn't bind you.
verses.notes: How can someone act and yet do nothing? When they drop attachment to results and rest content in the Self, their action leaves no trace. What does 'dependent on none' mean? Their peace doesn't hang on anyone or anything outside.

verses.en: Without expectations, with mind and body controlled, giving up all possessiveness, doing only what the body needs, such a person incurs no sin.
verses.hi: बिना आशा के, मन और शरीर को वश में रखकर, सब संग्रह छोड़कर, केवल शरीर के लिए ज़रूरी कर्म करने वाला व्यक्ति पाप का भागी नहीं होता।
verses.short: No cravings, mind in control, no hoarding. Just doing what's needed. Nothing bad sticks to you.
verses.notes: What kind of person is free from sin while working? One without craving, with mind and body controlled, who has let go of possessiveness. What is 'bodily work only'? Doing what's needed to live, without selfish motive.

verses.en: Content with whatever comes on its own, beyond opposites, free from envy, and the same in success and failure, such a person is not bound even when acting.
verses.hi: जो अपने आप मिले उसमें संतुष्ट, द्वंद्वों से परे, ईर्ष्या से मुक्त, और सफलता-असफलता में एक समान रहने वाला, कर्म करते हुए भी नहीं बँधता।
verses.short: Happy with what comes, unbothered by ups and downs, no jealousy. You act, but stay free.
verses.notes: How does a free person handle what comes? They are content with whatever comes naturally, beyond likes and dislikes and envy. Why aren't they bound? Because they stay even-minded in success and failure.

verses.en: For someone free from attachment, liberated, with a mind settled in knowledge, who works as an offering, all their karma melts away.
verses.hi: जिसकी आसक्ति मिट गई है, जो मुक्त है, जिसका मन ज्ञान में स्थित है, और जो यज्ञ के लिए कर्म करता है, उसके सारे कर्म घुलकर मिट जाते हैं।
verses.short: When attachment is gone and work becomes an offering, your karma just melts away.
verses.notes: When does karma fully dissolve? When a person is unattached, free, rooted in knowledge, and works only as an offering. What does this teach? The attitude behind work decides whether it binds.

verses.en: The act of offering is the Divine, the offering is the Divine, poured by the Divine into the fire that is the Divine. Whoever sees the Divine in all action reaches the Divine.
verses.hi: अर्पण करना ब्रह्म है, अर्पित चीज़ ब्रह्म है, ब्रह्म रूपी अग्नि में ब्रह्म के द्वारा ही आहुति दी जाती है। जो हर कर्म में ब्रह्म देखता है, वह ब्रह्म को ही पाता है।
verses.short: See the divine in everything: the offering, the act, the one who offers, the goal. Then every task becomes sacred.
verses.notes: What does this verse say about offering? The offering, the act and the one offering are all the Divine. Seeing this, work becomes worship. Why is it recited before meals? It turns eating into a sacred act by seeing the Divine in everything.

verses.en: Some yogis make offerings to the gods. Others offer the self as sacrifice into the fire of the Supreme.
verses.hi: कुछ योगी देवताओं के लिए यज्ञ करते हैं। दूसरे ब्रह्म रूपी अग्नि में यज्ञ के द्वारा ही यज्ञ की आहुति देते हैं।
verses.short: Some people worship through rituals, others through pure understanding. There's more than one way to give.
verses.notes: What different sacrifices are mentioned? Some worship the gods through rituals; others offer themselves into the fire of the Supreme. What is the point of listing them? To show there are many sincere ways to offer one's life.

verses.en: Some offer hearing and the other senses into the fire of self-control. Others offer sound and other sense objects into the fire of the senses.
verses.hi: कुछ लोग सुनने आदि इंद्रियों को संयम की अग्नि में अर्पित करते हैं। दूसरे शब्द आदि विषयों को इंद्रियों की अग्नि में अर्पित करते हैं।
verses.short: Some practice self-control over their senses, others enjoy the world mindfully. Both can be offerings.
verses.notes: What is offering the senses into restraint? Holding back the senses from their objects through self-control. What is offering sense objects into the senses? Experiencing the world without attachment, as an offering.

verses.en: Others offer all the actions of the senses and of the life breath into the fire of self-discipline, lit by knowledge.
verses.hi: दूसरे लोग सारी इंद्रियों और प्राण के कर्मों को ज्ञान से जलाई गई आत्म-संयम रूपी योग की अग्नि में अर्पित करते हैं।
verses.short: Some offer their senses and breath into the fire of a disciplined mind. Self-control as worship.
verses.notes: What sacrifice is described here? Offering all sense and breath activity into the fire of a controlled mind, lit by knowledge. What does it mean practically? Deep inner discipline in which the mind rests in the Self.

verses.en: Some offer wealth, some offer austerity, some offer yoga practice, and others with strict vows offer study and knowledge.
verses.hi: कुछ धन का यज्ञ करते हैं, कुछ तप का, कुछ योग का, और कठोर व्रत वाले कुछ लोग स्वाध्याय और ज्ञान का यज्ञ करते हैं।
verses.short: Some give wealth, some do tough discipline, some practise yoga, some study deeply. All count if done sincerely.
verses.notes: What other forms of sacrifice are there? Giving wealth, practising austerity, doing yoga, and studying scripture to gain knowledge. What do they share? Self-control and firm resolve.

verses.en: Others, devoted to breath control, offer the outgoing breath into the incoming and the incoming into the outgoing, holding the flow of both.
verses.hi: प्राणायाम में लगे दूसरे लोग प्राण और अपान की गति को रोककर अपान में प्राण को और प्राण में अपान को अर्पित करते हैं।
verses.short: Some focus on mindful eating and breathwork. Even breathing can become a spiritual practice.
verses.notes: What is this breath sacrifice? Breath control (pranayama), where incoming and outgoing breaths are regulated and held. Why mention a restricted diet? Moderate eating supports this practice and steadies the mind.

verses.en: Still others, eating with restraint, offer their life breaths into the life breaths. All of them understand sacrifice and are cleansed of wrongs by it.
verses.hi: और कुछ लोग नियमित भोजन करते हुए प्राणों को प्राणों में अर्पित करते हैं। ये सभी यज्ञ को जानने वाले हैं और यज्ञ से इनके पाप मिट जाते हैं।
verses.short: All of them understand what giving means, and giving cleans them up. That's how they move forward.
verses.notes: What do all these practices achieve? They clean away faults and lead to the eternal. What is the 'nectar' of sacrifice? What remains after offering: life lived with a pure heart.

verses.en: Those who enjoy the nectar left over from sacrifice reach the eternal Supreme. Arjuna, this world isn't for someone who makes no sacrifice, let alone the next.
verses.hi: जो यज्ञ से बचे अमृत को भोगते हैं, वे सनातन ब्रह्म को पाते हैं। हे कुरुश्रेष्ठ, जो यज्ञ नहीं करता उसके लिए यह लोक भी नहीं, फिर परलोक कहाँ?
verses.short: If you never give anything, even this life won't work out for you, let alone the next.
verses.notes: What happens to someone who never sacrifices? They don't find happiness even in this world, let alone beyond. Why is giving so central? A life with no giving shrinks into selfishness.

verses.en: Many kinds of sacrifice like these are laid out in the Vedas. Know that they all come from action. Knowing this, you will be free.
verses.hi: इस तरह के बहुत से यज्ञ वेदों में बताए गए हैं। जानो कि ये सब कर्म से पैदा होते हैं। यह जानकर तुम मुक्त हो जाओगे।
verses.short: There are many ways of giving, and all involve action. Understand that and you're free.
verses.notes: What do all sacrifices have in common? They all come from action. What freedom does knowing this bring? You see that action, rightly done, is itself a path to liberation.

verses.en: The sacrifice of knowledge is better than the sacrifice of material things, Arjuna. All action, without exception, finds its fulfilment in knowledge.
verses.hi: हे परंतप, चीज़ों के यज्ञ से ज्ञान का यज्ञ श्रेष्ठ है। हे पार्थ, सारे कर्म अंत में ज्ञान में ही पूरे होते हैं।
verses.short: Sharing wisdom beats sharing stuff. All action ultimately leads to understanding.
verses.notes: Why is the sacrifice of knowledge better? All action finally finds its fulfilment in knowledge. Does this mean rituals are useless? No. They prepare the way, but knowledge completes it.

verses.en: Learn this by bowing down, by asking questions and by serving. The wise who have seen the truth will teach you this knowledge.
verses.hi: इसे झुककर प्रणाम करके, सवाल पूछकर और सेवा करके सीखो। सत्य को देखने वाले ज्ञानी तुम्हें यह ज्ञान सिखाएँगे।
verses.short: Find a real teacher. Be humble, ask questions, and help out. That's how wisdom gets passed on.
verses.notes: How do we learn from a teacher? With humility, sincere questions and service. Who should we learn from? Those who have seen the truth themselves, not just read about it.

verses.en: Knowing this, you will never be confused like this again, Arjuna. Through it you will see all beings in yourself, and then in me.
verses.hi: हे पांडव, यह जानकर तुम फिर कभी ऐसे भ्रम में नहीं पड़ोगे। इससे तुम सभी प्राणियों को अपने भीतर और फिर मुझमें देखोगे।
verses.short: Once you get it, you won't be confused like this again. You'll see everyone as part of you, and you in me.
verses.notes: What does this knowledge do? It ends confusion for good. You see all beings in yourself and in the Divine. How does that change how we treat others? When you see yourself in everyone, kindness becomes natural.

verses.en: Even if you were the worst of all wrongdoers, you would cross over all wrongdoing on the boat of knowledge.
verses.hi: अगर तुम सब पापियों में सबसे बड़े पापी भी हो, तब भी ज्ञान की नाव से सारे पापों को पार कर जाओगे।
verses.short: Even if you've made the worst mistakes, wisdom is a boat that gets you across. Nobody's beyond saving.
verses.notes: Can even the worst wrongdoer be saved? Yes. The boat of knowledge can carry anyone across all wrongs. What hope does this give? Your past doesn't have to define your future.

verses.en: Just as a blazing fire turns wood to ash, Arjuna, the fire of knowledge turns all karma to ash.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, जैसे जलती आग लकड़ी को राख कर देती है, वैसे ही ज्ञान की आग सारे कर्मों को राख कर देती है।
verses.short: Like fire burns wood to ash, real understanding burns up your past karma.
verses.notes: How is knowledge like fire? As fire reduces wood to ash, knowledge burns away the hold of all past actions. Does this mean past mistakes don't matter? They matter, but understanding frees you from being bound by them.

verses.en: There is nothing in this world as purifying as knowledge. Someone perfected in yoga finds it within themselves in time.
verses.hi: इस दुनिया में ज्ञान जैसा पवित्र करने वाला कुछ नहीं है। योग में सिद्ध व्यक्ति समय के साथ इसे अपने भीतर पा लेता है।
verses.short: Nothing cleanses you like wisdom. Keep doing your work right, and it shows up within you in time.
verses.notes: Why is knowledge the greatest purifier? Nothing cleans the mind like true understanding. How does one find it? Through selfless action, it arises naturally within, in time.

verses.en: A person of faith, devoted and with senses controlled, gains knowledge. Having gained it, they soon reach supreme peace.
verses.hi: श्रद्धा वाला, लगन वाला और इंद्रियों को वश में रखने वाला व्यक्ति ज्ञान पाता है। ज्ञान पाकर वह जल्दी ही परम शांति पा लेता है।
verses.short: Trust it, stay committed, control your senses, and wisdom comes. With it comes deep peace, fast.
verses.notes: Who gains knowledge? One with faith, who is devoted to it and controls the senses. What follows knowledge? Supreme peace, and quickly.

verses.en: The ignorant, the faithless and the doubter are ruined. For the doubter there is no happiness, neither in this world nor the next.
verses.hi: अज्ञानी, श्रद्धाहीन और शक करने वाला व्यक्ति नष्ट हो जाता है। शक करने वाले के लिए न यह लोक है, न परलोक, न सुख।
verses.short: Constant doubt with no trust leaves you with nothing, here or anywhere. Overthinking everything kills happiness.
verses.notes: Why is doubt so harmful? A person full of doubt can't commit to anything, so they find no happiness here or beyond. Is all questioning bad? No. Honest questions lead to clarity. Constant doubt leads nowhere.

verses.en: Arjuna, actions don't bind someone who has given up action through yoga, whose doubts are cut by knowledge, and who is centred in the self.
verses.hi: हे धनंजय, जिसने योग से कर्मों को अर्पित कर दिया है, ज्ञान से जिसके संदेह कट गए हैं, और जो आत्मा में स्थित है, उसे कर्म नहीं बाँधते।
verses.short: Work without attachment, clear your doubts with understanding, stay grounded. Then actions can't trap you.
verses.notes: Who is not bound by action? The one who has offered actions through yoga, cleared doubt through knowledge, and is self-possessed. What brings these together? Action and knowledge working together.

verses.en: So cut this doubt in your heart, born of ignorance, with the sword of knowledge. Take up yoga and stand up, Arjuna.
verses.hi: इसलिए हे भारत, अज्ञान से पैदा हुए अपने दिल के इस संदेह को ज्ञान की तलवार से काटो। योग में स्थित हो जाओ और उठ खड़े हो।
verses.short: Cut through your doubt with the sword of wisdom. Now stand up and do what you need to do.
verses.notes: What does Krishna ask Arjuna to do? Cut through the doubt in his heart with the sword of knowledge, and rise. Why the image of a sword? Doubt needs to be cut decisively, not just thought about forever.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, you praise giving up action, and then you praise doing action with yoga. Tell me for certain which of the two is better.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे कृष्ण, आप कभी कर्मों के त्याग की और कभी कर्मयोग की प्रशंसा करते हैं। इन दोनों में जो पक्का बेहतर हो, वह मुझे बताइए।
verses.short: Arjuna: "You praise quitting action, then you praise doing action. Which one's actually better?"
verses.notes: What is Arjuna asking? Krishna has praised both renouncing action and selfless action. Arjuna wants to know which one is better. Why does he keep asking this? He wants one clear answer, a very human wish when facing a hard choice.

verses.en: Krishna said: Renouncing action and acting with yoga both lead to the highest good. But of the two, acting with yoga is better than renouncing action.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: कर्म का त्याग और कर्मयोग, दोनों ही परम कल्याण देते हैं। पर इन दोनों में कर्मयोग, कर्म-त्याग से श्रेष्ठ है।
verses.short: Krishna: "Both get you there, but doing your work selflessly beats just dropping everything."
verses.notes: Which is better, renunciation or Karma Yoga? Both lead to the highest good, but Karma Yoga is better. Why is Karma Yoga better? It is more practical and purifies the mind while you keep living and working.

verses.en: Someone who neither hates nor craves should be known as a true renunciant. Free from opposites, mighty Arjuna, they are easily freed from bondage.
verses.hi: जो न किसी से नफ़रत करता है, न कुछ चाहता है, उसे सच्चा संन्यासी जानो। हे महाबाहु, द्वंद्वों से मुक्त व्यक्ति आसानी से बंधन से छूट जाता है।
verses.short: Someone who doesn't hate or crave, and isn't tossed by ups and downs, has already let go. They're free.
verses.notes: Who is a true renunciate? Someone who neither hates nor craves, even while living an active life. Does renunciation mean leaving home? No. It's an inner state, free from likes and dislikes.

verses.en: Only the naive say the path of knowledge and the path of action are different, not the wise. Whoever truly follows even one gets the result of both.
verses.hi: ज्ञान और कर्मयोग को अलग-अलग नासमझ लोग बताते हैं, ज्ञानी नहीं। जो किसी एक में भी ठीक से टिकता है, वह दोनों का फल पाता है।
verses.short: Only beginners think knowledge and action are rivals. Commit fully to one and you get the benefits of both.
verses.notes: Are knowledge and action two different paths? Only the immature see them as separate. Following one well brings the fruit of both. Why does this matter? You don't have to choose between thinking deeply and acting well.

verses.en: The state reached by the path of knowledge is also reached by the path of action. Whoever sees knowledge and action as one truly sees.
verses.hi: ज्ञान मार्ग वाले जिस स्थान को पाते हैं, कर्मयोगी भी वहीं पहुँचते हैं। जो ज्ञान और कर्मयोग को एक देखता है, वही सही देखता है।
verses.short: Thinkers and doers reach the same place. Whoever sees they're one path really gets it.
verses.notes: Do both paths reach the same place? Yes. The goal reached through knowledge is also reached through selfless action. Who truly sees? The one who sees that the two paths are one.

verses.en: But renunciation is hard to reach without yoga, mighty Arjuna. A sage who practises yoga soon reaches the Supreme.
verses.hi: पर हे महाबाहु, कर्मयोग के बिना संन्यास पाना कठिन है। योग में लगा मुनि जल्दी ही ब्रह्म को पा लेता है।
verses.short: Trying to renounce everything without first doing the work is really hard. Act selflessly and you'll get there faster.
verses.notes: Why is renunciation hard without yoga? Without first purifying the mind through selfless action, true letting go is very difficult. What happens to the one who practises yoga? They reach the Supreme quickly.

verses.en: Someone devoted to yoga, pure in heart, self-controlled and master of the senses, who sees their own self in all beings, is not stained even while acting.
verses.hi: जो योग में लगा है, जिसका मन शुद्ध है, जो खुद पर और इंद्रियों पर काबू रखता है, और सब प्राणियों में अपनी आत्मा देखता है, वह कर्म करते हुए भी लिप्त नहीं होता।
verses.short: Clean heart, self-control, and seeing yourself in everyone. Then even while working, nothing sticks to you.
verses.notes: How can someone act and not be tainted? When their mind is pure, senses controlled, and they see their Self in all beings. What does 'self of all beings' mean? Feeling one with everyone, so selfishness has no ground.

verses.en: A person who knows the truth, steady in yoga, thinks, "I am not doing anything," even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping and breathing,
verses.hi: सत्य को जानने वाला योगी देखते, सुनते, छूते, सूँघते, खाते, चलते, सोते और साँस लेते हुए भी यही मानता है कि "मैं कुछ नहीं कर रहा,"
verses.short: Seeing, hearing, eating, walking, sleeping. The wise know it's the senses doing their thing, not ego.
verses.notes: Why does the wise person think 'I do nothing'? They know the senses are acting on their objects, while the Self only witnesses. Is this an excuse to avoid responsibility? No. It removes ego from action, not care from action.

verses.en: while talking, letting go, holding, opening and closing the eyes. They understand that it is just the senses moving among their objects.
verses.hi: बोलते, छोड़ते, पकड़ते, आँखें खोलते और बंद करते हुए भी। वह समझता है कि बस इंद्रियाँ अपने विषयों में बरत रही हैं।
verses.short: Talking, blinking, grabbing stuff: it's all senses meeting the world. You're the witness, not the ego.
verses.notes: What examples does Krishna give? Speaking, letting go, grasping, even opening and closing the eyes. What is the idea? Even simple actions are the senses at work. The Self stays untouched.

verses.en: Whoever acts by offering all actions to the Supreme and letting go of attachment is not touched by sin, like a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
verses.hi: जो सारे कर्म ब्रह्म को अर्पित करके और आसक्ति छोड़कर कर्म करता है, उसे पाप ऐसे नहीं छूता जैसे कमल के पत्ते को पानी।
verses.short: Act without attachment and offer it up, and nothing bad sticks, like water off a lotus leaf.
verses.notes: What does the lotus leaf example teach? A lotus leaf sits in water but stays dry. Act in the world but don't let it stick to you. How do we become like the lotus leaf? By offering actions to the Divine and dropping attachment.

verses.en: Yogis act with the body, mind, intellect and even the senses alone, letting go of attachment, to purify themselves.
verses.hi: योगी आसक्ति छोड़कर, अपने आप को शुद्ध करने के लिए, शरीर, मन, बुद्धि और केवल इंद्रियों से कर्म करते हैं।
verses.short: Yogis use body, mind and senses to work, but only to purify themselves, not to get stuff.
verses.notes: Why do yogis keep working? To purify themselves, not for personal gain. What tools do they use? Body, mind, intellect and senses, all without attachment.

verses.en: A balanced person who gives up the fruits of action reaches lasting peace. An unbalanced person, driven by desire and attached to results, is bound.
verses.hi: योग में स्थित व्यक्ति कर्म-फल छोड़कर स्थायी शांति पाता है। पर जो योग में नहीं, वह इच्छा से प्रेरित होकर फल में आसक्त रहता है और बँध जाता है।
verses.short: Let go of the results and you find lasting peace. Chase the results and you stay stuck.
verses.notes: Who finds lasting peace? The one who lets go of the fruits of action. Who stays bound? The one driven by desire and attached to results.

verses.en: Mentally giving up all actions, the self-controlled soul lives happily in the city of nine gates, the body, neither acting nor causing action.
verses.hi: मन से सारे कर्मों को त्यागकर, संयमी आत्मा नौ द्वारों वाले शहर, यानी शरीर में, सुख से रहती है, न खुद कुछ करती है न करवाती है।
verses.short: Your body is like a house with nine doors. Live in it calmly, without claiming credit for everything.
verses.notes: What is the 'city of nine gates'? The body, with its nine openings. The Self lives in it like a resident, not a worker. How does the wise person live in it? Happily and in control, without thinking they are the doer.

verses.en: The Lord does not create a sense of doership, or actions, or the link between action and result for people. It is nature that does all this.
verses.hi: ईश्वर लोगों के लिए न कर्तापन बनाता है, न कर्म, न कर्म और फल का संबंध। यह सब तो स्वभाव से होता है।
verses.short: Your true self doesn't create the drama of doing or the results. Your habits and nature run that show.
verses.notes: Does God make us act? No. The sense of doing, actions and their results come from our own nature. What does this mean for responsibility? We can't blame God for our choices. They come from our tendencies.

verses.en: The all-pervading Lord does not take on anyone's sin or good deeds. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and that is why beings are confused.
verses.hi: सर्वव्यापी ईश्वर न किसी का पाप लेता है, न पुण्य। ज्ञान अज्ञान से ढका है, इसलिए प्राणी भ्रम में रहते हैं।
verses.short: God isn't keeping score of your sins and good deeds. Confusion just hides the truth from us.
verses.notes: Does God take anyone's sins or merits? No. The Divine takes neither. Why are people confused then? Ignorance covers knowledge, and that causes delusion.

verses.en: But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the self, that knowledge lights up the Supreme like the sun.
verses.hi: पर जिनका अज्ञान आत्मा के ज्ञान से मिट गया है, उनका ज्ञान सूरज की तरह परमात्मा को प्रकाशित कर देता है।
verses.short: When real understanding wipes out that confusion, the truth shines like the sun.
verses.notes: What happens when ignorance is removed? Knowledge shines like the sun and reveals the Supreme. Why compare it to the sun? Just as the sun lights everything, knowledge makes everything clear.

verses.en: With their mind on the Supreme, their being in it, devoted to it and making it their goal, their wrongs washed away by knowledge, they reach the state of no return.
verses.hi: जिनकी बुद्धि उसमें है, जो उसी में लीन हैं, उसी में निष्ठा रखते हैं और उसी को लक्ष्य मानते हैं, ज्ञान से जिनके पाप धुल गए हैं, वे फिर लौटकर नहीं आते।
verses.short: Make the highest truth your focus, think about it, commit to it, and you'll reach a place you never fall back from.
verses.notes: Who reaches the point of no return? Those whose mind, intellect and devotion are fully set on the Supreme. What cleanses them? Knowledge, which washes away all faults.

verses.en: The wise see with equal eyes a learned and humble priest, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.
verses.hi: ज्ञानी लोग विद्वान और विनम्र ब्राह्मण, गाय, हाथी, कुत्ते और चांडाल को एक ही नज़र से देखते हैं।
verses.short: The wise see the same soul in a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast. No hierarchy.
verses.notes: How do the wise see others? Equally: a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast are seen as the same Self. Does this mean treating everyone the same way? It means equal respect and dignity, seeing the same Self in all.

verses.en: Those whose minds rest in equality have conquered the cycle of birth here and now. The Supreme is flawless and equal to all, so they live in the Supreme.
verses.hi: जिनका मन समता में टिका है, उन्होंने यहीं जन्म-मृत्यु के चक्र को जीत लिया है। ब्रह्म दोषरहित और सबके लिए समान है, इसलिए वे ब्रह्म में स्थित हैं।
verses.short: See everyone as equal, and you've already won at life, right here, right now.
verses.notes: Can we be free in this life itself? Yes. Those with an even mind overcome the cycle of birth here and now. Why is equality linked to the Divine? The Supreme is flawless and equal everywhere. An even mind reflects that.

verses.en: Someone who knows the Supreme and lives in it, steady-minded and unconfused, doesn't get excited by what is pleasant or upset by what is unpleasant.
verses.hi: जो ब्रह्म को जानता है और उसमें स्थित है, जिसकी बुद्धि स्थिर और भ्रम से मुक्त है, वह न प्रिय पाकर खुश होता है, न अप्रिय पाकर दुखी।
verses.short: Don't get hyped by good news or crushed by bad news. Stay steady and clear.
verses.notes: How does a knower of the Supreme react to good and bad? They don't get overly happy at the pleasant or upset at the unpleasant. What keeps them steady? A clear mind, free of confusion, rooted in the Supreme.

verses.en: Someone unattached to outside pleasures finds joy within. United with the Supreme through yoga, they enjoy endless happiness.
verses.hi: जो बाहर के सुखों से आसक्त नहीं है, वह अपने भीतर आनंद पाता है। योग से ब्रह्म से जुड़कर वह कभी न खत्म होने वाला सुख भोगता है।
verses.short: Stop needing outside things for happiness. Find joy within and it lasts forever.
verses.notes: Where does the wise person find happiness? Within, not in external pleasures. What kind of joy is it? Undying joy, because it doesn't depend on anything outside.

verses.en: Pleasures born from sense contact are the source of pain. They have a beginning and an end, Arjuna. The wise don't take delight in them.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, इंद्रियों के संपर्क से मिलने वाले सुख दुख की जड़ हैं। उनका आरंभ और अंत होता है, इसलिए ज्ञानी उनमें नहीं रमता।
verses.short: Pleasures from the senses start and end, and leave pain behind. The wise don't get hooked.
verses.notes: Why are sense pleasures called 'wombs of pain'? They begin and end, and their ending brings pain. Should we avoid all pleasure? No, but don't build your happiness on them. The wise don't rely on them.

verses.en: Whoever can withstand the rush of desire and anger here, before leaving the body, is a true yogi and a happy person.
verses.hi: जो शरीर छूटने से पहले यहीं इच्छा और क्रोध के वेग को सह लेता है, वही योगी है और वही सुखी इंसान है।
verses.short: If you can handle the rush of desire and anger in this life, you're a real yogi and truly happy.
verses.notes: Who is truly happy? The one who can handle the force of desire and anger before leaving the body. Is this about suppressing emotions? It's about not being carried away by them.

verses.en: Whoever finds happiness within, delight within and light within, that yogi becomes one with the Supreme and reaches liberation in it.
verses.hi: जो भीतर ही सुखी है, भीतर ही रमता है और भीतर ही जिसे प्रकाश मिलता है, वह योगी ब्रह्म-रूप होकर ब्रह्म-निर्वाण पाता है।
verses.short: Joy inside, peace inside, light inside. That person has found the ultimate happiness.
verses.notes: Where does a yogi find joy and light? Within. Their happiness, peace and light are all inside. What do they attain? Oneness with the Supreme and its peace.

verses.en: Sages whose wrongs are wiped away, whose doubts are cut, who are self-controlled and devoted to the good of all beings, reach liberation in the Supreme.
verses.hi: जिन ऋषियों के पाप मिट गए हैं, संदेह कट गए हैं, जो संयमी हैं और सब प्राणियों की भलाई में लगे हैं, वे ब्रह्म-निर्वाण पाते हैं।
verses.short: Calm, self-controlled, free from extremes and working for everyone's good. That's how you find bliss.
verses.notes: Who attains liberation? Sages free of doubt and faults, self-controlled, and devoted to the welfare of all beings. Why is helping others part of it? Caring for all beings flows naturally from seeing the one Self in all.

verses.en: For seekers free from desire and anger, with controlled minds and knowledge of the self, liberation in the Supreme is close on every side.
verses.hi: इच्छा और क्रोध से मुक्त, मन को वश में रखने वाले और आत्मा को जानने वाले साधकों के लिए ब्रह्म-निर्वाण चारों ओर मौजूद है।
verses.short: Free from desire and anger, mind under control. For those people, peace is right there.
verses.notes: How close is liberation for the disciplined? Very close, all around them, for those free of desire and anger. What does it require? Steady effort and a controlled mind.

verses.en: Shutting out outside contacts, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, and evening out the breath moving in and out through the nose,
verses.hi: बाहर के विषयों को बाहर ही छोड़कर, नज़र को भौंहों के बीच टिकाकर, और नाक में चलने वाली अंदर-बाहर की साँस को समान करके,
verses.short: Block out distractions, focus your gaze between your eyebrows, balance your breath. Meditation 101.
verses.notes: What practice is described here? Shutting out outer distractions, focusing between the eyebrows and balancing the breath. Why balance the breath? A calm breath leads to a calm mind.

verses.en: the sage who controls senses, mind and intellect, aims for freedom and is rid of desire, fear and anger, is truly free forever.
verses.hi: जिस मुनि ने इंद्रियों, मन और बुद्धि को वश में कर लिया है, जिसका लक्ष्य मोक्ष है और जो इच्छा, डर और क्रोध से मुक्त है, वह हमेशा मुक्त ही है।
verses.short: Senses, mind and intellect in control, freedom as the goal, no desire, fear or anger. That person is already free.
verses.notes: Who is forever free? The sage who controls senses, mind and intellect, aims for liberation, and is free of desire, fear and anger. What is the key? Letting go of desire, fear and anger together.

verses.en: Knowing me as the one who enjoys all sacrifice and austerity, the great Lord of all worlds, and the friend of all beings, one reaches peace.
verses.hi: मुझे सब यज्ञों और तपों का भोक्ता, सब लोकों का महान ईश्वर और सब प्राणियों का मित्र जानकर व्यक्ति शांति पाता है।
verses.short: Know that I'm the friend of every being and the one behind all good effort. That's where peace comes from.
verses.notes: How does one find peace? By knowing the Divine as the enjoyer of all offerings, Lord of all worlds, and friend of all beings. Why 'friend of all beings'? It shows the Divine is near and caring, not distant.

verses.en: Krishna said: Whoever does the work that needs doing without depending on its results is a true renunciant and a true yogi, not someone who just stops lighting the sacred fire or stops acting.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: जो कर्म-फल पर निर्भर हुए बिना अपना कर्तव्य करता है, वही संन्यासी और योगी है, न कि वह जो केवल अग्नि जलाना या काम करना छोड़ दे।
verses.short: A real renunciate isn't someone who quits everything. It's someone who does their duty without chasing rewards.
verses.notes: Who is a true renunciate? The one who does their duty without wanting its fruits, not just someone who has stopped working. Why does Krishna redefine renunciation? To show it's an inner attitude, not an outer show.

verses.en: What people call renunciation, know that to be yoga, Arjuna. No one becomes a yogi without giving up selfish plans.
verses.hi: हे पांडव, जिसे संन्यास कहते हैं, उसी को योग जानो। स्वार्थी संकल्पों को छोड़े बिना कोई योगी नहीं बनता।
verses.short: Letting go and selfless work are the same thing. You can't do either while still chasing what you want.
verses.notes: Are renunciation and yoga the same? Yes. No one becomes a yogi without letting go of selfish intentions. What must be renounced? Selfish plans and desires, not life itself.

verses.en: For a sage who wants to climb to yoga, action is the means. For one who has reached yoga, calmness is the means.
verses.hi: योग में चढ़ना चाहने वाले मुनि के लिए कर्म साधन है। योग पर पहुँच चुके व्यक्ति के लिए शांति ही साधन है।
verses.short: When you're starting out, action is the way. Once you've leveled up, calm is the way.
verses.notes: What helps a beginner in yoga? Action. Selfless work prepares the mind. What helps one who has advanced? Calm and stillness become the means.

verses.en: When someone no longer clings to sense objects or to actions, and has let go of all selfish plans, they are said to have reached yoga.
verses.hi: जब कोई न इंद्रियों के विषयों में आसक्त होता है, न कर्मों में, और सारे संकल्प छोड़ देता है, तब उसे योग पर पहुँचा हुआ कहते हैं।
verses.short: When you stop clinging to sense pleasures and to your actions, you've reached the top of yoga.
verses.notes: When is someone established in yoga? When they're no longer attached to sense objects or actions, and have let go of selfish intentions. Is this a sudden change? Usually gradual, built through practice.

verses.en: Lift yourself up by your own effort; don't drag yourself down. You are your own best friend, and you are your own worst enemy.
verses.hi: अपने आप को खुद ऊपर उठाओ, खुद को नीचे मत गिराओ। तुम खुद ही अपने मित्र हो, और खुद ही अपने दुश्मन।
verses.short: You can be your own best friend or your own worst enemy. Lift yourself up. Don't drag yourself down.
verses.notes: Who is responsible for lifting us up? We are. We must raise ourselves by our own effort. How can the mind be our friend and enemy? A trained mind helps us; an untrained one harms us.

verses.en: For someone who has mastered their own mind, the self is a friend. For someone who hasn't, the self acts like an enemy.
verses.hi: जिसने अपने मन को जीत लिया है, उसके लिए वह मित्र है। जिसने नहीं जीता, उसके लिए वही दुश्मन जैसा बर्ताव करता है।
verses.short: Master your mind and it becomes your best friend. Leave it untamed and it acts like your enemy.
verses.notes: When is the mind a friend? When you've mastered it. When is it an enemy? When it's uncontrolled, it works against you like a foe.

verses.en: For someone who has conquered themselves and is at peace, the higher self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and insult.
verses.hi: जिसने खुद को जीत लिया है और शांत है, उसका परमात्मा सर्दी-गर्मी, सुख-दुख और मान-अपमान में स्थिर रहता है।
verses.short: With a calm, controlled mind you stay steady through heat or cold, praise or insults.
verses.notes: What happens when the mind is mastered? You stay calm in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honour and insult. Why mention honour and insult? Because ego reacts strongly to these, and calm in them is a real sign of growth.

verses.en: A yogi satisfied with knowledge and wisdom, unshakeable, master of the senses, who sees a lump of earth, a stone and gold as the same, is called steady in yoga.
verses.hi: जो योगी ज्ञान और विज्ञान से तृप्त है, अडिग है, इंद्रियों को जीत चुका है, और मिट्टी, पत्थर और सोने को एक जैसा देखता है, वह योग में स्थित कहलाता है।
verses.short: To someone truly at peace, dirt, stone and gold are all the same. Status doesn't move them.
verses.notes: Who is a steady yogi? One content with knowledge and experience, unshaken, senses controlled. What does 'gold and clod alike' mean? Seeing a lump of earth, a stone and gold as equal, so greed has no grip.

verses.en: Someone who sees well-wishers, friends, enemies, neutral people, mediators, the hateful, relatives, the good and the wicked all with an equal mind stands out.
verses.hi: जो शुभचिंतक, मित्र, शत्रु, उदासीन, मध्यस्थ, द्वेषी, रिश्तेदार, सज्जन और पापी, सबको एक समान बुद्धि से देखता है, वह श्रेष्ठ है।
verses.short: Friends, haters, family, strangers, good people and bad: treat them all with the same fairness. That's next level.
verses.notes: How does a great yogi treat people? Equally, whether friend, enemy, neutral, relative, saint or sinner. Is this realistic? It's a high goal. Each step toward it makes life calmer.

verses.en: A yogi should keep practising, staying alone in a quiet place, with mind and body controlled, free from expectations and possessiveness.
verses.hi: योगी को एकांत में अकेले रहकर, मन और शरीर को वश में रखकर, आशा और संग्रह से मुक्त होकर लगातार अभ्यास करना चाहिए।
verses.short: Find some alone time daily. Quiet your thoughts, drop your wants, and just focus.
verses.notes: How should a yogi practise? Alone in a quiet place, with mind controlled, free from craving and possessiveness. Why alone? Solitude reduces distractions and helps the mind settle.

verses.en: In a clean place, set up a firm seat, neither too high nor too low, covered with kusha grass, a deerskin and a cloth.
verses.hi: साफ़ जगह पर अपना स्थिर आसन लगाओ, जो न बहुत ऊँचा हो न बहुत नीचा, और उस पर कुश, मृगछाला और कपड़ा बिछा हो।
verses.short: Set up a clean, comfortable spot, not too high or too low. Your meditation space matters.
verses.notes: What kind of seat is recommended? A clean, firm seat, neither too high nor too low. Why such detail about the seat? A stable, comfortable posture supports a steady mind.

verses.en: Sitting there, focusing the mind on one point and controlling thoughts and senses, practise yoga to purify yourself.
verses.hi: उस आसन पर बैठकर, मन को एकाग्र करके और विचारों व इंद्रियों को वश में रखकर, खुद को शुद्ध करने के लिए योग का अभ्यास करो।
verses.short: Sit there, focus your mind, control your senses, and practise to clear your inner self.
verses.notes: What should one do on the seat? Focus the mind, control thoughts and senses, and practise yoga. What is the purpose? Purifying the self.

verses.en: Hold the body, head and neck straight and still. Stay steady, gaze at the tip of the nose, and don't look around.
verses.hi: शरीर, सिर और गर्दन को सीधा और स्थिर रखो। अडिग रहकर नाक के आगे के हिस्से पर नज़र टिकाओ और इधर-उधर मत देखो।
verses.short: Back, neck and head straight. Stay still. Soft focus on the tip of your nose. No looking around.
verses.notes: How should the body be held? Spine, head and neck straight and still. Why gaze at the tip of the nose? To keep the eyes from wandering, so the mind stays inward.

verses.en: Calm and fearless, keeping the vow of self-restraint, controlling the mind, sit focused with your thoughts on me and me as your goal.
verses.hi: शांत और निडर होकर, ब्रह्मचर्य के व्रत में रहकर, मन को वश में करके, मुझमें चित्त लगाकर और मुझे ही लक्ष्य मानकर बैठो।
verses.short: Stay calm and fearless, keep your discipline, and focus your mind on the Divine.
verses.notes: What inner attitude is needed? Calm, fearless, disciplined, with the mind fixed on the Divine. Why fearlessness? A fearful mind can't settle into meditation.

verses.en: Practising like this, always keeping the mind controlled, the yogi reaches the peace that rests in me, the highest freedom.
verses.hi: इस तरह लगातार अभ्यास करते हुए, मन को वश में रखने वाला योगी मुझमें स्थित परम निर्वाण रूपी शांति पाता है।
verses.short: Practise like this regularly and you'll reach a peace that's the highest kind there is.
verses.notes: What does steady meditation lead to? The supreme peace that rests in the Divine. Is this peace temporary? No. It's the deepest and most lasting peace.

verses.en: Arjuna, yoga isn't for someone who eats too much or too little, or who sleeps too much or too little.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, योग न बहुत ज़्यादा खाने वाले के लिए है, न बिल्कुल न खाने वाले के लिए, न बहुत सोने वाले के लिए, न बहुत जागने वाले के लिए।
verses.short: Overeating or starving, oversleeping or pulling all-nighters: none of it works. Balance is the key.
verses.notes: Who can't succeed in yoga? Those who eat too much or too little, or sleep too much or too little. What is the lesson? Balance. Extremes disturb the mind.

verses.en: For someone balanced in eating and recreation, balanced in effort at work, and balanced in sleep and waking, yoga ends all sorrow.
verses.hi: जो खाने-पीने और घूमने-फिरने में संतुलित है, काम में संतुलित मेहनत करता है, और सोने-जागने में संतुलित है, उसके लिए योग सारे दुख मिटा देता है।
verses.short: Balanced food, fun, work and sleep. That's how yoga actually ends your stress.
verses.notes: Who does yoga free from sorrow? Those moderate in eating, recreation, work, sleep and waking. How can I apply this? Build a balanced routine; it's the foundation of a calm mind.

verses.en: When the disciplined mind rests in the self alone, free from craving for any desire, that person is called steady in yoga.
verses.hi: जब वश में किया हुआ मन केवल आत्मा में टिक जाता है और सारी इच्छाओं की लालसा से मुक्त हो जाता है, तब व्यक्ति योग में स्थित कहलाता है।
verses.short: When your mind rests in your true self and stops craving stuff, you're ready for real yoga.
verses.notes: When is one established in yoga? When the disciplined mind rests in the Self, free of all craving. What is the sign? No longer chasing desires.

verses.en: "Like a lamp in a windless place that doesn't flicker": this is the image used for a yogi with a controlled mind, practising union with the self.
verses.hi: "जैसे हवा रहित जगह में रखा दीया नहीं डोलता", यही उपमा उस योगी के लिए दी जाती है जिसका मन वश में है और जो आत्मा में योग का अभ्यास करता है।
verses.short: Like a candle flame that doesn't flicker in a room with no wind. That's a focused mind.
verses.notes: What does the lamp example mean? A lamp in a windless place doesn't flicker. A yogi's controlled mind is that steady. What is the 'wind' in our lives? Distractions, desires and worries that shake the mind.

verses.en: When the mind, stilled by the practice of yoga, comes to rest, and seeing the self through the self, one is content in the self,
verses.hi: जब योग के अभ्यास से रुका हुआ मन शांत हो जाता है, और व्यक्ति खुद से खुद को देखकर अपने भीतर ही संतुष्ट रहता है,
verses.short: When practice settles the mind, you see your true self and feel joy just from that.
verses.notes: What happens when the mind becomes still? You see the Self through the Self and find joy in it. Where does this joy come from? From within, not from anything outside.

verses.en: when one knows that endless joy which the intellect can grasp but the senses cannot, and once settled there never moves from the truth,
verses.hi: जब वह उस अनंत सुख को जानता है जिसे बुद्धि पकड़ सकती है पर इंद्रियाँ नहीं, और उसमें टिककर फिर सत्य से नहीं हिलता,
verses.short: There's a happiness beyond the senses that only a clear mind can feel. Once you find it, you don't slip.
verses.notes: What kind of happiness is this? Infinite happiness, grasped by a clear understanding, beyond the senses. What happens once it's known? One never moves away from the truth.

verses.en: having gained which one thinks no gain is greater, and settled in which one is not shaken even by great sorrow,
verses.hi: जिसे पाकर वह किसी और लाभ को उससे बड़ा नहीं मानता, और जिसमें टिककर बड़े से बड़ा दुख भी उसे नहीं हिला पाता,
verses.short: Once you've got it, nothing else compares. Even the hardest pain can't shake you.
verses.notes: Why is no other gain greater? Once found, everything else looks small in comparison. What happens even in great sorrow? The person established in it isn't shaken.

verses.en: know that this freedom from contact with sorrow is called yoga. It should be practised with determination and an undiscouraged mind.
verses.hi: दुख के संपर्क से इस छुटकारे को ही योग जानो। इस योग का अभ्यास पक्के निश्चय और बिना निराश हुए मन से करना चाहिए।
verses.short: Yoga is literally disconnecting from suffering. Practise it with determination. Don't give up.
verses.notes: How does Krishna define yoga here? As freedom from union with sorrow. How should yoga be practised? With determination and without losing heart.

verses.en: Giving up completely all desires born of selfish wishes, and reining in the senses from every side with the mind,
verses.hi: संकल्प से पैदा होने वाली सारी इच्छाओं को पूरी तरह छोड़कर, और मन से इंद्रियों के समूह को हर तरफ़ से रोककर,
verses.short: Drop the wants your mind keeps cooking up, and pull your senses back from every direction.
verses.notes: What should one give up first? All desires born from mental plans. How are the senses handled? The mind gently draws them back from every direction.

verses.en: one should little by little become still, with the intellect held firm. Fixing the mind on the self, think of nothing else.
verses.hi: धैर्य से पकड़ी हुई बुद्धि के साथ धीरे-धीरे शांत होना चाहिए। मन को आत्मा में टिकाकर कुछ और नहीं सोचना चाहिए।
verses.short: Slowly, step by step, steady your mind with willpower and focus only on your true self.
verses.notes: How fast should one progress? Little by little, with patience. What should the mind rest on? The Self, thinking of nothing else.

verses.en: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders off, bring it back from there and place it under the control of the self.
verses.hi: चंचल और अस्थिर मन जहाँ-जहाँ भटके, वहाँ-वहाँ से उसे रोककर आत्मा के ही वश में लाना चाहिए।
verses.short: Mind wandering again? Totally normal. Gently bring it back, every single time. That's the whole practice.
verses.notes: What if the mind wanders? Wherever it goes, gently bring it back to the Self. Is wandering a failure? No. Bringing it back each time is the practice itself.

verses.en: Supreme joy comes to the yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passions are calmed, who is free from wrong and has become one with the Supreme.
verses.hi: जिस योगी का मन शांत है, जिसका रजोगुण शांत हो गया है, जो पाप से मुक्त है और ब्रह्म में लीन है, उसे परम सुख मिलता है।
verses.short: Calm mind, no restlessness, no guilt. That yogi finds the highest happiness.
verses.notes: Who receives supreme happiness? The yogi whose mind is peaceful, passions calmed, and free from faults. What does 'becoming one with Brahman' mean? Realising your oneness with the Supreme.

verses.en: Practising like this always, free from wrong, the yogi easily enjoys the endless joy of contact with the Supreme.
verses.hi: इस तरह लगातार अभ्यास करता हुआ पापरहित योगी आसानी से ब्रह्म के संपर्क का अनंत सुख भोगता है।
verses.short: Keep practising and stay clean inside, and supreme joy comes easily.
