verses.notes: What does constant practice bring? The bliss of contact with the Supreme, easily. Why 'easily'? After the mind is purified, joy flows naturally.

verses.en: Someone united in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self. They see the same everywhere.
verses.hi: योग से जुड़ा व्यक्ति सब प्राणियों में अपनी आत्मा को और सब प्राणियों को अपनी आत्मा में देखता है। वह हर जगह एक समान देखता है।
verses.short: With a focused mind you see yourself in everyone and everyone in yourself. We're all connected.
verses.notes: How does the yogi see the world? They see the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self. How does this change behaviour? Harming others becomes like harming yourself.

verses.en: Whoever sees me everywhere and sees everything in me, I am never lost to them, and they are never lost to me.
verses.hi: जो मुझे हर जगह देखता है और सबको मुझमें देखता है, मैं उससे कभी दूर नहीं होता और वह मुझसे कभी दूर नहीं होता।
verses.short: See me in everyone and everyone in me, and we'll never lose each other.
verses.notes: What does Krishna promise here? One who sees him everywhere is never lost to him, and he is never lost to them. What does this relationship feel like? Constant closeness, like never being alone.

verses.en: A yogi who, rooted in oneness, worships me as present in all beings lives in me, however they may be living.
verses.hi: जो योगी एकता में स्थित होकर सब प्राणियों में बसे मुझे भजता है, वह किसी भी तरह रहते हुए मुझमें ही रहता है।
verses.short: Love the Divine in every being, and however you live, you stay connected to me.
verses.notes: Can someone living a normal life be a yogi? Yes. One who sees the Divine in all beings lives in him, however they live. What matters most? The vision of oneness, not outer circumstances.

verses.en: Arjuna, a yogi who sees the pleasure or pain of all beings as their own is considered the highest.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, जो योगी सब प्राणियों के सुख-दुख को अपने जैसा ही देखता है, वह सबसे श्रेष्ठ माना जाता है।
verses.short: Feel others' pain and joy as your own. That empathy is the highest kind of yoga.
verses.notes: Who is the highest yogi? The one who feels others' joy and pain as their own. Is this empathy? Yes, empathy rooted in seeing one Self in all.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, this yoga of evenness that you have described, I can't see it lasting, because the mind is so restless.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे मधुसूदन, आपने समता का जो योग बताया, मन की चंचलता के कारण मुझे इसकी स्थिरता नहीं दिखती।
verses.short: Arjuna: "This sounds great, but my mind is all over the place. How do I keep it steady?"
verses.notes: What is Arjuna's doubt? He can't see how this yoga of even-mindedness can last, because the mind is so restless. Why is this question so relatable? Everyone who has tried to meditate knows the restless mind.

verses.en: The mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. Controlling it seems as hard as controlling the wind.
verses.hi: हे कृष्ण, मन बड़ा चंचल, बेचैन करने वाला, ताकतवर और ज़िद्दी है। इसे वश में करना मुझे हवा को रोकने जितना कठिन लगता है।
verses.short: "The mind is restless, stubborn and strong. Controlling it feels like trying to control the wind." So relatable.
verses.notes: How does Arjuna describe the mind? Restless, turbulent, strong and stubborn, as hard to control as the wind. Is Arjuna exaggerating? No, and Krishna agrees with him.

verses.en: Krishna said: No doubt, mighty Arjuna, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it can be trained by practice and detachment.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे महाबाहु, इसमें कोई शक नहीं कि मन चंचल है और मुश्किल से वश में होता है। पर हे कौन्तेय, अभ्यास और वैराग्य से इसे काबू किया जा सकता है।
verses.short: Krishna: "True, it's tough. But with practice and letting go, you can train it."
verses.notes: How can the mind be controlled? Through practice (abhyasa) and detachment (vairagya). What do these mean? Practice is returning again and again; detachment is loosening the pull of desire.

verses.en: In my view, yoga is hard to reach for someone without self-control. But someone who is self-controlled and keeps trying can reach it by the right means.
verses.hi: मेरे विचार से जिसका मन वश में नहीं, उसके लिए योग पाना कठिन है। पर जो मन को वश में करके कोशिश करता रहता है, वह सही तरीके से इसे पा सकता है।
verses.short: Without self-control yoga's hard. But with effort and the right method, anyone can do it.
verses.notes: Who can achieve yoga? Not someone with an uncontrolled mind, but someone who strives with the right means. What's the hopeful part? It can be done with effort and the right method.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, what happens to someone who has faith but doesn't try hard enough, whose mind slips away from yoga before reaching its goal?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे कृष्ण, जो श्रद्धा तो रखता है पर पूरी कोशिश नहीं करता, और जिसका मन योग से भटक जाता है, वह योग की सिद्धि न पाकर किस गति को जाता है?
verses.short: Arjuna: "What if someone tries with faith but slips up and doesn't make it? What happens to them?"
verses.notes: What is Arjuna worried about? What happens to someone with faith who tries but doesn't reach the goal? Why is this a common fear? Many worry their effort will be wasted if they fall short.

verses.en: Mighty Krishna, having lost both worlds, without support and confused on the path to the Supreme, doesn't such a person vanish like a broken cloud?
verses.hi: हे महाबाहु, क्या वह दोनों तरफ़ से भटककर, बिना सहारे के और ब्रह्म के मार्ग में उलझकर, फटे हुए बादल की तरह नष्ट नहीं हो जाता?
verses.short: "Do they lose both worlds and just vanish, like a cloud torn apart?" The fear of failing halfway.
verses.notes: What image does Arjuna use? A broken cloud, torn apart and vanishing. What does he fear exactly? Losing both worldly success and spiritual progress.

verses.en: Krishna, please clear this doubt of mine completely. No one but you can remove it.
verses.hi: हे कृष्ण, मेरा यह संदेह पूरी तरह दूर कीजिए। आपके सिवा इस संदेह को मिटाने वाला कोई और नहीं है।
verses.short: "Krishna, only you can clear this doubt. Please answer."
verses.notes: Why does Arjuna ask only Krishna? He trusts that no one else can clear this doubt completely. What does this show about their bond? Deep trust in his teacher.

verses.en: Krishna said: Arjuna, there is no ruin for such a person, neither in this world nor the next. My friend, no one who does good ever comes to a bad end.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे पार्थ, ऐसे व्यक्ति का न इस लोक में नाश होता है, न परलोक में। हे प्रिय, भलाई करने वाला कभी बुरी गति को नहीं जाता।
verses.short: Krishna: "Nobody who tries to do good ever ends up lost. Not here, not after." Effort is never wasted.
verses.notes: Is the effort of a failed seeker wasted? Never, in this world or the next. No one who does good comes to a bad end. Why is this verse comforting? Every sincere step counts, even if you stumble.

verses.en: One who falls from yoga reaches the worlds of the virtuous, lives there for many years, and is then born into a pure and prosperous family.
verses.hi: योग से भटका व्यक्ति पुण्य करने वालों के लोकों में जाकर बहुत सालों तक रहता है, फिर पवित्र और समृद्ध लोगों के घर जन्म लेता है।
verses.short: They're reborn into a good, comfortable family to keep going. The universe saves your progress.
verses.notes: Where is such a seeker reborn? After enjoying good worlds, in a pure and prosperous family. What does this give them? Good conditions to continue their journey.

verses.en: Or they are born into a family of wise yogis. A birth like that is very rare in this world.
verses.hi: या फिर वह बुद्धिमान योगियों के कुल में ही जन्म लेता है। ऐसा जन्म इस दुनिया में बहुत दुर्लभ है।
verses.short: Or they're born into a family of wise people. That's a rare blessing.
verses.notes: What is the other possibility? Being born in a family of wise yogis. Why is this rare? Such a supportive environment for spiritual growth is hard to find.

verses.en: There they regain the understanding from their previous life, and from there they strive even harder for perfection, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे कुरुनंदन, वहाँ उसे पिछले जन्म की समझ फिर मिल जाती है, और वह सिद्धि के लिए और ज़्यादा मेहनत करता है।
verses.short: They pick up the wisdom from their past life and push even harder. Like loading a saved game.
verses.notes: What carries over to the next life? The understanding gained in the previous life. What happens then? They strive even harder toward perfection.

verses.en: Their past practice carries them along almost by itself. Even someone who merely wants to know about yoga goes beyond ritual religion.
verses.hi: पिछले अभ्यास के कारण वह अपने आप ही उस ओर खिंचा चला जाता है। योग को जानने की इच्छा रखने वाला भी वेदों के कर्मकांड से आगे निकल जाता है।
verses.short: Past practice pulls them forward almost automatically. Even curiosity about yoga lifts you higher.
verses.notes: How does past practice help? It pulls you forward almost automatically, even without trying. Why does this matter? Good habits built now keep helping you later.

verses.en: A yogi who strives hard, cleansed of all wrongs and perfected over many lives, then reaches the highest goal.
verses.hi: मेहनत से कोशिश करने वाला योगी, जिसके सारे पाप धुल गए हैं और जो कई जन्मों में सिद्ध हुआ है, फिर परम गति पाता है।
verses.short: Keep striving sincerely, life after life, and you'll reach the highest goal.
verses.notes: How does the yogi finally reach the goal? By sincere effort over many lives, purified of all faults. What does this teach about patience? Real growth can take a long time, and that's okay.

verses.en: The yogi is greater than those who practise austerity, greater than scholars, and greater than those who do ritual work. So be a yogi, Arjuna.
verses.hi: योगी तपस्वियों से श्रेष्ठ है, ज्ञानियों से भी श्रेष्ठ माना जाता है, और कर्मकांड करने वालों से भी श्रेष्ठ है। इसलिए हे अर्जुन, योगी बनो।
verses.short: A yogi beats someone who only does tough discipline, only studies, or only does rituals. So be a yogi.
verses.notes: Why is the yogi greater than others? Greater than ascetics, scholars and ritualists, because the yogi seeks union with the Divine itself. What does Krishna urge? 'Therefore, Arjuna, be a yogi.'

verses.en: And of all yogis, the one who worships me with faith, with their inner self absorbed in me, I consider the most united with me.
verses.hi: और सब योगियों में भी जो श्रद्धा से, अपने अंतर्मन को मुझमें लगाकर मुझे भजता है, उसे मैं सबसे श्रेष्ठ योगी मानता हूँ।
verses.short: And of all yogis, the one who loves me with full faith and heart is the closest to me.
verses.notes: Who is the best of all yogis? The one who worships Krishna with faith, with their inner self absorbed in him. Why does this point to devotion? It sets the stage for the next chapters on love and devotion.

verses.en: Krishna said: Arjuna, hear how, with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and relying on me, you will know me fully and without doubt.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे पार्थ, सुनो कि मुझमें मन लगाकर, मेरी शरण में योग का अभ्यास करते हुए, तुम मुझे पूरी तरह और बिना संदेह के कैसे जानोगे।
verses.short: Krishna: "Keep your mind on me and practise, and I'll show you how to know me completely."
verses.notes: What will Krishna teach in this chapter? How to know him completely, with the mind fixed on him and relying on him. What does 'without doubt' mean here? Knowledge so clear that no confusion remains.

verses.en: I will explain to you this knowledge along with its realisation, completely. Once you know it, nothing more remains to be known here.
verses.hi: मैं तुम्हें यह ज्ञान, विज्ञान सहित, पूरी तरह बताऊँगा। इसे जानकर यहाँ और कुछ जानना बाकी नहीं रहता।
verses.short: "I'll give you the full knowledge and the lived experience. After this, there's nothing left to figure out."
verses.notes: What two kinds of knowledge does Krishna offer? Knowledge (jnana) and its realisation (vijnana), understanding plus direct experience. Why is nothing else left to know? Knowing the source of everything covers everything.

verses.en: Among thousands of people, hardly one strives for perfection. And among those who strive and succeed, hardly one knows me as I truly am.
verses.hi: हज़ारों लोगों में कोई एक सिद्धि के लिए कोशिश करता है। और कोशिश करने वाले सिद्धों में भी कोई एक मुझे सच में जानता है।
verses.short: Out of thousands, a few try. Out of those trying, very few truly get it. Rare, but possible.
verses.notes: How rare is it to truly know the Divine? Among thousands, a few strive; among those, hardly one truly knows him. Should this discourage us? No. It shows how precious the effort is.

verses.en: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and ego: these are the eight parts of my material nature.
verses.hi: धरती, पानी, आग, हवा, आकाश, मन, बुद्धि और अहंकार, ये मेरी प्रकृति के आठ हिस्से हैं।
verses.short: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, ego: these eight make up my material side.
verses.notes: What are the eight parts of Krishna's lower nature? Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and ego. Why include mind and ego in 'nature'? They are also part of the changing material world, not the true Self.

verses.en: This is my lower nature. But know my higher nature too, mighty Arjuna: the life force that holds up this whole world.
verses.hi: यह मेरी निचली प्रकृति है। पर हे महाबाहु, इससे अलग मेरी ऊँची प्रकृति को भी जानो, वह जीव रूपी शक्ति जो इस पूरे जगत को थामे हुए है।
verses.short: That's my lower nature. My higher nature is the life force that keeps the whole universe running.
verses.notes: What is Krishna's higher nature? The life-principle, the conscious souls that sustain the universe. How is it different from the lower? The lower is matter; the higher is consciousness.

verses.en: Understand that all beings come from these two natures. I am the origin of the whole universe and also its dissolution.
verses.hi: समझ लो कि सारे प्राणी इन्हीं दो प्रकृतियों से पैदा होते हैं। मैं ही पूरे जगत की उत्पत्ति हूँ और मैं ही उसका अंत।
verses.short: Matter plus life force creates everything. And I'm the source and the end of it all.
verses.notes: Where do all beings come from? From these two natures, matter and consciousness. What role does Krishna claim? He is both the origin and the end of the whole universe.

verses.en: Arjuna, there is nothing higher than me. Everything is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
verses.hi: हे धनंजय, मुझसे ऊपर कुछ भी नहीं है। यह सब कुछ मुझमें ऐसे पिरोया है जैसे धागे में मोती।
verses.short: Nothing is higher than me. Everything is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
verses.notes: What does the thread and pearls image mean? Everything is strung on Krishna like pearls on a thread. He holds it all together, unseen. Is there anything higher than him? Krishna says nothing is higher.

verses.en: Arjuna, I am the taste in water, the light in the moon and sun, the sacred syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space and the strength in people.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, मैं पानी में स्वाद हूँ, चाँद और सूरज में रोशनी हूँ, सब वेदों में ओंकार हूँ, आकाश में शब्द हूँ और इंसानों में पुरुषार्थ हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the taste of water, the light of the sun and moon, the Om in prayers. Look closely and you'll see me everywhere.
verses.notes: Where can we see Krishna in daily life? In the taste of water, the light of sun and moon, Om in the scriptures, sound in space and strength in people. Why such ordinary examples? To show the Divine is present in simple, everyday things.

verses.en: I am the pure fragrance of the earth and the brightness in fire. I am the life in all beings and the discipline in those who practise austerity.
verses.hi: मैं धरती में पवित्र गंध हूँ और आग में तेज हूँ। मैं सब प्राणियों में जीवन हूँ और तपस्वियों में तप हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the fresh smell of earth, the heat in fire, the life in every being, the discipline in the disciplined.
verses.notes: What more examples does Krishna give? The fragrance of earth, the brilliance of fire, the life in beings and the discipline of ascetics. What is the common thread? He is the essence that makes each thing what it is.

verses.en: Arjuna, I am the timeless seed from which every being grows. In the clever, I am their cleverness; in the radiant, I am their radiance.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, हर प्राणी जिस सनातन बीज से उगता है, वह मैं हूँ। समझदारों में उनकी समझ और तेजस्वियों में उनकी चमक मैं ही हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the original seed of all beings, the intelligence of the smart, and the shine of the brilliant.
verses.notes: What is the 'eternal seed'? Krishna is the original source from which all beings grow. Where else is he present? As the intelligence of the wise and the brilliance of the brilliant.

verses.en: I am the strength of the strong, free from craving and attachment. And I am the desire in beings that does not go against what is right, Arjuna.
verses.hi: मैं बलवानों का वह बल हूँ जो इच्छा और आसक्ति से मुक्त है। और हे भरतश्रेष्ठ, प्राणियों में धर्म के अनुकूल इच्छा भी मैं ही हूँ।
verses.short: I'm strength without greed, and desire that doesn't go against what's right. Healthy ambition is divine.
verses.notes: What kind of strength is divine? Strength free from selfish desire and attachment. Is desire always bad? No. Desire that's in line with dharma is a form of the Divine.

verses.en: Know that all states of goodness, passion and dullness come from me alone. But I am not in them; they are in me.
verses.hi: सत्त्व, रज और तम के जो भी भाव हैं, उन्हें मुझसे ही पैदा हुआ जानो। पर मैं उनमें नहीं हूँ, वे मुझमें हैं।
verses.short: Every mood, calm, restless or lazy, comes from me. But I'm not trapped in them; they're in me.
verses.notes: Where do the three gunas come from? From Krishna, but he isn't in them; they are in him. What does that difference mean? He is their source but not controlled by them.

verses.en: Confused by these three qualities, the whole world fails to recognise me, who am beyond them and unchanging.
verses.hi: इन तीन गुणों के भावों से भ्रमित यह पूरा जगत मुझे नहीं पहचानता, जो इनसे परे और अविनाशी हूँ।
verses.short: People get so caught up in their moods that they miss what's beyond them: me.
verses.notes: Why doesn't the world recognise the Divine? It is deluded by the three gunas and can't see what lies beyond them. What is beyond the gunas? The unchanging Divine.

verses.en: This divine illusion of mine, made of the three qualities, is hard to get past. But those who surrender to me cross over it.
verses.hi: तीन गुणों वाली मेरी यह दिव्य माया पार करना कठिन है। पर जो मेरी शरण में आते हैं, वे इस माया को पार कर जाते हैं।
verses.short: This illusion is hard to escape. But those who turn to me get through it.
verses.notes: Why is Maya hard to cross? It is divine and made of the three gunas, so it is very powerful. Who crosses it? Those who take refuge in Krishna alone.

verses.en: Wrongdoers, the deluded and the lowest of people don't turn to me. Their understanding is stolen by illusion and they take on a demonic nature.
verses.hi: बुरे कर्म करने वाले, मूर्ख और नीच लोग मेरी शरण में नहीं आते। माया ने उनका ज्ञान छीन लिया है और वे आसुरी स्वभाव अपना लेते हैं।
verses.short: People who keep doing harm, lost in confusion and ego, don't turn to me. They're stuck.
verses.notes: Who doesn't turn to the Divine? Wrongdoers, the foolish, the lowest of people, and those whose wisdom is stolen by illusion. What blocks them? Delusion and a demonic nature.

verses.en: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the curious, those seeking wealth, and the wise.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, चार तरह के पुण्यात्मा लोग मुझे भजते हैं: दुखी, जिज्ञासु, धन चाहने वाले और ज्ञानी।
verses.short: Four kinds of good people turn to me: those in pain, the curious, those who need help, and the wise.
verses.notes: What four kinds of people turn to God? The distressed, the seekers of knowledge, the seekers of wealth, and the wise. Are all of them good? Yes. Krishna calls them all virtuous.

verses.en: Of these, the wise one, always united with me and devoted to me alone, stands out. I am very dear to the wise, and they are dear to me.
verses.hi: इनमें हमेशा मुझसे जुड़ा और केवल मेरा भक्त ज्ञानी श्रेष्ठ है। मैं ज्ञानी को बहुत प्रिय हूँ और वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.short: Of these, the wise one who loves me for my own sake is the best. We're very dear to each other.
verses.notes: Who is the best among these four? The wise one, always connected and devoted to the One. Why is the wise one dearest? Their love is pure, wanting nothing but the Divine.

verses.en: All of these are noble, but I consider the wise one to be my very self. Steady in mind, they have taken me as the highest goal.
verses.hi: ये सभी उदार हैं, पर ज्ञानी को मैं अपनी आत्मा ही मानता हूँ। स्थिर मन वाला वह मुझे ही सबसे ऊँची गति मानकर मुझमें टिका है।
verses.short: All of them are good, but the wise one feels like my own self. They want nothing but me.
verses.notes: How does Krishna see the wise devotee? As his very own Self. Does he look down on the other three? No. All are noble; the wise one is simply closest.

verses.en: After many births, the wise person surrenders to me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare.
verses.hi: बहुत से जन्मों के बाद ज्ञानी यह जानकर मेरी शरण में आता है कि सब कुछ वासुदेव ही है। ऐसा महात्मा बहुत दुर्लभ है।
verses.short: After many lives, the wise realise "the Divine is everything" and come to me. Such souls are rare.
verses.notes: What does the wise person realise after many births? That Vasudeva, the Divine, is everything. Why is such a person rare? Seeing the Divine in everything takes great maturity.

verses.en: Those whose understanding is carried off by various desires turn to other gods, following various rituals, led by their own nature.
verses.hi: जिनका ज्ञान तरह-तरह की इच्छाओं ने छीन लिया है, वे अपने स्वभाव से प्रेरित होकर तरह-तरह के नियम अपनाते हुए दूसरे देवताओं की शरण लेते हैं।
verses.short: People driven by wants turn to other gods for quick results, based on their own nature.
verses.notes: Why do people worship other gods? Driven by their nature and desires, they seek quick results through various rituals. Is Krishna criticising them? He is explaining, not condemning. Their desires guide their choices.

verses.en: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that faith of theirs firm.
verses.hi: जो भक्त जिस रूप की श्रद्धा से पूजा करना चाहता है, मैं उसकी उसी श्रद्धा को पक्का कर देता हूँ।
verses.short: Whatever form someone worships with faith, I make their faith stronger.
verses.notes: What does Krishna do for sincere worshippers of any form? He makes their faith steady. What does this show about Krishna? He supports all sincere faith.

verses.en: Filled with that faith, they worship that form and get what they wish for from it. But in truth, it is I who give those things.
verses.hi: उस श्रद्धा से भरकर वह उस रूप की पूजा करता है और उससे अपनी इच्छाएँ पूरी पाता है। पर असल में वे चीज़ें मैं ही देता हूँ।
verses.short: They pray with faith and get what they want, but really, it's me giving it.
verses.notes: Who really grants the results of worship? Krishna himself, even when another form is worshipped. What does this mean? All sincere prayers ultimately reach the same source.

verses.en: But the results gained by those of small understanding don't last. Worshippers of the gods go to the gods; my devotees come to me.
verses.hi: पर कम समझ वालों को मिलने वाला फल नाशवान होता है। देवताओं को पूजने वाले देवताओं के पास जाते हैं, और मेरे भक्त मेरे पास आते हैं।
verses.short: Those small rewards don't last. Aim for the gods and you reach them. Aim for me and you reach me.
verses.notes: Why are those results limited? They are sought for small, passing ends. Where do devotees of Krishna go? To him, the lasting goal.

verses.en: The unwise think that I, the unseen, have taken on a visible form. They don't know my higher nature, which is unchanging and supreme.
verses.hi: नासमझ लोग सोचते हैं कि मैं अदृश्य होकर भी बस एक रूप में प्रकट हुआ हूँ। वे मेरे अविनाशी और सर्वोच्च स्वरूप को नहीं जानते।
verses.short: People who don't get it think I'm just a person who showed up. They miss my unlimited side.
verses.notes: What mistake do the ignorant make? They think Krishna is only a person who was born, not the eternal unmanifest. What do they miss? His supreme, unchanging nature.

verses.en: I am not visible to everyone, being veiled by my own divine power. This confused world does not recognise me, the unborn and unchanging.
verses.hi: अपनी योगमाया से ढका होने के कारण मैं सबको दिखाई नहीं देता। यह भ्रमित दुनिया मुझ अजन्मे और अविनाशी को नहीं पहचानती।
verses.short: I'm hidden behind illusion, so not everyone sees me. The world doesn't recognise that I'm eternal.
verses.notes: Why isn't Krishna visible to all? He is veiled by his own Maya. Who fails to recognise him? The deluded world, which doesn't know him as unborn and unchanging.

verses.en: Arjuna, I know all beings of the past, the present and the future, but no one knows me.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, मैं भूतकाल, वर्तमान और भविष्य के सब प्राणियों को जानता हूँ, पर मुझे कोई नहीं जानता।
verses.short: I know everyone: past, present and future. But nobody truly knows me.
verses.notes: What does Krishna know? All beings, past, present and future. Why does no one know him? The limited mind can't fully grasp the unlimited.

verses.en: Arjuna, from birth all beings fall into confusion, caused by the pull of opposites that arise from liking and disliking.
verses.hi: हे भारत, इच्छा और द्वेष से पैदा होने वाले द्वंद्वों के मोह के कारण सब प्राणी जन्म से ही भ्रम में पड़ जाते हैं।
verses.short: From birth, everyone gets trapped in love-hate cycles. That's what confuses us.
verses.notes: Why are beings deluded from birth? Because of the pull of opposites, born from liking and disliking. What are the 'pairs of opposites'? Pleasure and pain, gain and loss, praise and blame.

verses.en: But people of good deeds, whose wrongs have come to an end, are freed from the confusion of opposites and worship me with firm resolve.
verses.hi: पर पुण्य कर्म करने वाले जिन लोगों के पाप खत्म हो गए हैं, वे द्वंद्वों के मोह से छूटकर पक्के निश्चय से मुझे भजते हैं।
verses.short: Those who keep doing good eventually break free of that cycle and commit to me fully.
verses.notes: Who is freed from this delusion? Those whose wrongs have ended through good deeds. What do they do then? Worship the Divine with firm resolve.

verses.en: Those who take refuge in me and strive for freedom from old age and death come to know the Supreme, the self, and all about action.
verses.hi: जो मेरी शरण लेकर बुढ़ापे और मृत्यु से छुटकारे के लिए कोशिश करते हैं, वे ब्रह्म को, आत्मा को और सारे कर्म को जान लेते हैं।
verses.short: Those who turn to me to get past ageing and death come to understand the whole truth.
verses.notes: Who truly knows Brahman? Those who take refuge in Krishna to be free from old age and death. What else do they understand? The Self and the whole of action.

verses.en: Those who know me as the basis of the material world, of the divine and of all sacrifice, keep their minds on me and know me even at the hour of death.
verses.hi: जो मुझे भौतिक जगत, देवताओं और यज्ञ के आधार के रूप में जानते हैं, वे मुझमें मन लगाए रखकर मृत्यु के समय भी मुझे जानते हैं।
verses.short: Those who know me in every part of life keep remembering me, even at the very end.
verses.notes: What do they know at the time of death? They know Krishna as the Lord of the material, the divine and all sacrifice, even at death. Why do these terms matter? They set up Arjuna's questions in the next chapter.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, what is the Supreme? What is the self? What is action? What is meant by the material realm, and what by the divine realm?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने पूछा: हे पुरुषोत्तम, ब्रह्म का अर्थ क्या है, अध्यात्म का अर्थ क्या है, और कर्म का? अधिभूत और अधिदैव से क्या मतलब है?
verses.short: Arjuna drops a list of deep questions: What's the ultimate reality? What's the self? What's karma?
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask? What is Brahman, what is the Self, what is action, what is the material plane and what is the divine plane? Why these questions? Krishna used these terms at the end of Chapter 7, and Arjuna wants them explained.

verses.en: Who is the lord of sacrifice here in this body, and how? And at the hour of death, how can the self-controlled know you?
verses.hi: हे मधुसूदन, इस शरीर में अधियज्ञ कौन है और कैसे है? और मृत्यु के समय संयमी लोग आपको कैसे जानते हैं?
verses.short: "And how can someone remember you at the moment of death?" The biggest question of all.
verses.notes: What else does Arjuna want to know? Who is the Lord of sacrifice in the body, and how is Krishna known at the time of death? Why ask about death? Because how we face death reflects how we lived.

verses.en: Krishna said: The Supreme is the imperishable highest. The self is one's own true nature. Action is the creative force that brings beings into existence.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: परम अविनाशी ही ब्रह्म है। अपना असली स्वभाव अध्यात्म कहलाता है। प्राणियों को पैदा करने वाली रचनात्मक शक्ति कर्म कहलाती है।
verses.short: Krishna: "The ultimate reality never changes. Your true nature is your self. Karma is the action that creates life."
verses.notes: How does Krishna define Brahman and the Self? Brahman is the imperishable Supreme; the Self is one's own inner nature. What is 'action' here? The creative force that brings beings into existence.

verses.en: The material realm is everything that perishes. The divine realm is the cosmic spirit. And I myself, here in the body, am the lord of sacrifice, best of embodied beings.
verses.hi: नाशवान चीज़ें अधिभूत हैं। विराट पुरुष अधिदैव है। और हे देहधारियों में श्रेष्ठ, इस शरीर में अधियज्ञ मैं ही हूँ।
verses.short: "The physical world keeps changing. The cosmic spirit runs it. And I live inside every body."
verses.notes: What are the material and divine planes? The material is the perishable world; the divine is the cosmic Person. Who is the Lord of sacrifice in the body? Krishna himself, dwelling within.

verses.en: Whoever leaves the body at the end remembering me alone reaches my state of being. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hi: जो अंत समय में मुझे ही याद करते हुए शरीर छोड़ता है, वह मेरे स्वरूप को पाता है। इसमें कोई संदेह नहीं।
verses.short: Whoever thinks of me at their last moment comes straight to me. No doubt about it.
verses.notes: What happens to one who remembers Krishna at death? They reach him. There is no doubt. Is it enough to remember only at the end? The next verses explain that what we remember at the end depends on how we lived.

verses.en: Whatever a person remembers when leaving the body at the end, Arjuna, they go to that very state, having always been absorbed in it.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, अंत में शरीर छोड़ते समय इंसान जिस भाव को याद करता है, वह उसी को पाता है, क्योंकि वह हमेशा उसी भाव में डूबा रहा होता है।
verses.short: Whatever you think about most in life is what you'll think of at the end. And that's where you'll go.
verses.notes: Why does the last thought matter? Whatever you think of at the end, you go to that state. What shapes that last thought? Whatever you've been absorbed in all your life.

verses.en: So remember me at all times, and fight. With your mind and intellect offered to me, you will surely come to me.
verses.hi: इसलिए हर समय मुझे याद करो और युद्ध करो। मन और बुद्धि मुझे अर्पित करके तुम निश्चय ही मुझे पाओगे।
verses.short: So remember me all the time, and keep doing your work. Mind and heart on me, you'll reach me.
verses.notes: What is Krishna's advice? Remember him at all times, and keep doing your duty. How can we remember God while busy? Offer your mind and work to him; remembrance becomes part of the work.

verses.en: With a mind trained by practice that doesn't wander elsewhere, constantly thinking of the supreme divine being, one reaches it, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, अभ्यास से साधे हुए और कहीं और न भटकने वाले मन से लगातार परम दिव्य पुरुष का चिंतन करने वाला उसी को पाता है।
verses.short: Practise focusing, don't let your mind drift, and you'll reach the supreme.
verses.notes: How does one reach the Supreme? By a mind steady through practice that doesn't wander to anything else. What is the role of practice? It trains the mind to return to the Divine naturally.

verses.en: One should meditate on the all-knowing, the ancient, the ruler, subtler than the subtlest, the support of all, beyond thought, bright as the sun and beyond darkness.
verses.hi: उस सर्वज्ञ, पुरातन, सबके शासक, सूक्ष्म से भी सूक्ष्म, सबके आधार, सोच से परे, सूरज जैसे तेजस्वी और अंधकार से परे परमात्मा का ध्यान करना चाहिए।
verses.short: Meditate on the one who knows all, is ancient, subtle, shines like the sun and is beyond darkness.
verses.notes: How is the Supreme described? All-knowing, ancient, the ruler, subtler than the subtlest, support of all, brilliant like the sun, beyond darkness. Why so many descriptions? They help the mind hold a vast reality in meditation.

verses.en: At the time of death, with a steady mind, full of devotion and the power of yoga, drawing the life breath fully between the eyebrows, one reaches that supreme divine being.
verses.hi: मृत्यु के समय स्थिर मन से, भक्ति और योग-बल से भरकर, प्राण को भौंहों के बीच ठीक से टिकाकर, व्यक्ति उस परम दिव्य पुरुष को पाता है।
verses.short: At the end, with a steady mind full of love and focus, you reach that supreme being.
verses.notes: What does the yogi do at the time of death? Fixes the life-breath between the eyebrows with a steady mind and devotion. What do they reach? The supreme, divine Person.

verses.en: I will briefly tell you about that goal which knowers of the Vedas call imperishable, which seekers free from attachment enter, and for which people live a life of self-restraint.
verses.hi: जिसे वेद जानने वाले अविनाशी कहते हैं, आसक्ति छोड़ चुके साधक जिसमें प्रवेश करते हैं, और जिसके लिए लोग ब्रह्मचर्य का पालन करते हैं, उस पद के बारे में मैं तुम्हें संक्षेप में बताता हूँ।
verses.short: Here's a quick summary of the ultimate goal that wise people work so hard to reach.
verses.notes: What is the 'imperishable goal'? What the wise call the Imperishable, entered by those free from attachment. Why do people practise discipline? To reach this goal.

verses.en: Closing all the gates of the senses, holding the mind in the heart, drawing the life breath up to the head and steady in yogic focus,
verses.hi: इंद्रियों के सब दरवाज़े बंद करके, मन को हृदय में रोककर, प्राण को सिर में चढ़ाकर और योग की धारणा में टिककर,
verses.short: Close off distractions, centre your mind in your heart, and stay steady in meditation.
verses.notes: What practice is described? Closing the senses, holding the mind in the heart and the breath in the head. Is this for everyone? It's an advanced practice; the inner discipline behind it is what matters most.

verses.en: chanting the one syllable Om, which is the Supreme, and remembering me, whoever departs leaving the body reaches the highest goal.
verses.hi: ब्रह्म रूपी एक अक्षर ओम का उच्चारण करते हुए और मुझे याद करते हुए जो शरीर छोड़ता है, वह परम गति पाता है।
verses.short: Chant Om and think of me as you leave your body, and you reach the highest goal.
verses.notes: What is the power of Om? Saying Om while remembering Krishna at death leads to the supreme goal. Why Om? It is the sacred sound that stands for Brahman.

verses.en: Arjuna, for the yogi who always remembers me with undivided mind, constantly devoted, I am easy to reach.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, जो योगी अनन्य मन से हमेशा मुझे याद करता है और लगातार मुझसे जुड़ा रहता है, उसके लिए मैं आसानी से मिलने वाला हूँ।
verses.short: For someone who remembers me constantly with full focus, I'm easy to reach.
verses.notes: For whom is Krishna easy to reach? For the yogi who remembers him constantly with an undivided mind. What is the key word? Constant. Regular remembrance makes him close.

verses.en: Having come to me, great souls are not reborn into this temporary home of sorrow. They have reached the highest perfection.
verses.hi: मुझे पाकर महात्मा फिर से इस दुखों के घर और नाशवान जन्म में नहीं आते। वे परम सिद्धि पा चुके हैं।
verses.short: Those who reach me don't come back to a temporary world full of pain. They've made it.
verses.notes: What happens after reaching Krishna? No rebirth into this temporary world of sorrow. Why call birth 'the home of sorrow'? Every life here involves loss, change and pain.

verses.en: Arjuna, all worlds, even up to the realm of Brahma, are subject to return. But on reaching me, there is no rebirth.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, ब्रह्मलोक तक के सारे लोक लौटकर आने वाले हैं। पर हे कौन्तेय, मुझे पाकर फिर जन्म नहीं होता।
verses.short: Every world, even the highest heaven, has a return ticket. Reach me and there's no return.
verses.notes: Is even heaven permanent? No. All worlds, even Brahma's, involve return. What is different about reaching Krishna? There is no return after that.

verses.en: Those who understand cosmic day and night know that a day of Brahma lasts a thousand ages, and his night also lasts a thousand ages.
verses.hi: जो दिन और रात का रहस्य जानते हैं, वे जानते हैं कि ब्रह्मा का एक दिन हज़ार युगों का होता है और उनकी रात भी हज़ार युगों की।
verses.short: A single day of the creator lasts thousands of ages. Our timeline is tiny on the cosmic scale.
verses.notes: How long is a day of Brahma? A thousand cycles of ages, and his night is just as long. Why mention such huge time? To show even vast cosmic cycles are temporary.

verses.en: When that day begins, all visible things come out of the unseen. When night falls, they dissolve back into that same unseen.
verses.hi: ब्रह्मा का दिन शुरू होने पर सारी दिखने वाली चीज़ें अव्यक्त से प्रकट होती हैं, और रात आने पर उसी अव्यक्त में लीन हो जाती हैं।
verses.short: When the cosmic day starts, everything appears. When cosmic night falls, everything dissolves.
verses.notes: What happens at Brahma's day and night? At dawn all beings emerge; at night they merge back into the unmanifest. What does this cycle show? Creation and dissolution keep repeating.

verses.en: This same multitude of beings comes into being again and again, and helplessly dissolves when night falls, Arjuna, and appears again when day comes.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, यही प्राणियों का समूह बार-बार पैदा होकर रात आने पर मजबूरी में लीन हो जाता है, और दिन आने पर फिर प्रकट होता है।
verses.short: Beings appear and disappear again and again, on repeat, with every cosmic day and night.
verses.notes: Do beings choose this cycle? No. They are born again and again, helplessly, by the force of nature. How do we escape? By reaching the Supreme, beyond this cycle.

verses.en: But beyond that unseen there is another unseen, eternal reality, which does not perish when all beings perish.
verses.hi: पर उस अव्यक्त से परे एक और सनातन अव्यक्त भाव है, जो सब प्राणियों के नष्ट होने पर भी नष्ट नहीं होता।
verses.short: But beyond all that is something eternal that never gets destroyed, even when everything else does.
verses.notes: What lies beyond the unmanifest? Another eternal unmanifest reality that never perishes. Why is it special? Even when everything else dissolves, it remains.

verses.en: That unseen is called the imperishable, and it is said to be the highest goal. Those who reach it never return. That is my supreme home.
verses.hi: उस अव्यक्त को अक्षर कहा जाता है और उसे ही परम गति कहते हैं। जिसे पाकर लोग वापस नहीं लौटते, वही मेरा परम धाम है।
verses.short: That eternal state is my home. Once you reach it, you never come back.
verses.notes: What is Krishna's supreme abode? The imperishable unmanifest, the highest goal. What happens there? Those who reach it do not return.

verses.en: Arjuna, that Supreme Being, in whom all beings live and by whom all this is pervaded, can be reached by undivided devotion.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, वह परम पुरुष, जिसमें सब प्राणी रहते हैं और जिससे यह सब व्याप्त है, अनन्य भक्ति से ही मिलता है।
verses.short: The supreme, who holds everything, is reached through pure, single-minded devotion.
verses.notes: How is the Supreme reached? Through single-minded devotion. Where is this Supreme? All beings are in him, and he pervades all.

verses.en: Now, best of the Bharatas, I will tell you the times at which yogis who depart either do not return or do return.
verses.hi: हे भरतश्रेष्ठ, अब मैं तुम्हें वह समय बताता हूँ जिसमें शरीर छोड़ने वाले योगी या तो लौटकर नहीं आते या लौट आते हैं।
verses.short: Now I'll tell you about the two ways people leave this world: one with return, one without.
verses.notes: What will Krishna explain now? The times or paths by which yogis leave and either return or don't. Why does this matter? It shows two directions a life can lead.

verses.en: Fire, light, daytime, the bright half of the month, the six months of the sun's northern path: those who know the Supreme and depart then go to the Supreme.
verses.hi: आग, प्रकाश, दिन, शुक्ल पक्ष और उत्तरायण के छह महीने, इस मार्ग में जाने वाले ब्रह्म के ज्ञानी ब्रह्म को पाते हैं।
verses.short: The path of light: those who know the truth take this route and don't come back.
verses.notes: What is the path of light? Fire, light, day, the bright fortnight and the northern course of the sun. Knowers of Brahman go by it to Brahman. Is this about timing or symbolism? Many read it symbolically: a life of light and knowledge leads upward.

verses.en: Smoke, night, the dark half of the month, the six months of the sun's southern path: the yogi who departs then reaches the light of the moon and returns.
verses.hi: धुआँ, रात, कृष्ण पक्ष और दक्षिणायन के छह महीने, इस मार्ग में जाने वाला योगी चंद्रमा की ज्योति पाकर लौट आता है।
verses.short: The path of smoke and darkness: those who take this route come back again.
verses.notes: What is the path of darkness? Smoke, night, the dark fortnight and the southern course. The yogi reaches lunar light and returns. What does 'returns' mean? Rebirth after enjoying the results of good deeds.

verses.en: These two paths of the world, the bright and the dark, are considered eternal. By one, a person does not return; by the other, they return again.
verses.hi: संसार के ये दो मार्ग, शुक्ल और कृष्ण, सनातन माने जाते हैं। एक से जाने वाला लौटता नहीं, और दूसरे से जाने वाला फिर लौट आता है।
verses.short: Two eternal paths, light and dark. One leads out of the cycle, the other back into it.
verses.notes: What are the two eternal paths? The bright path, which leads to no return, and the dark path, which leads back. Why call them eternal? They have always existed in the order of the universe.

verses.en: Knowing these two paths, Arjuna, no yogi is ever confused. So at all times, be steady in yoga.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, इन दोनों मार्गों को जानने वाला कोई योगी भ्रम में नहीं पड़ता। इसलिए हे अर्जुन, हर समय योग में स्थित रहो।
verses.short: A yogi who knows these paths isn't confused. So stay steady in yoga, always.
verses.notes: Why isn't the yogi confused? Knowing both paths, they aren't misled. What is Krishna's advice? Be steady in yoga at all times.

verses.en: Whatever good results are promised for studying the Vedas, for sacrifice, austerity and charity, the yogi who knows this goes beyond them all and reaches the supreme, original home.
verses.hi: वेद पढ़ने, यज्ञ, तप और दान का जो भी पुण्य-फल बताया गया है, यह जानकर योगी उन सबसे आगे निकल जाता है और परम आदि स्थान को पाता है।
verses.short: Know this, and you go beyond all the rewards of rituals and good deeds to the supreme state.
verses.notes: What does the yogi go beyond? The rewards of study, sacrifice, austerity and charity. Where do they reach? The supreme, primal abode.

verses.en: Krishna said: Since you don't find fault, I will tell you this deepest secret, knowledge along with its realisation. Knowing it, you will be freed from all harm.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: क्योंकि तुम दोष नहीं निकालते, मैं तुम्हें यह सबसे गहरा रहस्य, विज्ञान सहित ज्ञान, बताऊँगा, जिसे जानकर तुम अशुभ से मुक्त हो जाओगे।
verses.short: Krishna: "Since you don't nitpick, I'll tell you the deepest secret. It'll free you."
verses.notes: Why does Krishna share this secret with Arjuna? Because Arjuna doesn't find fault or argue for the sake of it. He is open to learning. What will this knowledge do? Free him from all that is harmful.

verses.en: This is the king of knowledge, the king of secrets, the purest and the highest. It can be directly experienced, it is in line with what is right, it is easy to practise and it never fades.
verses.hi: यह सब विद्याओं का राजा, सब रहस्यों का राजा, सबसे पवित्र और उत्तम है। इसका सीधा अनुभव होता है, यह धर्म के अनुकूल है, करने में आसान है और कभी नष्ट नहीं होता।
verses.short: This is the king of all knowledge. You can experience it directly, and it's actually enjoyable to practise.
verses.notes: Why is it called the royal knowledge? It is the highest knowledge, the deepest secret and the greatest purifier. Is it hard to practise? No. Krishna says it is easy, pleasant and can be directly experienced.

verses.en: Arjuna, people who have no faith in this path don't reach me and return to the cycle of death and rebirth.
verses.hi: हे परंतप, जो लोग इस धर्म में श्रद्धा नहीं रखते, वे मुझे न पाकर मृत्यु और संसार के चक्र में लौट आते हैं।
verses.short: People with zero faith in this keep going around in the cycle and never reach me.
verses.notes: What happens to those without faith? They don't reach the Divine and keep returning to the cycle of birth and death. Why is faith so important? Without trust, you never begin the journey.

verses.en: This whole universe is pervaded by me in my unseen form. All beings rest in me, but I do not rest in them.
verses.hi: यह पूरा जगत मेरे अदृश्य रूप से व्याप्त है। सब प्राणी मुझमें स्थित हैं, पर मैं उनमें स्थित नहीं हूँ।
verses.short: I'm in everything, unseen. Everything rests in me, but I'm not limited by any of it.
verses.notes: How does Krishna pervade everything? In his unmanifest form, he fills the whole universe. What does 'I am not in them' mean? Everything depends on him, but he doesn't depend on anything.

verses.en: And yet beings do not rest in me. See my divine mystery! I support all beings and bring them into existence, but my self does not rest in them.
verses.hi: और फिर भी प्राणी मुझमें स्थित नहीं हैं। मेरी दिव्य योग-शक्ति देखो! मैं सब प्राणियों को धारण करता और पैदा करता हूँ, फिर भी मेरी आत्मा उनमें स्थित नहीं है।
verses.short: I hold everything up, yet I'm not stuck in anything. That's my mystery.
verses.notes: Isn't this a contradiction? Krishna calls it his divine mystery: he supports all beings, yet isn't bound within them. How do beings exist then? By his will alone.

verses.en: Just as the mighty wind, blowing everywhere, always rests in space, understand that all beings rest in me in the same way.
verses.hi: जैसे हर जगह बहने वाली तेज़ हवा हमेशा आकाश में ही रहती है, वैसे ही समझो कि सब प्राणी मुझमें स्थित हैं।
verses.short: Like wind moves through the sky but stays in the sky, all beings move within me.
verses.notes: What does the air and sky example mean? Wind moves everywhere within the sky without affecting it. Beings move within the Divine the same way. Why this image? It helps picture something vast holding everything without being touched.

verses.en: Arjuna, at the end of a cosmic cycle all beings merge into my nature. At the start of the next cycle, I send them forth again.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, कल्प के अंत में सब प्राणी मेरी प्रकृति में लीन हो जाते हैं, और कल्प की शुरुआत में मैं उन्हें फिर से रचता हूँ।
verses.short: At the end of a cosmic cycle everything returns to me, and at the start I send it out again.
verses.notes: What happens at the end of a cosmic cycle? All beings merge back into Krishna's nature. And at the beginning? He sends them forth again.

verses.en: Taking hold of my own nature, I send forth this whole multitude of beings again and again. They are helpless, under the control of nature.
verses.hi: अपनी प्रकृति को वश में करके मैं प्रकृति के अधीन इस पूरे प्राणी-समूह को बार-बार रचता हूँ।
verses.short: Through nature I create again and again. Beings follow nature's flow.
verses.notes: How does creation happen again and again? Krishna uses his own nature to bring beings forth repeatedly. Why are beings 'helpless'? They are under the sway of nature and their past actions.

verses.en: These actions don't bind me, Arjuna. I sit as if neutral, unattached to these actions.
verses.hi: हे धनंजय, ये कर्म मुझे नहीं बाँधते। मैं इन कर्मों से अनासक्त होकर उदासीन की तरह बैठा रहता हूँ।
verses.short: None of this binds me, because I stay detached. Like a chill observer.
verses.notes: Why don't these actions bind Krishna? He stays detached, like a neutral witness. What can we learn? We too can act fully without being bound, if we let go of attachment.

verses.en: Under my watch, nature produces everything moving and unmoving. Because of this, Arjuna, the world keeps turning.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, मेरी देखरेख में प्रकृति चर-अचर सब कुछ पैदा करती है। इसी कारण यह संसार चलता रहता है।
verses.short: Under my watch, nature creates everything, and the world keeps turning.
verses.notes: Who really runs the universe? Nature, under Krishna's guidance, produces everything moving and unmoving. What does 'the world revolves' mean? The cycle of creation keeps turning because of this.

verses.en: The deluded look down on me when I take a human form, not knowing my higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.
verses.hi: जब मैं मनुष्य का शरीर धारण करता हूँ, तो मूर्ख लोग मुझे तुच्छ समझते हैं। वे सब प्राणियों के महान ईश्वर के रूप में मेरे परम भाव को नहीं जानते।
verses.short: Some people see me in human form and dismiss me. They don't see who I really am.
verses.notes: Why do some people dismiss Krishna? They see only his human form and don't know his supreme nature. What is the lesson? Don't judge by appearance; the Divine can be hidden in the ordinary.

verses.en: Their hopes are empty, their actions useless, their knowledge pointless and their minds confused. They take on a deluding, cruel and demonic nature.
verses.hi: उनकी आशाएँ बेकार हैं, कर्म बेकार हैं, ज्ञान बेकार है और मन भटका हुआ है। वे राक्षसी और आसुरी मोह वाली प्रकृति अपना लेते हैं।
verses.short: Their hopes, actions and knowledge go to waste because they're stuck in a negative mindset.
verses.notes: What happens to the deluded? Their hopes, actions and knowledge all go to waste. Why? Their nature is ruled by delusion and harmful tendencies.

verses.en: But great souls, Arjuna, who take on a divine nature, worship me with undivided minds, knowing me as the unchanging origin of all beings.
verses.hi: पर हे पार्थ, दैवी प्रकृति अपनाने वाले महात्मा मुझे सब प्राणियों का अविनाशी आदि कारण जानकर अनन्य मन से भजते हैं।
verses.short: Great souls with a divine nature worship me single-mindedly, knowing I'm the source of everything.
verses.notes: How do great souls worship? With an undistracted mind, knowing Krishna as the eternal source of all. What nature do they have? A divine nature, full of good qualities.

verses.en: Always singing my praises, striving with firm resolve, bowing to me with devotion, they worship me, always united with me.
verses.hi: हमेशा मेरा कीर्तन करते हुए, पक्के व्रत से कोशिश करते हुए, भक्ति से मुझे प्रणाम करते हुए, वे हमेशा मुझसे जुड़कर मेरी उपासना करते हैं।
verses.short: They keep singing about me, stay committed, and bow with love. Pure devotion.
verses.notes: What do devoted souls do? They praise him constantly, strive with firm resolve and bow with devotion. Is this only ritual? No. It's a lifestyle of steady love and remembrance.

verses.en: Others worship me through the offering of knowledge, seeing me as one, as many, and in countless ways as the one whose face is everywhere.
verses.hi: दूसरे लोग ज्ञान-यज्ञ से मेरी पूजा करते हैं, मुझे एक रूप में, अलग-अलग रूपों में और हर दिशा में मुख वाले विराट रूप में देखते हुए।
verses.short: Others worship me through knowledge: as one, as many, as the whole universe.
verses.notes: What other ways of worship are mentioned? Some worship through knowledge, seeing the Divine as one, as separate, or in many forms. What is the message? There are many valid ways to approach the Divine.

verses.en: I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the healing herb. I am the sacred chant, I am the ghee, I am the fire and I am the act of offering.
verses.hi: मैं ही क्रतु हूँ, मैं ही यज्ञ हूँ, पितरों को दिया अन्न मैं हूँ, औषधि मैं हूँ। मंत्र मैं हूँ, घी मैं हूँ, अग्नि मैं हूँ और हवन भी मैं ही हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the ritual, the offering, the herb, the mantra, the fire and the act of offering. I'm all of it.
verses.notes: What does Krishna say he is in a ritual? The ritual, the offering, the herb, the mantra, the ghee, the fire and the act of offering. What is the point? Every part of worship is the Divine itself.

verses.en: I am the father of this world, its mother, its supporter and its grandfather. I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.
verses.hi: इस जगत का पिता, माता, धारण करने वाला और दादा मैं हूँ। जानने योग्य, पवित्र करने वाला, ओंकार, और ऋग्वेद, सामवेद और यजुर्वेद भी मैं हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the father, mother and grandparent of the universe. I'm Om, and every sacred text.
verses.notes: What relations does Krishna claim with the world? Father, mother, supporter and grandfather of the universe. What else is he? The purifier, Om, and the Vedas.

verses.en: I am the goal, the support, the master, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend. I am the beginning, the end, the foundation, the storehouse and the imperishable seed.
verses.hi: मैं ही लक्ष्य, पालनहार, स्वामी, साक्षी, निवास, शरण और मित्र हूँ। मैं ही उत्पत्ति, प्रलय, आधार, भंडार और अविनाशी बीज हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the goal, the support, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend. The start and end of everything.
verses.notes: What roles does Krishna describe here? Goal, supporter, Lord, witness, home, refuge and friend. Which one is most comforting? 'Friend'. The Supreme is also your closest well-wisher.

verses.en: I give heat. I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and also death. I am both what is and what is not, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, मैं ही गर्मी देता हूँ, मैं ही बारिश को रोकता और बरसाता हूँ। मैं अमृत भी हूँ और मृत्यु भी, सत् भी हूँ और असत् भी।
verses.short: I bring heat and rain. I'm life and death, what exists and what doesn't.
verses.notes: What opposites does Krishna say he is? Heat and rain, immortality and death, being and non-being. Why include death? Everything, even endings, is part of the Divine.

verses.en: Those who follow the three Vedas, drink the soma and are cleansed of sin worship me through sacrifices and pray to reach heaven. Reaching the holy world of Indra, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods.
verses.hi: तीनों वेदों का पालन करने वाले, सोमरस पीने वाले और पापों से शुद्ध हुए लोग यज्ञों से मेरी पूजा करके स्वर्ग की प्रार्थना करते हैं। पुण्य से इंद्रलोक पाकर वे स्वर्ग में देवताओं के दिव्य सुख भोगते हैं।
verses.short: Some perform rituals to get into heaven. They get there and enjoy divine pleasures.
verses.notes: What do ritual worshippers seek? Heaven, through Vedic sacrifices. Do they get it? Yes, they reach heaven and enjoy divine pleasures there.

verses.en: Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, they return to the world of mortals when their merit runs out. Following the rituals of the three Vedas and wanting pleasures, they keep coming and going.
verses.hi: उस विशाल स्वर्ग का सुख भोगकर, पुण्य खत्म होने पर वे फिर मृत्युलोक में आ जाते हैं। इस तरह तीनों वेदों के कर्मकांड का पालन करने वाले, भोग चाहने वाले लोग आते-जाते रहते हैं।
verses.short: But when their good-karma balance runs out, they come back. Heaven is a holiday, not a home.
verses.notes: What happens after heaven? When their merit runs out, they return to the mortal world. What is the lesson? Rewards based on desire are temporary; they come and go.

verses.en: But those who worship me thinking of nothing else, always devoted, I bring them what they lack and protect what they have.
verses.hi: पर जो लोग किसी और का नहीं, केवल मेरा चिंतन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, हमेशा मुझसे जुड़े उन लोगों का योग-क्षेम मैं खुद संभालता हूँ।
verses.short: Those who focus only on me, I take care of. What they need, I bring. What they have, I protect.
verses.notes: What does Krishna promise devoted hearts? He takes care of what they need and protects what they have. Why is this verse so loved? It's a promise of care for those who trust fully.

verses.en: Arjuna, even devotees of other gods who worship them with faith are really worshipping me, though not in the proper way.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, जो भक्त श्रद्धा से दूसरे देवताओं की पूजा करते हैं, वे भी असल में मेरी ही पूजा करते हैं, पर सही विधि से नहीं।
verses.short: Even people who worship other gods with faith are really worshipping me, just indirectly.
verses.notes: What about those who worship other gods with faith? They are really worshipping Krishna, though not in the ideal way. What does this show? Sincere faith is never wasted.

verses.en: I am the one who enjoys all sacrifices and their Lord. But they don't know me as I truly am, so they fall back.
verses.hi: सब यज्ञों का भोक्ता और स्वामी मैं ही हूँ। पर वे मुझे सच में नहीं जानते, इसलिए गिर जाते हैं।
verses.short: I'm the one who receives every offering. Not knowing this, people slip back.
verses.notes: Why do some people fall back? They don't recognise Krishna as the true enjoyer and Lord of all worship. What's missing? Knowing who is really receiving the worship.

verses.en: Worshippers of the gods go to the gods, worshippers of ancestors go to the ancestors, worshippers of spirits go to the spirits, and my worshippers come to me.
verses.hi: देवताओं को पूजने वाले देवताओं के पास जाते हैं, पितरों को पूजने वाले पितरों के पास, भूतों को पूजने वाले भूतों के पास, और मुझे पूजने वाले मेरे पास आते हैं।
verses.short: You become what you worship. Worship the gods and you go to them. Worship me and you come to me.
verses.notes: Where do worshippers go? To what they worship: gods, ancestors or spirits. And those who worship Krishna? They come to him.

verses.en: Whoever offers me with love a leaf, a flower, a fruit or some water, I accept that offering of love from a pure heart.
verses.hi: जो प्रेम से मुझे एक पत्ता, फूल, फल या थोड़ा पानी अर्पित करता है, उस शुद्ध मन वाले के प्रेम से दिए उस उपहार को मैं स्वीकार करता हूँ।
verses.short: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, or some water, given with love: I accept it. It's the heart that counts.
verses.notes: What does God want as an offering? Just a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, offered with love. What matters most? The love behind the offering, not its cost.

verses.en: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give and whatever discipline you practise, Arjuna, do it as an offering to me.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, तुम जो कुछ करते हो, जो खाते हो, जो हवन करते हो, जो दान देते हो और जो तप करते हो, वह सब मुझे अर्पित कर दो।
verses.short: Whatever you do, eat, give or practise, offer it to me. Turn your whole life into an offering.
verses.notes: How can daily life become worship? Offer whatever you do, eat, give or endure to the Divine. Does this mean changing what I do? Mostly it changes how you do it, with a sense of offering.

verses.en: This way you will be freed from the bonds of action and their good and bad results. With your mind set on renunciation through yoga, you will be free and come to me.
verses.hi: इस तरह तुम कर्म के बंधनों और उनके अच्छे-बुरे फलों से छूट जाओगे। संन्यास-योग में मन लगाकर तुम मुक्त होकर मुझे पाओगे।
verses.short: Do this and you're freed from good and bad karma alike. Free, you'll come to me.
verses.notes: What does offering everything do? Frees you from the binding results of good and bad actions. Where does it lead? To Krishna himself.

verses.en: I am the same towards all beings. No one is hateful to me and no one is my favourite. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.
verses.hi: मैं सब प्राणियों के लिए एक समान हूँ। न कोई मुझे अप्रिय है, न प्रिय। पर जो भक्ति से मुझे भजते हैं, वे मुझमें हैं और मैं उनमें हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the same to everyone. No favourites, no haters. But those who love me live in me, and I in them.
verses.notes: Does God have favourites? No. He is the same to all, with no one hated or favoured. Then why are devotees close to him? Because they turn toward him with love, and love creates closeness.

verses.en: Even if a person of very bad conduct worships me with undivided devotion, they should be seen as good, because they have made the right decision.
verses.hi: अगर बहुत बुरे आचरण वाला व्यक्ति भी अनन्य भाव से मुझे भजता है, तो उसे साधु ही मानना चाहिए, क्योंकि उसने सही निश्चय कर लिया है।
verses.short: Even someone who's done terrible things, if they turn to me sincerely, should be seen as good. They've chosen right.
verses.notes: Can a wrongdoer become good? Yes. If they turn to the Divine with undivided devotion, they should be seen as good. Why? Their resolve has become right, and that's what counts now.

verses.en: They quickly become righteous and find lasting peace. Arjuna, declare it boldly: my devotee is never lost.
verses.hi: वह जल्दी ही धर्मात्मा बन जाता है और स्थायी शांति पाता है। हे कौन्तेय, यह पक्का जान लो कि मेरा भक्त कभी नष्ट नहीं होता।
verses.short: They change quickly and find lasting peace. Tell the world: my devotee never falls.
verses.notes: How quickly does change happen? Quickly. Such a person soon becomes righteous and finds lasting peace. What promise does Krishna make? 'My devotee never perishes.'

verses.en: Arjuna, whoever takes refuge in me, whatever their birth, women, merchants and labourers too, reaches the highest goal.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, जो भी मेरी शरण लेता है, चाहे उसका जन्म कैसा भी हो, स्त्रियाँ, वैश्य और शूद्र भी, वे परम गति पाते हैं।
verses.short: Anyone, regardless of birth, gender or class, who turns to me reaches the highest. No exceptions.
verses.notes: Who can reach the highest goal? Anyone who takes refuge in the Divine, whatever their birth, gender or social position. Why mention these groups? In a society with rigid divisions, Krishna says the path is open to all.

verses.en: How much more then the pure priests and devoted royal sages! Having come into this temporary, joyless world, worship me.
verses.hi: फिर पुण्यात्मा ब्राह्मणों और भक्त राजर्षियों का तो कहना ही क्या! इस नाशवान और दुख भरे संसार में आकर मुझे भजो।
verses.short: This world is temporary and full of struggle. So while you're here, connect with me.
verses.notes: What does Krishna say about the world? It is temporary and joyless, so turn to the Divine while here. Is this pessimistic? It's realistic: lasting joy isn't found in passing things.

verses.en: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me and bow to me. Uniting yourself with me and making me your goal, you will surely come to me.
verses.hi: मुझमें मन लगाओ, मेरे भक्त बनो, मेरी पूजा करो और मुझे प्रणाम करो। इस तरह खुद को मुझसे जोड़कर और मुझे लक्ष्य मानकर तुम मुझे ही पाओगे।
verses.short: Keep your mind on me, love me, honour me, bow to me. Make me your goal and you'll reach me.
verses.notes: What is Krishna's simple instruction? Fix your mind on him, be devoted, worship him and bow to him. What is the result? You will surely come to him.

verses.en: Krishna said: Listen again, mighty Arjuna, to my supreme words. Because you are dear to me, I will tell you this for your good.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे महाबाहु, मेरे परम वचन फिर से सुनो। तुम मुझे प्रिय हो, इसलिए तुम्हारे भले के लिए मैं यह कहूँगा।
verses.short: Krishna: "Listen again, because I want what's best for you, and you love me."
verses.notes: Why does Krishna keep teaching? Because he wants Arjuna's good and Arjuna listens with love. What is this chapter about? Krishna's divine glories and where to see them.

verses.en: My origin is a mystery even to the gods and the great sages, since every one of them came from me in the first place.
verses.hi: न देवता मेरी उत्पत्ति जानते हैं, न महर्षि, क्योंकि मैं हर तरह से देवताओं और महर्षियों का भी आदि कारण हूँ।
verses.short: Not even gods or great sages know where I come from. I'm their source.
verses.notes: Why don't even gods know Krishna's origin? Because he is their source. What comes later can't fully know what came first. What does this tell us? The Divine is beyond even the highest beings.

verses.en: Whoever knows me as unborn, without beginning, and the great Lord of the worlds is free from confusion among mortals and is released from all sins.
verses.hi: जो मुझे अजन्मा, अनादि और सब लोकों का महान ईश्वर जानता है, वह इंसानों में भ्रम से मुक्त है और सब पापों से छूट जाता है।
verses.short: Whoever knows I'm unborn and beginningless, the Lord of all, is free from confusion and wrongdoing.
verses.notes: Who is free from delusion? The one who knows Krishna as unborn, beginningless and Lord of the worlds. What does such knowledge do? It frees them from all wrongs.

verses.en: Intelligence, knowledge, clarity, forgiveness, truth, self-control, calm, pleasure, pain, birth, death, fear and fearlessness,
verses.hi: बुद्धि, ज्ञान, भ्रम से मुक्ति, क्षमा, सत्य, इंद्रियों पर काबू, मन की शांति, सुख, दुख, जन्म, मृत्यु, डर और निडरता,
verses.short: Intelligence, wisdom, patience, truth, self-control, joy, pain, fear, courage: every quality comes from me.
verses.notes: What qualities come from Krishna? Intelligence, knowledge, clarity, patience, truth, self-control, calm, joy, sorrow, birth, death, fear and fearlessness. Why include sorrow and fear? All experiences arise from the same source.

verses.en: non-violence, evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame and disgrace: all these different states of beings come from me alone.
verses.hi: अहिंसा, समता, संतोष, तप, दान, यश और अपयश, प्राणियों के ये तरह-तरह के भाव मुझसे ही पैदा होते हैं।
verses.short: Kindness, contentment, discipline, generosity, fame and even bad reputation all arise from me.
verses.notes: What more qualities are listed? Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame and infamy. What is the message? Every human quality has its root in the Divine.

verses.en: The seven great sages of old and the four Manus came from my mind and share my nature. All the creatures of the world descend from them.
verses.hi: पुराने सात महर्षि और चार मनु मेरे ही भाव वाले हैं और मेरे मन से पैदा हुए हैं। दुनिया के सारे प्राणी उन्हीं से हुए हैं।
verses.short: The great sages and the first ancestors of humanity were born from my mind.
verses.notes: Who are the seven sages and four Manus? Ancient progenitors of humanity, born from Krishna's mind. Why mention them? All beings descend from them, and they come from Krishna.

verses.en: Whoever truly knows this glory and power of mine is united with me in unshakeable yoga. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hi: जो मेरी इस विभूति और योग-शक्ति को सच में जानता है, वह अटल योग से मुझसे जुड़ जाता है। इसमें कोई संदेह नहीं।
verses.short: Truly understand my glory and power, and your devotion becomes unshakeable.
verses.notes: What happens to one who truly knows Krishna's glory? They become steady in unwavering devotion. Why does knowing lead to love? Seeing the Divine's greatness naturally inspires devotion.

verses.en: I am the source of everything; everything comes from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with deep feeling.
verses.hi: मैं ही सबकी उत्पत्ति हूँ, सब कुछ मुझसे ही चलता है। यह जानकर बुद्धिमान लोग भाव से भरकर मुझे भजते हैं।
verses.short: I'm the source of everything. The wise get this and love me with their whole heart.
verses.notes: What do the wise realise? Krishna is the source of everything, and everything comes from him. How do they respond? They worship him with deep feeling.

verses.en: With their minds on me and their lives given to me, enlightening one another and always talking about me, they are content and full of joy.
verses.hi: मुझमें मन लगाकर, मुझमें प्राण अर्पित करके, एक-दूसरे को समझाते हुए और हमेशा मेरी चर्चा करते हुए वे संतुष्ट और आनंदित रहते हैं।
verses.short: Their minds on me, lives centred on me, they inspire each other and talk about me. They're always happy.
verses.notes: What do true devotees do? Their minds and lives are centred on Krishna; they inspire each other and talk about him. How do they feel? Content and joyful.

verses.en: To those who are always devoted and worship me with love, I give the understanding by which they come to me.
verses.hi: जो हमेशा मुझसे जुड़े रहते हैं और प्रेम से मुझे भजते हैं, उन्हें मैं वह बुद्धि-योग देता हूँ जिससे वे मुझ तक पहुँचते हैं।
verses.short: To those who love me constantly, I give the understanding that brings them to me.
verses.notes: What does Krishna give his devotees? The understanding that brings them to him. Who receives it? Those who are always connected and worship with love.

verses.en: Out of compassion for them, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
verses.hi: उन पर कृपा करने के लिए, उनके हृदय में रहकर, मैं ज्ञान के चमकते दीपक से अज्ञान से पैदा हुए अंधकार को मिटा देता हूँ।
verses.short: Out of love, I light up their hearts and destroy the darkness of ignorance.
verses.notes: How does Krishna help devotees inwardly? Out of compassion, he lights the lamp of knowledge in their hearts. What does the lamp remove? The darkness of ignorance.

verses.en: Arjuna said: You are the Supreme, the highest home, the purest of all, the eternal divine being, the first god, unborn and all-pervading.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: आप ही सबसे ऊँचा सत्य, सबका अंतिम ठिकाना और सबसे पवित्र हैं। आप हमेशा रहने वाले दिव्य पुरुष हैं, सबसे पहले देव, जिनका न जन्म होता है और जो हर जगह फैले हैं।
verses.short: Arjuna: "You're the supreme reality, the highest light, the purest of all. The sages agree."
verses.notes: How does Arjuna respond? He calls Krishna the Supreme Brahman, the supreme abode and the supreme purifier. What has changed in Arjuna? He now sees Krishna as far more than a friend.

verses.en: All the sages say so about you, as do the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa. And now you yourself tell me so.
verses.hi: सारे ऋषि, देवर्षि नारद, असित, देवल और व्यास आपके बारे में यही कहते हैं, और अब आप खुद भी मुझसे यही कह रहे हैं।
verses.short: "Great seers like Narada and Vyasa said so, and now you're telling me yourself."
verses.notes: Who else praised Krishna this way? Sages like Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa. What does Arjuna add? 'And now you tell me yourself.'

verses.en: Krishna, I accept as true everything you tell me. Lord, neither the gods nor the demons understand your true form.
verses.hi: हे केशव, आप जो कुछ मुझसे कहते हैं, उसे मैं सच मानता हूँ। हे भगवन, आपके असली स्वरूप को न देवता जानते हैं, न दानव।
verses.short: "I believe everything you've said. Neither gods nor demons truly know you."
verses.notes: Does Arjuna believe Krishna? Yes. He accepts everything Krishna has said as true. What does he admit? Neither gods nor demons truly know Krishna's nature.

verses.en: Only you know yourself by yourself, Supreme Being, source and Lord of all beings, God of gods, ruler of the world.
verses.hi: हे पुरुषोत्तम, हे सब प्राणियों को रचने वाले और उनके ईश्वर, हे देवों के देव, हे जगत के स्वामी, आप खुद ही अपने आप को जानते हैं।
verses.short: "Only you know yourself, Krishna. Creator of all, God of gods."
verses.notes: Who alone knows Krishna? Only Krishna knows himself. What titles does Arjuna use? Supreme Person, source of beings, Lord of beings, God of gods, Lord of the world.

verses.en: Please tell me fully about your divine glories, through which you pervade and stand in all these worlds.
verses.hi: कृपया अपनी उन दिव्य विभूतियों के बारे में पूरी तरह बताइए, जिनसे आप इन सब लोकों में व्याप्त होकर स्थित हैं।
verses.short: "Please tell me all the ways you show up in the world."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna request? To hear in full about the divine glories through which Krishna pervades the worlds. Why ask for this? To have concrete ways to think of the Divine.

verses.en: How should I know you, great yogi, while always meditating on you? In which forms should I think of you, Lord?
verses.hi: हे योगेश्वर, हमेशा आपका चिंतन करते हुए मैं आपको कैसे जानूँ? हे भगवन, किन-किन रूपों में मुझे आपका ध्यान करना चाहिए?
verses.short: "How can I keep thinking of you? Where should I look to find you?"
verses.notes: What is Arjuna's practical question? How should he meditate on Krishna, and in what forms? Why is this helpful? The mind needs something to focus on.

verses.en: Krishna, tell me again in detail about your power and your glories. I never tire of hearing your nectar-like words.
verses.hi: हे जनार्दन, अपनी योग-शक्ति और विभूतियों के बारे में फिर से विस्तार से बताइए। आपके अमृत जैसे वचन सुनते हुए मेरा मन नहीं भरता।
verses.short: "Tell me again in detail. I can't get enough of hearing you." Arjuna is hooked.
verses.notes: Why does Arjuna ask again? He never tires of hearing Krishna's words, which feel like nectar. What does this show? Real interest makes learning a joy.

verses.en: Krishna said: Very well, Arjuna, I will tell you about my divine glories, but only the main ones. There is no end to my vastness.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: अच्छा, हे कुरुश्रेष्ठ, मैं तुम्हें अपनी मुख्य-मुख्य दिव्य विभूतियाँ बताता हूँ, क्योंकि मेरे विस्तार का कोई अंत नहीं है।
verses.short: Krishna: "I'll share the highlights. My glories are literally endless."
verses.notes: Will Krishna describe everything? No. His glories are endless, so he names only the main ones. Why only the main ones? Enough to show the pattern without overwhelming.

verses.en: Arjuna, I live as the self deep inside every creature. Every being starts from me, lives in me and ends in me.
verses.hi: हे गुडाकेश, मैं सब प्राणियों के हृदय में बसी आत्मा हूँ। मैं ही सब प्राणियों का आदि, मध्य और अंत हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the self inside every heart. The beginning, middle and end of every being.
verses.notes: What is Krishna's first and most important glory? He is the Self in the heart of all beings. What else? The beginning, middle and end of all beings.

verses.en: Among the Adityas I am Vishnu; among lights I am the radiant sun. Among the wind gods I am Marichi; among the stars I am the moon.
verses.hi: आदित्यों में मैं विष्णु हूँ, प्रकाश देने वालों में किरणों वाला सूरज हूँ। मरुतों में मैं मरीचि हूँ और नक्षत्रों में चंद्रमा।
verses.short: Among lights I'm the sun, among night skies I'm the moon. Wherever something shines brightest, that's me.
verses.notes: What examples does Krishna give here? Vishnu among the Adityas, the sun among lights, Marichi among the Maruts and the moon among stars. What is the pattern? He is the best in each group.

verses.en: Of the Vedas I am the Sama, the sung one; of the gods, Indra their king. Of the senses I am the mind, and in every creature I am the awareness that makes it alive.
verses.hi: वेदों में मैं सामवेद हूँ, देवताओं में इंद्र हूँ। इंद्रियों में मैं मन हूँ और प्राणियों में चेतना हूँ।
verses.short: Among scriptures I'm the musical Sama Veda, among senses I'm the mind, in living beings I'm consciousness.
verses.notes: What are Krishna's glories here? The Sama Veda among Vedas, Indra among gods, the mind among senses and consciousness in beings. Why the mind among senses? The mind guides all the senses.

verses.en: Among the Rudras I am Shiva; among the yakshas and rakshasas I am Kubera, lord of wealth. Among the Vasus I am fire; among mountains I am Meru.
verses.hi: रुद्रों में मैं शंकर हूँ, यक्षों और राक्षसों में धन का स्वामी कुबेर हूँ। वसुओं में मैं अग्नि हूँ और पर्वतों में मेरु।
verses.short: Among Rudras I'm Shiva, among mountains I'm Meru. The best of every category is me.
verses.notes: Which glories are named here? Shankara among Rudras, Kubera among Yakshas, Agni among Vasus and Meru among mountains. What do they share? Each is the chief of its group.

verses.en: Arjuna, among priests know me as their chief, Brihaspati. Among generals I am Skanda; among bodies of water I am the ocean.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, पुरोहितों में मुझे उनका मुखिया बृहस्पति जानो। सेनापतियों में मैं स्कंद हूँ और जलाशयों में समुद्र।
verses.short: Among priests I'm Brihaspati, among generals Skanda, among waters the ocean.
verses.notes: What glories are listed? Brihaspati among priests, Skanda among generals and the ocean among waters. Why the ocean? It is the greatest of all bodies of water.

verses.en: Among the great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the single syllable Om. Among offerings I am silent chanting; among unmoving things I am the Himalaya.
verses.hi: महर्षियों में मैं भृगु हूँ, शब्दों में एक अक्षर ओम हूँ। यज्ञों में मैं जप-यज्ञ हूँ और स्थिर चीज़ों में हिमालय।
verses.short: Among words I'm Om, among prayers I'm quiet chanting, among the unmoving I'm the Himalayas.
verses.notes: What glories are named? Bhrigu among sages, Om among words, japa among sacrifices and the Himalayas among mountains. Why is japa the best sacrifice? Repeating the Divine name is simple, pure and open to all.

verses.en: Of all trees I am the holy peepal; of the divine sages, Narada. Of the celestial singers I am Chitraratha, and of those who have reached perfection, the sage Kapila.
verses.hi: सब पेड़ों में मैं पीपल हूँ, देवर्षियों में नारद हूँ। गंधर्वों में मैं चित्ररथ हूँ और सिद्धों में कपिल मुनि।
verses.short: Among trees I'm the sacred fig, among divine sages Narada, among perfected beings Kapila.
verses.notes: What glories are named? The ashvattha among trees, Narada among divine sages, Chitraratha among Gandharvas and Kapila among the perfected. Who is Kapila? A great sage, the founder of Sankhya philosophy.

verses.en: Among horses know me as Uchchaihshravas, born from the nectar of the ocean. Among royal elephants I am Airavata, and among people I am the king.
verses.hi: घोड़ों में मुझे अमृत के साथ पैदा हुआ उच्चैःश्रवा जानो। बड़े हाथियों में मैं ऐरावत हूँ और इंसानों में राजा।
verses.short: Among horses I'm the divine Uchchaihshravas, among elephants Airavata, among people the leader.
verses.notes: What glories are named? Uchchaihshravas among horses, Airavata among elephants and the king among people. Why the king? A good ruler reflects divine order and protection.

verses.en: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am the wish-fulfilling Kamadhenu. I am Kandarpa, the god of love who creates life; among serpents I am Vasuki.
verses.hi: शस्त्रों में मैं वज्र हूँ, गायों में कामधेनु हूँ। संतान पैदा करने वाला कामदेव मैं हूँ, और सर्पों में वासुकि हूँ।
verses.short: Among weapons I'm the thunderbolt, among cows the wish-fulfilling one, among serpents Vasuki.
verses.notes: What glories are named? The thunderbolt among weapons, the wish-fulfilling cow among cows, the god of love who brings new life, and Vasuki among serpents. Why include the god of love? Desire that creates life, in line with dharma, is divine.

verses.en: Among the nagas I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among the ancestors I am Aryama; among those who keep order I am Yama.
verses.hi: नागों में मैं अनंत हूँ, जल के प्राणियों में वरुण हूँ। पितरों में मैं अर्यमा हूँ और नियम बनाए रखने वालों में यमराज।
verses.short: Among snakes I'm Ananta, among water beings Varuna, among those who keep order, Yama.
verses.notes: What glories are named? Ananta among serpents, Varuna among water beings, Aryama among ancestors and Yama among controllers. Why Yama? He represents perfect discipline and justice.

verses.en: Among the daityas I am Prahlada; among those who count I am time. Among animals I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda.
verses.hi: दैत्यों में मैं प्रह्लाद हूँ, गिनती करने वालों में समय हूँ। पशुओं में मैं सिंह हूँ और पक्षियों में गरुड़।
verses.short: Among animals I'm the lion, among birds Garuda, among demons' kids the devoted Prahlada.
