verses.notes: What glories are named? Prahlada among Daityas, time among measurers, the lion among animals and Garuda among birds. Why Prahlada? Born among demons, he was a great devotee, showing the Divine shines anywhere.

verses.en: Among purifiers I am the wind; among warriors I am Rama. Among sea creatures I am the makara; among rivers I am the Ganga.
verses.hi: पवित्र करने वालों में मैं हवा हूँ, शस्त्रधारियों में राम हूँ। जल-जीवों में मैं मगर हूँ और नदियों में गंगा।
verses.short: Among moving things I'm the wind, among warriors Rama, among rivers the Ganga.
verses.notes: What glories are named? The wind among purifiers, Rama among warriors, the makara among water creatures and the Ganga among rivers. Why the Ganga? It is the most sacred river, a symbol of purity.

verses.en: Of all creations I am the beginning, the end and also the middle, Arjuna. Among kinds of knowledge I am knowledge of the self; in debate I am the logic that reveals truth.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, सारी सृष्टि का आदि, अंत और मध्य मैं ही हूँ। विद्याओं में मैं अध्यात्म-विद्या हूँ और बहस करने वालों में सत्य तक पहुँचाने वाला तर्क।
verses.short: I'm the start, middle and end of creation. Among sciences, self-knowledge. In a debate, honest logic.
verses.notes: What glories are named? The beginning, middle and end of creation, self-knowledge among sciences, and reasoning in debate. Why self-knowledge? It is the highest of all learning.

verses.en: Among letters I am A; among compound words I am the pair. I alone am endless time, and I am the creator whose face is everywhere.
verses.hi: अक्षरों में मैं अ हूँ, समासों में द्वंद्व समास। मैं ही कभी न खत्म होने वाला काल हूँ, और हर दिशा में मुख वाला रचयिता भी मैं हूँ।
verses.short: Among letters I'm 'A'. I'm endless time itself, and the creator who sees in every direction.
verses.notes: What glories are named? The letter 'A', the dvandva compound, endless time and the creator facing all directions. Why the letter 'A'? It is the first letter and present in all sounds.

verses.en: I am death that takes all, and the source of all that is yet to be. Among feminine qualities I am fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, steadiness and patience.
verses.hi: सबको हर लेने वाली मृत्यु मैं हूँ और आने वाली हर चीज़ की उत्पत्ति भी मैं हूँ। स्त्री-गुणों में मैं कीर्ति, श्री, वाणी, स्मृति, मेधा, धृति और क्षमा हूँ।
verses.short: I'm death that takes all, and the source of all that's coming. I'm fame, memory, patience and forgiveness.
verses.notes: What glories are named? All-devouring death, the origin of all to come, and fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness and patience. Why list these qualities? They are the finest qualities, honoured as divine.

verses.en: Among hymns I am the Brihat Sama; among poetic metres I am the Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am spring, full of flowers.
verses.hi: सामवेद के गीतों में मैं बृहत्साम हूँ, छंदों में गायत्री हूँ। महीनों में मैं मार्गशीर्ष हूँ और ऋतुओं में फूलों वाला वसंत।
verses.short: Among hymns I'm the Brihat Saman, among metres the Gayatri, among seasons spring.
verses.notes: What glories are named? Brihatsama among hymns, Gayatri among metres, Margashirsha among months and spring among seasons. Why spring? It's the season of flowers and new life.

verses.en: Of the cheats I am gambling; I am the brilliance of the brilliant. I am victory, I am determination, and I am the goodness of the good.
verses.hi: छल करने वालों में मैं जुआ हूँ, तेजस्वियों का तेज हूँ। मैं जीत हूँ, मैं निश्चय हूँ, और सात्त्विक लोगों का सत्त्व मैं हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the brilliance of the brilliant, the victory, the effort, and the goodness of good people.
verses.notes: Why is gambling listed? Among the cunning, gambling is the strongest; even there, Krishna is the power behind it. What else is named? Brilliance, victory, determination and goodness.

verses.en: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Arjuna. Among sages I am Vyasa, and among poets I am the seer Ushana.
verses.hi: वृष्णियों में मैं वासुदेव हूँ, पांडवों में अर्जुन हूँ। मुनियों में मैं व्यास हूँ और कवियों में शुक्राचार्य।
verses.short: Among the Vrishnis I'm Krishna, among the Pandavas Arjuna, among sages Vyasa. Yes, Arjuna, you too.
verses.notes: What glories are named? Vasudeva among the Vrishnis, Arjuna among the Pandavas, Vyasa among sages and Ushana among poets. Why is Arjuna listed? Krishna sees his glory in his dear friend too.

verses.en: Among those who punish I am the rod of justice; among those seeking victory I am wise strategy. Among secrets I am silence, and I am the wisdom of the wise.
verses.hi: दंड देने वालों में मैं दंड हूँ, जीत चाहने वालों में नीति हूँ। रहस्यों में मैं मौन हूँ और ज्ञानियों का ज्ञान मैं हूँ।
verses.short: I'm discipline among rulers, strategy among winners, silence among secrets, wisdom among the wise.
verses.notes: What glories are named? Justice among rulers, strategy among those seeking victory, silence among secrets and wisdom among the wise. Why silence? The best-kept secret is the one never spoken.

verses.en: Arjuna, I am the seed of all beings. Nothing moving or unmoving can exist without me.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, सब प्राणियों का बीज मैं ही हूँ। चर या अचर ऐसा कुछ भी नहीं जो मेरे बिना हो।
verses.short: I'm the seed of every being. Nothing moving or still exists without me.
verses.notes: What is Krishna in all beings? The seed. Nothing moving or unmoving exists without him. What does this sum up? Everything owes its existence to the Divine.

verses.en: There is no end to my divine glories, Arjuna. What I have described is only a small sample of my vastness.
verses.hi: हे परंतप, मेरी दिव्य विभूतियों का कोई अंत नहीं है। मैंने तो अपने विस्तार का बस थोड़ा-सा उदाहरण बताया है।
verses.short: My divine forms have no limit. This was just a small sample.
verses.notes: Is this the full list? No. Krishna's glories are endless; this was just a brief sample. What should we take from that? Look for the Divine beyond any list.

verses.en: Whatever is glorious, beautiful or powerful, know that it comes from a spark of my splendour.
verses.hi: जो कुछ भी महिमा वाला, सुंदर या शक्तिशाली है, उसे मेरे तेज के एक अंश से पैदा हुआ जानो।
verses.short: Wherever you see power, beauty or greatness, that's a tiny spark of me.
verses.notes: How can we recognise the Divine anywhere? Wherever there is power, beauty or excellence, it's a spark of Krishna's glory. How can I use this daily? When something amazes you, see the Divine in it.

verses.en: But what is the use of all these details, Arjuna? I hold up this entire universe with just a single fraction of myself.
verses.hi: पर हे अर्जुन, इतने विस्तार को जानने से क्या लाभ? मैं इस पूरे जगत को अपने एक अंश मात्र से थामे हुए हूँ।
verses.short: But why all these details? Just know: I hold up this entire universe with a tiny fraction of myself.
verses.notes: What is Krishna's closing point? He supports the whole universe with just a fraction of himself. Why say 'what use is all this detail'? The key is to know he is the support of all, not to memorise lists.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Out of kindness to me, you have told me the deepest secret about the self. Your words have cleared away my confusion.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: मुझ पर कृपा करके आपने आत्मा के बारे में जो परम रहस्य बताया, उन वचनों से मेरा यह भ्रम दूर हो गया।
verses.short: Arjuna: "You've shared the deepest secret with me, and my confusion is gone."
verses.notes: How does Arjuna feel after Chapter 10? Grateful. He says Krishna's teaching has cleared his confusion. What is the 'mystery of the Self'? The truth about the soul and the Divine that Krishna has been explaining.

verses.en: Lotus-eyed Krishna, I have heard from you in detail about the birth and passing away of beings, and about your endless greatness.
verses.hi: हे कमलनयन, मैंने आपसे प्राणियों के जन्म और नाश के बारे में विस्तार से सुना है, और आपकी अनंत महिमा के बारे में भी।
verses.short: "I've heard how everything begins and ends in you, and how great you are."
verses.notes: What has Arjuna learned? How all beings arise and dissolve in Krishna, and his unchanging greatness. What does he want now? To see that greatness, not just hear about it.

verses.en: Supreme Lord, it is just as you have described yourself. Still, greatest of beings, I wish to see your divine form.
verses.hi: हे परमेश्वर, आपने अपने बारे में जैसा कहा, वह बिल्कुल वैसा ही है। फिर भी हे पुरुषोत्तम, मैं आपका ईश्वरीय रूप देखना चाहता हूँ।
verses.short: "I believe you. But now I want to actually see your divine form."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask to see? Krishna's divine, cosmic form. Does he doubt Krishna? No. He believes Krishna's words; he simply longs to see it.

verses.en: Lord, if you think I am able to see it, then, master of yoga, show me your eternal self.
verses.hi: हे प्रभु, अगर आप मानते हैं कि मैं उसे देख सकता हूँ, तो हे योगेश्वर, मुझे अपना अविनाशी स्वरूप दिखाइए।
verses.short: "If you think I can handle it, please show me." Brave request.
verses.notes: How does Arjuna ask? Humbly: only if Krishna thinks he is able to see it. What can we learn from this? Even a sincere request can be made with humility.

verses.en: Krishna said: Arjuna, see my hundreds and thousands of divine forms, of many kinds, colours and shapes.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे पार्थ, मेरे सैकड़ों-हज़ारों तरह के, अलग-अलग रंगों और आकारों वाले दिव्य रूपों को देखो।
verses.short: Krishna: "Then look. Hundreds and thousands of my forms, in every colour and shape."
verses.notes: What does Krishna say to Arjuna? 'Behold my forms, hundreds and thousands, divine, of many colours and shapes.' Why so many forms? The Divine is infinite and appears in endless ways.

verses.en: See the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins and the wind gods. See many wonders no one has ever seen before, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे भारत, आदित्यों, वसुओं, रुद्रों, दोनों अश्विनी कुमारों और मरुतों को देखो। ऐसे बहुत से अद्भुत रूप देखो जो पहले कभी नहीं देखे गए।
verses.short: "See all the gods and wonders no one has ever seen before."
verses.notes: What will Arjuna see in Krishna? The Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins, Maruts and wonders never seen before. What is the point? All the gods exist within the one Divine.

verses.en: See now the whole universe, moving and unmoving, gathered in one place in my body, and anything else you wish to see.
verses.hi: हे गुडाकेश, आज मेरे इस शरीर में एक जगह स्थित पूरे चर-अचर जगत को देखो, और जो कुछ और देखना चाहो, वह भी।
verses.short: "The whole universe, everything moving and still, is right here in my body. Look."
verses.notes: What will Arjuna see in Krishna's body? The whole universe, moving and unmoving, all in one place. What else is offered? Whatever else Arjuna wishes to see.

verses.en: But you can't see me with these eyes of yours. I give you divine sight. See my divine power.
verses.hi: पर तुम अपनी इन आँखों से मुझे नहीं देख सकते। मैं तुम्हें दिव्य दृष्टि देता हूँ। मेरी ईश्वरीय योग-शक्ति देखो।
verses.short: "Your normal eyes can't handle this. Here, I'm giving you divine vision." Upgrade unlocked.
verses.notes: Why can't Arjuna see it with normal eyes? Human eyes can't take in the infinite. What does Krishna give him? Divine sight.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: O King, having said this, Krishna, the great lord of yoga, showed Arjuna his supreme divine form.
verses.hi: संजय ने कहा: हे राजन, ऐसा कहकर महायोगेश्वर श्रीहरि ने अर्जुन को अपना परम ईश्वरीय रूप दिखाया।
verses.short: And then Krishna reveals his supreme cosmic form. The biggest reveal in the Gita.
verses.notes: Who describes this moment? Sanjaya, telling King Dhritarashtra what he sees. What does Krishna reveal? His supreme, majestic form.

verses.en: It had countless mouths and eyes, countless wonderful sights, countless divine ornaments and countless raised divine weapons.
verses.hi: उसमें अनगिनत मुख और आँखें थीं, अनगिनत अद्भुत दृश्य थे, अनगिनत दिव्य गहने थे और अनगिनत उठे हुए दिव्य शस्त्र थे।
verses.short: Countless faces and eyes, endless wonders, divine jewellery and weapons everywhere.
verses.notes: What does the cosmic form look like? Countless mouths and eyes, wonderful sights, divine ornaments and raised weapons. Why so overwhelming? It shows everything at once, beyond normal understanding.

verses.en: Wearing divine garlands and clothes, anointed with divine fragrances, full of every wonder, the endless God faced every direction.
verses.hi: दिव्य मालाएँ और वस्त्र पहने, दिव्य सुगंध लगाए, हर तरह के आश्चर्य से भरे, वे अनंत देव हर दिशा में मुख किए हुए थे।
verses.short: Divine garlands and robes, heavenly fragrance, glowing, infinite, facing every direction at once.
verses.notes: What more is described? Divine garlands, garments and fragrance, infinite and facing every direction. What does 'facing all directions' mean? The Divine is present everywhere at once.

verses.en: If a thousand suns rose at once in the sky, their light might come close to the brilliance of that great being.
verses.hi: अगर आकाश में एक साथ हज़ार सूरज उग आएँ, तो शायद उनकी रोशनी उस महात्मा के तेज जैसी हो सके।
verses.short: Imagine a thousand suns rising at once. That's how bright this form was.
verses.notes: How bright was the cosmic form? Like a thousand suns rising at once. Why is this line famous? It's one of the most powerful images in the Gita, often quoted to describe overwhelming light.

verses.en: There, in the body of the God of gods, Arjuna saw the whole universe in one place, divided in many ways.
verses.hi: तब अर्जुन ने देवों के देव के शरीर में एक जगह स्थित, अनेक हिस्सों में बँटे पूरे जगत को देखा।
verses.short: Arjuna saw the entire universe, in all its variety, in one place: inside Krishna.
verses.notes: What did Arjuna see in one place? The whole universe, with all its divisions, inside the body of the God of gods. What does this show? All diversity rests in one reality.

verses.en: Then Arjuna, filled with wonder, his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the Lord and, with joined palms, spoke.
verses.hi: तब आश्चर्य से भरे, रोंगटे खड़े हुए अर्जुन ने सिर झुकाकर प्रभु को प्रणाम किया और हाथ जोड़कर बोला।
verses.short: Arjuna is stunned, goosebumps everywhere. He bows his head and folds his hands.
verses.notes: How did Arjuna react? Filled with wonder, hair standing on end, he bowed and joined his palms. What does this show? Awe naturally leads to reverence.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Lord, I see in your body all the gods and every kind of being: Brahma seated on the lotus, Shiva, all the sages and the divine serpents.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे देव, मैं आपके शरीर में सब देवताओं और हर तरह के प्राणियों को देख रहा हूँ: कमल पर बैठे ब्रह्मा, शिव, सब ऋषि और दिव्य सर्प।
verses.short: "I see all the gods, all beings, Brahma, the sages and the divine serpents in you."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna see first? All the gods, all beings, Brahma on his lotus, Shiva, the sages and divine serpents. What is the message? Every divine being is within Krishna.

verses.en: I see you everywhere, with endless forms, countless arms, bellies, mouths and eyes. Lord of the universe, I see no end, no middle and no beginning to you.
verses.hi: मैं आपको हर तरफ़ अनंत रूपों में, अनगिनत भुजाओं, पेटों, मुखों और आँखों के साथ देख रहा हूँ। हे विश्वेश्वर, हे विश्वरूप, मुझे आपका न अंत दिखता है, न मध्य, न आदि।
verses.short: "Endless arms, faces and eyes everywhere. I can't find your beginning, middle or end."
verses.notes: What can't Arjuna find? The beginning, middle or end of this form. Why? Because it is truly infinite.

verses.en: I see you with crown, mace and discus, a mass of light shining everywhere, hard to look at, blazing like fire and sun on all sides, beyond measure.
verses.hi: मैं आपको मुकुट, गदा और चक्र के साथ, हर तरफ़ चमकते तेज के पुंज के रूप में देख रहा हूँ, जिसे देखना कठिन है, जो आग और सूरज की तरह हर ओर दमक रहा है और अपार है।
verses.short: "You're a mass of blazing light, like fire and the sun. Hard to even look at."
verses.notes: How does the form appear? As a mass of light shining everywhere, with crown, mace and discus, too bright to look at. Why mention crown, mace and discus? They link the cosmic form to the familiar form of Vishnu.

verses.en: You are the imperishable, the highest to be known. You are the final resting place of this universe. You are the unchanging guardian of eternal dharma. I believe you are the timeless Supreme Being.
verses.hi: आप ही जानने योग्य परम अक्षर हैं। आप ही इस विश्व का परम आधार हैं। आप ही सनातन धर्म के अविनाशी रक्षक हैं। मेरे मत में आप ही सनातन पुरुष हैं।
verses.short: "You're the eternal, the highest truth, the support of everything, the protector of what's right."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna realise? Krishna is the Imperishable, the support of the universe and protector of eternal dharma. What has changed? Arjuna now knows, not just believes.

verses.en: I see you without beginning, middle or end, with endless power and countless arms, the sun and moon as your eyes, your mouth a blazing fire, heating this universe with your radiance.
verses.hi: मैं आपको आदि, मध्य और अंत से रहित, अनंत शक्ति और अनगिनत भुजाओं वाला देख रहा हूँ। सूरज और चाँद आपकी आँखें हैं, आपका मुख जलती आग है, और आप अपने तेज से इस विश्व को तपा रहे हैं।
verses.short: "No beginning, no end, infinite power. Sun and moon are your eyes. Your fire heats the universe."
verses.notes: What are Krishna's eyes in this form? The sun and the moon. What else does Arjuna see? Infinite power and a blazing fire that heats the whole universe.

verses.en: The space between heaven and earth, and every direction, is filled by you alone. Great one, seeing this wondrous and terrifying form of yours, the three worlds tremble.
verses.hi: धरती और आकाश के बीच का सारा स्थान और सब दिशाएँ अकेले आपसे भरी हैं। हे महात्मा, आपके इस अद्भुत और भयानक रूप को देखकर तीनों लोक काँप रहे हैं।
verses.short: "You fill the space between earth and sky. All three worlds are shaking at this sight."
verses.notes: How large is the form? It fills the space between heaven and earth and all directions. How do the worlds react? They tremble at this wondrous and fearsome form.

verses.en: Hosts of gods are entering you. Some, afraid, praise you with joined palms. Great sages and perfected beings cry "May all be well!" and praise you with rich hymns.
verses.hi: देवताओं के समूह आपमें प्रवेश कर रहे हैं। कुछ डरकर हाथ जोड़े आपकी स्तुति कर रहे हैं। महर्षि और सिद्ध "कल्याण हो" कहकर भरपूर स्तुतियों से आपका गुणगान कर रहे हैं।
verses.short: "Gods are entering you. Some, afraid, pray with folded hands. Sages sing your praises."
verses.notes: What are the gods doing? Entering Krishna; some in fear praise him with folded hands. And the sages? They say 'May all be well' and sing his praises.

verses.en: The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, the two Ashvins, the wind gods, the ancestors, and hosts of gandharvas, yakshas, demons and perfected beings all gaze at you in amazement.
verses.hi: रुद्र, आदित्य, वसु, साध्य, विश्वेदेव, दोनों अश्विनी कुमार, मरुत, पितर, और गंधर्वों, यक्षों, असुरों और सिद्धों के समूह, सब हैरान होकर आपको देख रहे हैं।
verses.short: "Every kind of divine being is staring at you in total amazement."
verses.notes: Who is watching in amazement? Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Ashvins, Maruts, ancestors, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras and Siddhas. What does this show? All of existence is in awe of the Divine.

verses.en: Mighty one, seeing your vast form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs and feet, many bellies and terrible teeth, the worlds tremble, and so do I.
verses.hi: हे महाबाहु, अनेक मुखों और आँखों, अनेक भुजाओं, जाँघों और पैरों, अनेक पेटों और भयानक दाँतों वाले आपके विशाल रूप को देखकर सब लोग घबरा रहे हैं, और मैं भी।
verses.short: "So many mouths, eyes, arms and terrifying teeth. The worlds are trembling, and so am I."
verses.notes: Why does the form become frightening? It has countless mouths, eyes, arms and terrible teeth. How do the worlds feel? Terrified, and so is Arjuna.

verses.en: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colours, mouths wide open and huge eyes shining, my heart trembles, Vishnu. I find no courage and no peace.
verses.hi: हे विष्णु, आकाश को छूते, कई रंगों में दमकते, मुँह फैलाए और बड़ी चमकती आँखों वाले आपको देखकर मेरा मन काँप रहा है। मुझे न धीरज मिल रहा है, न शांति।
verses.short: "You're touching the sky, blazing in every colour. I'm shaking inside and can't find calm."
verses.notes: What is happening to Arjuna? His heart trembles; he loses courage and peace. Why share this fear? It's an honest picture of facing the infinite.

verses.en: Seeing your mouths with terrible teeth, blazing like the fire at the end of time, I lose all sense of direction and find no comfort. Have mercy, Lord of gods, home of the universe.
verses.hi: भयानक दाँतों वाले और प्रलय की आग जैसे दहकते आपके मुखों को देखकर मुझे दिशाओं का पता नहीं चल रहा और चैन नहीं मिल रहा। हे देवेश, हे जगन्निवास, प्रसन्न होइए।
verses.short: "Your mouths look like the fire at the end of time. I'm lost. Please, have mercy."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna see in the mouths? Fangs like the fire at the end of time. How does he feel? Lost, unable to find his bearings or peace.

verses.en: All these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with hosts of kings, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, along with our own leading warriors too,
verses.hi: धृतराष्ट्र के ये सब पुत्र, राजाओं के समूहों के साथ, भीष्म, द्रोण और कर्ण, और हमारी तरफ़ के प्रमुख योद्धा भी,
verses.short: "I see Duryodhana's brothers, Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and our warriors too..."
verses.notes: Who does Arjuna see entering the mouths? Dhritarashtra's sons, Bhishma, Drona, Karna and warriors from both sides. What does this mean? Arjuna is shown the outcome of the war before it happens.

verses.en: are rushing into your terrifying mouths with their dreadful teeth. Some are seen caught between your teeth, their heads crushed.
verses.hi: आपके भयानक दाँतों वाले डरावने मुखों में तेज़ी से घुस रहे हैं। कुछ आपके दाँतों के बीच फँसे दिख रहे हैं, जिनके सिर चूर हो गए हैं।
verses.short: "...rushing into your terrifying mouths and being crushed." Arjuna sees the outcome before the battle.
verses.notes: What happens to them? They rush into the terrible mouths; some are crushed between the teeth. Why such a harsh image? It shows the power of time that ends everything.

verses.en: As the many currents of rivers rush towards the ocean, these heroes of the human world are entering your blazing mouths.
verses.hi: जैसे नदियों की कई धाराएँ समुद्र की ओर दौड़ती हैं, वैसे ही इस मनुष्य-लोक के ये वीर आपके दहकते मुखों में प्रवेश कर रहे हैं।
verses.short: "Like rivers rushing into the ocean, these heroes are flowing into your blazing mouths."
verses.notes: What is the river example? Like rivers rushing into the ocean, warriors enter Krishna's flaming mouths. What does it suggest? Their end is as natural and certain as rivers reaching the sea.

verses.en: As moths rush at full speed into a blazing fire to their destruction, these people are rushing at full speed into your mouths to their destruction.
verses.hi: जैसे पतंगे पूरी तेज़ी से जलती आग में मरने के लिए घुसते हैं, वैसे ही ये लोग भी पूरी तेज़ी से नष्ट होने के लिए आपके मुखों में घुस रहे हैं।
verses.short: "Like moths flying into a flame, they're rushing to their end."
verses.notes: What is the moth example? Like moths rushing into a flame, people rush to their destruction. What's different from the river image? Moths are drawn by their own desire, like people pulled by their choices.

verses.en: Devouring all the worlds on every side with your flaming mouths, you lick your lips. Your fierce rays fill the whole universe with light and scorch it, Vishnu.
verses.hi: हे विष्णु, अपने जलते मुखों से हर ओर से सारे लोकों को निगलते हुए आप होंठ चाट रहे हैं। आपकी तीखी किरणें पूरे जगत को तेज से भरकर तपा रही हैं।
verses.short: "You're swallowing the worlds with your flaming mouths. Your rays are burning up the universe."
verses.notes: What is the form doing? Devouring the worlds with flaming mouths, its fierce rays filling the universe. What does this represent? Time consuming all things.

verses.en: Tell me, who are you in this fierce form? I bow to you, greatest of gods. Have mercy. I want to know you, the original one, because I don't understand what you are doing.
verses.hi: मुझे बताइए, इस भयानक रूप में आप कौन हैं? हे देवश्रेष्ठ, आपको नमस्कार है, प्रसन्न होइए। मैं आप आदि पुरुष को जानना चाहता हूँ, क्योंकि मैं आपका यह कार्य नहीं समझ पा रहा।
verses.short: "Who are you in this terrifying form? Please be kind. I want to understand you."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask? 'Who are you, in this fierce form?' He wants to understand Krishna's purpose. Why ask now? The form is so overwhelming he no longer recognises his friend.

verses.en: Krishna said: I am Time, the mighty destroyer of worlds, come here to wipe out these people. Even without you, none of these warriors lined up in the opposing armies will survive.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: मैं लोकों का नाश करने वाला बढ़ा हुआ काल हूँ, और यहाँ इन लोगों को खत्म करने आया हूँ। तुम्हारे बिना भी विरोधी सेनाओं में खड़े ये सारे योद्धा नहीं बचेंगे।
verses.short: Krishna: "I am Time, the destroyer of worlds. Even without you, these warriors won't survive."
verses.notes: Who does Krishna say he is? 'I am Time, the mighty destroyer of worlds.' What does he say about the warriors? Even without Arjuna, they will not survive.

verses.en: So stand up and win glory. Defeat your enemies and enjoy a thriving kingdom. They have already been slain by me. Be just the instrument, Arjuna.
verses.hi: इसलिए उठो और यश पाओ। शत्रुओं को जीतकर समृद्ध राज्य भोगो। इन्हें मैं पहले ही मार चुका हूँ। हे सव्यसाची, तुम बस निमित्त बन जाओ।
verses.short: "So rise and win. I've already decided the outcome. You're just the instrument."
verses.notes: What does 'be merely an instrument' mean? The outcome is already decided; Arjuna is only the means. How can this help us? Do your part fully, but don't carry the weight of the whole outcome.

verses.en: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and the other great warriors have already been slain by me. Kill them, don't be afraid. Fight, and you will defeat your rivals in battle.
verses.hi: द्रोण, भीष्म, जयद्रथ, कर्ण और दूसरे वीर योद्धाओं को मैं पहले ही मार चुका हूँ। तुम उन्हें मारो, घबराओ मत। युद्ध करो, तुम युद्ध में शत्रुओं को जीतोगे।
verses.short: "Their fate is sealed. Don't be distressed. Fight, and you'll win."
verses.notes: What does Krishna tell Arjuna to do? Fight Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha and Karna, who are already slain by him. What reassurance is given? 'Don't be distressed. You will win.'

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Hearing Krishna's words, Arjuna, trembling and with joined palms, bowed again and, terrified, spoke to Krishna in a choked voice.
verses.hi: संजय ने कहा: केशव के ये वचन सुनकर काँपते हुए, हाथ जोड़े अर्जुन ने फिर प्रणाम किया और बहुत डरा हुआ, भर्राई आवाज़ में श्रीकृष्ण से बोला।
verses.short: Arjuna, trembling and emotional, bows again and again and speaks with folded hands.
verses.notes: How does Arjuna respond? Trembling, he bows again and speaks with folded hands, his voice choked. Who reports this? Sanjaya, to Dhritarashtra.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, it is right that the world rejoices and delights in praising you. Demons flee in fear in all directions, and all the perfected beings bow to you.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे हृषीकेश, यह ठीक ही है कि आपका गुणगान करके दुनिया खुश होती है और प्रेम से भर जाती है। डरे हुए राक्षस सब दिशाओं में भाग रहे हैं और सिद्धों के सारे समूह आपको नमस्कार कर रहे हैं।
verses.short: "No wonder the world celebrates you. Negativity runs away, and the wise bow to you."
verses.notes: How does the world respond to Krishna? It rejoices in his praise; the wicked flee in fear and the perfected bow. What does Arjuna say? That this is fitting.

verses.en: And why shouldn't they bow to you, great one, greater even than Brahma, the first creator? Endless Lord of gods, home of the universe, you are the imperishable, what is and what is not, and what lies beyond both.
verses.hi: और हे महात्मा, वे आपको नमस्कार क्यों न करें, आप तो आदि-रचयिता ब्रह्मा से भी बड़े हैं। हे अनंत, हे देवेश, हे जगन्निवास, आप अक्षर हैं, सत् और असत् हैं, और उनसे परे भी जो है, वह आप ही हैं।
verses.short: "Why wouldn't they bow? You're the creator of even the creator. Infinite, Lord of gods."
verses.notes: Why should all bow to Krishna? He is the first creator, greater even than Brahma. What does Arjuna call him? Infinite, Lord of gods, home of the universe, beyond being and non-being.

verses.en: You are the first God, the ancient Being, the final resting place of this universe. You are the knower and what is to be known, the highest home. Endless one, the universe is pervaded by you.
verses.hi: आप आदिदेव, पुरातन पुरुष और इस विश्व के परम आधार हैं। आप ही जानने वाले हैं, जानने योग्य हैं और परम धाम हैं। हे अनंतरूप, यह विश्व आपसे व्याप्त है।
verses.short: "You're the first God, the ancient one, the resting place of the universe, the knower and the known."
verses.notes: How does Arjuna praise Krishna here? As the first God, the ancient Person, the resting place of the universe. What else? The knower, the known and the supreme abode.

verses.en: You are the wind, death, fire, the water god, the moon, the father of beings and the great-grandfather. I bow to you a thousand times, and again and again I bow to you.
verses.hi: आप ही वायु, यम, अग्नि, वरुण, चंद्रमा, प्रजापति और प्रपितामह हैं। आपको हज़ारों बार नमस्कार है, और फिर बार-बार नमस्कार है।
verses.short: "You're wind, fire, water, the moon, the creator. A thousand salutes to you, again and again."
verses.notes: Which gods does Arjuna say Krishna is? Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati and the great-grandfather. How does he respond? 'Salutations to you a thousand times, again and again.'

verses.en: I bow to you in front and behind, I bow to you on every side, you who are everything. Your strength is endless and your might is boundless. You pervade everything, so you are everything.
verses.hi: आपको आगे से नमस्कार, पीछे से नमस्कार, हे सर्वरूप, हर ओर से नमस्कार। आपकी शक्ति अनंत है और पराक्रम अपार है। आप सबमें व्याप्त हैं, इसलिए आप ही सब कुछ हैं।
verses.short: "Salutes from the front, from behind, from every side. You're everything, infinite in power."
verses.notes: Why bow in every direction? Krishna is everywhere, so Arjuna bows to him from front, back and all sides. What does Arjuna say Krishna is? Everything, of infinite power.

verses.en: Thinking of you as a friend, I carelessly called you "Hey Krishna, hey Yadava, hey buddy," not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or affection.
verses.hi: आपको मित्र मानकर, आपकी इस महिमा को न जानते हुए, लापरवाही से या प्रेम से मैंने जो "हे कृष्ण, हे यादव, हे सखा" कहा,
verses.short: "I called you 'buddy' and 'Krishna' casually, not knowing who you really are..."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna regret? Casually calling Krishna 'friend' or 'Yadava' without knowing his greatness. Was Arjuna wrong? Not really. His closeness came from love. But seeing Krishna's greatness makes him humble.

verses.en: And if I ever disrespected you in jest, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, I ask your forgiveness, immeasurable one.
verses.hi: और हे अच्युत, अगर मज़ाक में, खेलते, सोते, बैठते या खाते समय, अकेले में या दूसरों के सामने मैंने आपका अपमान किया हो, तो हे अपार प्रभु, मैं आपसे क्षमा माँगता हूँ।
verses.short: "...and joked around with you while eating and hanging out. Please forgive me." Best friend realising his friend is God.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask forgiveness for? Any disrespect in jokes, play, rest, sitting or eating, alone or with others. What does this teach? Real friendship also includes respect.

verses.en: You are the father of the whole world, moving and unmoving. You are its object of worship and its greatest teacher. No one equals you in the three worlds; how could anyone be greater, you of unmatched power?
verses.hi: आप इस चर-अचर जगत के पिता हैं, पूजनीय हैं और सबसे बड़े गुरु हैं। हे अतुलनीय प्रभाव वाले, तीनों लोकों में आपके बराबर भी कोई नहीं, फिर आपसे बड़ा कहाँ से होगा?
verses.short: "You're the father of the world, the greatest teacher. No one equals you, let alone surpasses you."
verses.notes: What is Krishna to the world? Its father, its greatest teacher and most worthy of worship. Is anyone equal to him? None in all three worlds.

verses.en: So I bow down and lay my body before you, and ask your grace, adorable Lord. As a father forgives a son, a friend a friend, a lover the beloved, please forgive me.
verses.hi: इसलिए मैं शरीर को झुकाकर आपको प्रणाम करता हूँ और आप पूजनीय ईश्वर से कृपा माँगता हूँ। जैसे पिता पुत्र को, मित्र मित्र को और प्रिय अपने प्रिय को क्षमा करता है, वैसे ही हे देव, मुझे क्षमा कीजिए।
verses.short: "I bow down completely. Forgive me like a father forgives a son, a friend a friend."
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask for? Forgiveness, as a father forgives a son, a friend a friend, a lover the beloved. What do these examples show? The Divine relates to us with love in many ways.

verses.en: I am thrilled to have seen what no one has seen before, but my mind is shaken with fear. Show me your familiar form again, God. Have mercy, Lord of gods, home of the universe.
verses.hi: जो पहले कभी नहीं देखा, उसे देखकर मैं रोमांचित हूँ, पर मेरा मन डर से व्याकुल है। हे देव, मुझे फिर से अपना वही रूप दिखाइए। हे देवेश, हे जगन्निवास, प्रसन्न होइए।
verses.short: "I'm thrilled but also scared. Please show me your familiar form again."
verses.notes: How does Arjuna feel now? Thrilled to have seen it, but his mind is shaken with fear. What does he ask? To see Krishna's gentle, familiar form again.

verses.en: I want to see you as before, with crown, mace and discus in hand. Thousand-armed one, universal form, take your four-armed form again.
verses.hi: मैं आपको पहले की तरह मुकुट, गदा और हाथ में चक्र लिए देखना चाहता हूँ। हे हज़ार भुजाओं वाले, हे विश्वमूर्ति, फिर से अपने चार भुजाओं वाले रूप में आ जाइए।
verses.short: "I want to see you with your crown, mace and discus, in your four-armed form."
verses.notes: Which form does Arjuna want to see? The four-armed form with crown, mace and discus. Why that form? It's divine but gentle and approachable.

verses.en: Krishna said: Arjuna, out of my grace and by my own power, I have shown you this supreme form, radiant, universal, endless and original, which no one but you has seen before.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे अर्जुन, मैंने प्रसन्न होकर अपनी योग-शक्ति से तुम्हें यह परम, तेजस्वी, विश्वरूप, अनंत और आदि रूप दिखाया है, जिसे तुम्हारे सिवा पहले किसी ने नहीं देखा।
verses.short: Krishna: "Out of love I showed you this form. No one but you has ever seen it."
verses.notes: Why was Arjuna shown this form? Out of Krishna's grace. No one else had seen it before. What makes it special? It's the radiant, infinite, primal form.

verses.en: Not by the Vedas, sacrifices or study, not by charity, rituals or severe austerities can anyone in the human world see me in this form, except you, hero of the Kurus.
verses.hi: हे कुरुवीर, न वेदों से, न यज्ञ और अध्ययन से, न दान से, न कर्मकांड से और न कठोर तप से, इंसानी दुनिया में तुम्हारे सिवा कोई मुझे इस रूप में देख सकता है।
verses.short: "Not scriptures, rituals, charity or hard discipline can show this form. Only grace."
verses.notes: Can study or rituals reveal this form? No. Not by Vedas, sacrifice, study, charity, rituals or austerity. Then how did Arjuna see it? By grace, given out of love.

verses.en: Don't be afraid or confused after seeing this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and with a happy heart, see my familiar form again.
verses.hi: मेरे इस भयानक रूप को देखकर न डरो, न घबराओ। डर छोड़कर और प्रसन्न मन से फिर मेरे उसी रूप को देखो।
verses.short: "Don't be scared or confused. Relax, and look at my familiar form again."
verses.notes: What does Krishna tell the frightened Arjuna? Don't be afraid or confused. With a calm heart, see my familiar form again. What does this show about Krishna? He is caring as well as mighty.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Having said this, Krishna showed Arjuna his own form again. The great one, taking his gentle form once more, comforted the frightened Arjuna.
verses.hi: संजय ने कहा: अर्जुन से ऐसा कहकर वासुदेव ने उसे फिर अपना रूप दिखाया। उन महात्मा ने फिर से सौम्य रूप धारण करके डरे हुए अर्जुन को धीरज बँधाया।
verses.short: Krishna returns to his gentle human form and comforts the shaken Arjuna.
verses.notes: What does Krishna do next? He returns to his gentle form and comforts Arjuna. Who narrates this? Sanjaya, to Dhritarashtra.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, seeing this gentle human form of yours, I am calm again and myself once more.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे जनार्दन, आपका यह सौम्य मानव रूप देखकर अब मैं शांत हो गया हूँ और फिर से अपने स्वभाव में आ गया हूँ।
verses.short: Arjuna: "Seeing your human form again, I feel calm and like myself."
verses.notes: How does Arjuna feel now? Calm again, back to his normal self. Why does the human form comfort him? It's the form he knows and loves.

verses.en: Krishna said: The form of mine you have seen is very hard to see. Even the gods always long to see this form.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: मेरा जो रूप तुमने देखा, उसके दर्शन बहुत कठिन हैं। देवता भी हमेशा इस रूप के दर्शन के लिए तरसते हैं।
verses.short: "Even the gods long to see the form you just saw. It's incredibly rare."
verses.notes: How rare is this vision? Very rare. Even the gods long to see it. What does this tell us about Arjuna? He received an extraordinary grace.

verses.en: Not by the Vedas, nor austerity, nor charity, nor sacrifice can I be seen as you have seen me.
verses.hi: मुझे इस रूप में, जैसे तुमने देखा, वेद पढ़कर, तप करके, दान देकर या यज्ञ करके कोई नहीं देख पाता।
verses.short: "Not through study, discipline, charity or rituals can anyone see me like that."
verses.notes: What can't reveal this form? Not Vedas, austerity, charity or sacrifice. Why repeat this? To set up the answer in the next verse: devotion.

verses.en: But by undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known like this, seen as I truly am, and entered into.
verses.hi: पर हे अर्जुन, अनन्य भक्ति से मुझे इस रूप में जाना जा सकता है, सच में देखा जा सकता है, और हे परंतप, मुझमें प्रवेश भी किया जा सकता है।
verses.short: "Only through pure, single-minded love can someone truly know, see and become one with me."
verses.notes: How can the Divine truly be known? Through single-minded devotion: to know, see and enter into him. Why devotion above everything? Love opens what effort alone can't.

verses.en: Whoever works for me, makes me their goal, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without hatred towards any being, comes to me, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पांडव, जो मेरे लिए कर्म करता है, मुझे ही लक्ष्य मानता है, मेरा भक्त है, आसक्ति से मुक्त है और किसी प्राणी से वैर नहीं रखता, वह मुझे पाता है।
verses.short: Work for me, make me your goal, love me, drop attachments and hate no one. That's how you reach me.
verses.notes: Who reaches Krishna? One who works for him, sees him as supreme, is devoted, unattached and without hatred toward any being. Why is this verse a summary? It sums up the whole path: action, devotion, detachment and kindness.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Some devotees are always devoted and worship you; others worship the imperishable, unseen. Which of them knows yoga best?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: कुछ भक्त हमेशा आपसे जुड़कर आपकी उपासना करते हैं, और कुछ अविनाशी, अदृश्य ब्रह्म की। इनमें योग को सबसे अच्छी तरह कौन जानता है?
verses.short: Arjuna: "Who's doing it better, those who love you in a personal form or those who meditate on the formless?"
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask? Who is the better yogi: one who worships Krishna in form, or one who meditates on the formless? Why is this question important? It's a choice many seekers face.

verses.en: Krishna said: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, always devoted and full of deep faith, I consider the most united with me.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: जो मुझमें मन लगाकर, हमेशा मुझसे जुड़े रहकर और पूरी श्रद्धा से मेरी उपासना करते हैं, उन्हें मैं सबसे श्रेष्ठ योगी मानता हूँ।
verses.short: Krishna: "Those who focus on me with full faith and love, I consider the best."
verses.notes: Whom does Krishna consider the best? Those who fix their minds on him with steady devotion and supreme faith. Why? Devotion to a personal form is direct and heartfelt.

verses.en: But those who worship the imperishable, which can't be described, is unseen, everywhere, beyond thought, unchanging, unmoving and constant,
verses.hi: पर जो उस अक्षर की उपासना करते हैं जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, जो अदृश्य, सर्वव्यापी, सोच से परे, अपरिवर्तनीय, अचल और स्थिर है,
verses.short: "Those who meditate on the formless, infinite and unchanging..."
verses.notes: What about worshippers of the formless? Those who meditate on the indescribable, unmanifest, all-pervading Absolute. How is the formless described? Unthinkable, unchanging, unmoving and eternal.

verses.en: controlling all the senses, even-minded everywhere and devoted to the good of all beings, they too reach me.
verses.hi: सब इंद्रियों को वश में करके, हर जगह समान बुद्धि रखकर और सब प्राणियों की भलाई में लगे रहकर, वे भी मुझे ही पाते हैं।
verses.short: "...with self-control, balance and care for everyone, also reach me."
verses.notes: Do worshippers of the formless also reach Krishna? Yes, if they control their senses, stay even-minded and work for all beings' good. So both paths work? Yes. Both lead to the same goal.

verses.en: But the struggle is greater for those whose minds are set on the unseen. The path of the unseen is hard for embodied beings to walk.
verses.hi: पर जिनका मन अदृश्य में लगा है, उनकी राह ज़्यादा कठिन है। शरीरधारियों के लिए अदृश्य का मार्ग मुश्किल से तय होता है।
verses.short: But the formless path is much harder. It's tough for humans to connect with something abstract.
verses.notes: Why is the formless path harder? Embodied beings find it hard to focus on something with no form. Is it wrong to choose it? Not wrong, just more difficult.

verses.en: But those who offer all their actions to me, make me their goal, and worship me by meditating on me with single-minded devotion,
verses.hi: पर जो अपने सारे कर्म मुझे अर्पित करके, मुझे लक्ष्य मानकर, अनन्य भक्ति से मेरा ध्यान करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं,
verses.short: Those who dedicate everything to me, make me their goal and meditate on me with love...
verses.notes: What do devoted worshippers do? They offer all actions to Krishna, see him as the goal and meditate on him with single-minded devotion. What makes this path easier? Love gives the mind a natural focus.

verses.en: for them, Arjuna, whose minds are absorbed in me, I soon become the rescuer from the ocean of death and rebirth.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, मुझमें मन लगाने वाले उन लोगों को मैं जल्दी ही मृत्यु और संसार के सागर से पार निकाल देता हूँ।
verses.short: ...I quickly pull them out of the ocean of struggle. I've got them.
verses.notes: What does Krishna promise his devotees? He soon lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth. Why is this comforting? The devotee isn't alone; the Divine actively saves.

verses.en: Keep your mind on me alone and let your understanding rest in me. Then you will live in me. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hi: अपना मन केवल मुझमें लगाओ और बुद्धि मुझमें टिकाओ। उसके बाद तुम मुझमें ही रहोगे, इसमें कोई संदेह नहीं।
verses.short: Keep your mind and thoughts on me, and you'll live in me. No doubt.
verses.notes: What is the highest practice? Fix your mind and intellect on Krishna alone. What is the result? You will live in him, without doubt.

verses.en: If you can't keep your mind steady on me, Arjuna, then try to reach me through the practice of regular focus.
verses.hi: हे धनंजय, अगर तुम अपना मन मुझमें स्थिर नहीं रख पाते, तो अभ्यास-योग के ज़रिए मुझे पाने की कोशिश करो।
verses.short: Can't focus on me constantly? Then practise. Bring your mind back, again and again.
verses.notes: What if I can't keep my mind on God? Then practise. Keep bringing the mind back again and again. Is practice enough? Yes. Repeated effort leads to him.

verses.en: If you can't even practise, then make working for me your highest aim. Even by doing things for my sake, you will reach perfection.
verses.hi: अगर तुम अभ्यास भी नहीं कर पाते, तो मेरे लिए कर्म करने को ही सबसे बड़ा लक्ष्य बना लो। मेरे लिए कर्म करके भी तुम सिद्धि पा लोगे।
verses.short: Can't practise regularly? Then just do your work for me. That alone gets you there.
verses.notes: What if even practice is too hard? Then do your work for Krishna's sake. Will that work? Yes. Krishna says this alone brings perfection.

verses.en: And if you can't do even this, then, taking refuge in me and with self-control, let go of the results of all your actions.
verses.hi: और अगर यह भी नहीं कर पाते, तो मेरी शरण लेकर और मन को वश में रखकर सारे कर्मों के फल का त्याग कर दो।
verses.short: Can't even do that? Then just let go of the results of what you do. Start there.
verses.notes: What if even that isn't possible? Then simply let go of the results of your actions, with self-control. Why does Krishna give so many options? So everyone can start where they are.

verses.en: Knowledge is better than mechanical practice, meditation is better than knowledge, and letting go of results is better than meditation. Peace follows right after letting go.
verses.hi: बिना समझ के अभ्यास से ज्ञान बेहतर है, ज्ञान से ध्यान बेहतर है, और ध्यान से कर्म-फल का त्याग बेहतर है। त्याग से तुरंत शांति मिलती है।
verses.short: Understanding beats mechanical practice, meditation beats understanding, and letting go of results brings instant peace.
verses.notes: What is ranked highest here? Knowledge is better than practice, meditation better than knowledge, and letting go of results better than meditation. Why is letting go best? Peace follows immediately.

verses.en: Someone who hates no being, is friendly and compassionate, free from "mine" and ego, the same in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,
verses.hi: जो किसी प्राणी से नफ़रत नहीं करता, सबका मित्र और दयालु है, "मेरेपन" और अहंकार से मुक्त है, सुख-दुख में एक जैसा और क्षमाशील है,
verses.short: No hate, always kind, no ego, calm through ups and downs, forgiving. That person is dear to me.
verses.notes: What qualities make a devotee dear to Krishna? No hatred toward anyone, friendliness, compassion, no ego, even in pleasure and pain, and forgiving. Can these be practised? Yes. Each one can be grown little by little.

verses.en: always content, steady in yoga, self-controlled and firm in resolve, with mind and understanding offered to me: that devotee is dear to me.
verses.hi: हमेशा संतुष्ट, योग में स्थित, संयमी और पक्के निश्चय वाला है, और जिसने मन और बुद्धि मुझे अर्पित कर दी है, ऐसा भक्त मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.short: Content, disciplined, determined, mind and heart given to me. That person is dear to me.
verses.notes: What more qualities are listed? Content, steady in practice, self-controlled, firm, with mind and intellect given to Krishna. What ties them together? A heart turned fully toward the Divine.

verses.en: Someone who doesn't disturb the world and isn't disturbed by it, who is free from excitement, envy, fear and anxiety, is dear to me.
verses.hi: जिससे दुनिया परेशान नहीं होती और जो दुनिया से परेशान नहीं होता, जो खुशी के उछाल, ईर्ष्या, डर और घबराहट से मुक्त है, वह मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.short: They don't disturb anyone, and no one disturbs them. Free from excitement, fear and stress. Dear to me.
verses.notes: What does 'not disturbing the world' mean? Others feel safe around them, and they aren't disturbed by others. What are they free from? Excitement, envy, fear and anxiety.

verses.en: Someone who expects nothing, is pure, capable, unbiased and untroubled, and has given up all self-serving projects: that devotee is dear to me.
verses.hi: जो किसी से कुछ उम्मीद नहीं रखता, पवित्र है, कुशल है, निष्पक्ष है, बेफ़िक्र है और जिसने स्वार्थ के सारे काम छोड़ दिए हैं, ऐसा भक्त मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.short: No neediness, clean inside, skilled, unbothered, not chasing every new project. Dear to me.
verses.notes: What qualities are named here? Free from expectation, pure, capable, impartial, untroubled, and not driven by selfish projects. What does 'capable' mean? Skilful and ready to do what's needed.

verses.en: Someone who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, and has let go of both good and bad: that devoted person is dear to me.
verses.hi: जो न खुशी से उछलता है, न नफ़रत करता है, न शोक करता है, न लालसा रखता है, और जिसने शुभ-अशुभ दोनों छोड़ दिए हैं, ऐसा भक्त मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.short: Not overly happy, hateful, sad or greedy. Beyond good and bad, full of love for me. Dear to me.
verses.notes: How does the devotee handle highs and lows? They don't overly rejoice, hate, grieve or crave. What does 'renouncing good and evil' mean? Letting go of attachment to both pleasant and unpleasant results.

verses.en: Someone who is the same towards enemy and friend, in honour and insult, in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and is free from attachment,
verses.hi: जो शत्रु और मित्र, मान और अपमान, सर्दी-गर्मी और सुख-दुख में एक समान रहता है और आसक्ति से मुक्त है,
verses.short: Same with friends and enemies, respect and insult, heat and cold, pleasure and pain. No attachments.
verses.notes: How does the devotee treat friend and foe? The same, and the same in honour and insult, heat and cold, pleasure and pain. What is the root of this? Freedom from attachment.

verses.en: who takes blame and praise alike, speaks little, is content with whatever comes, isn't tied to a home, and has a steady mind: that devoted person is dear to me.
verses.hi: जो निंदा और प्रशंसा को एक जैसा मानता है, कम बोलता है, जो मिले उसमें संतुष्ट रहता है, किसी घर से बँधा नहीं और जिसकी बुद्धि स्थिर है, ऐसा भक्त इंसान मुझे प्रिय है।
verses.short: Praise or criticism, same reaction. Speaks less, content with whatever, steady and devoted. Dear to me.
verses.notes: How does the devotee react to praise and blame? Equally. They are quiet, content with whatever comes, and steady. What does 'no home' mean? Not clinging to any place as their own.

verses.en: But those who follow this nectar of right living as I have described it, with faith and with me as their goal, are extremely dear to me.
verses.hi: पर जो श्रद्धा से और मुझे लक्ष्य मानकर, मेरे बताए इस धर्ममय अमृत का पालन करते हैं, वे भक्त मुझे बहुत ही प्रिय हैं।
verses.short: Those who live these values with faith and make me their goal are the dearest of all to me.
verses.notes: Who is most dear to Krishna? Those who follow these teachings with faith, holding him as supreme. Why call it 'nectar'? Living these qualities brings deep, lasting joy.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, I want to understand nature and spirit, the field and the knower of the field, and knowledge and what is to be known.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे केशव, मुझे समझाइए कि प्रकृति और पुरुष क्या हैं, क्षेत्र और उसे जानने वाला क्या हैं, और ज्ञान क्या है और किसे जानना है।
verses.short: Arjuna wants to understand the basics: the body, the soul, and how knowing really works.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna want to learn? About nature and spirit, the field and its knower, knowledge and what is to be known. Why do these topics matter? They explain what we are and what the world is.

verses.en: Krishna said: Arjuna, this body is called the field. Those who know the truth call whoever knows it the knower of the field.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे कौन्तेय, इस शरीर को क्षेत्र कहते हैं। जो इसे जानता है, उसे सत्य जानने वाले क्षेत्रज्ञ कहते हैं।
verses.short: Krishna: "Your body is the field. The one who knows the body is the knower of the field."
verses.notes: What is the 'field'? The body. Everything that can be observed. Who is the 'knower of the field'? The awareness that knows the body: the Self.

verses.en: Know me as the knower in all fields, Arjuna. Understanding the field and its knower is what I consider true knowledge.
verses.hi: हे भारत, हर शरीर रूपी क्षेत्र को भीतर से जानने वाला मैं ही हूँ। शरीर और उसे जानने वाले के फ़र्क को समझ लेना ही मेरी नज़र में सच्चा ज्ञान है।
verses.short: "I'm the knower in every body. Understanding the body and the knower is real knowledge."
verses.notes: Who is the knower in all bodies? Krishna says he is the knower in every field. What is true knowledge? Knowing the difference between the field and its knower.

verses.en: Hear from me briefly what the field is, what it is like, how it changes and where it comes from, and who the knower is and what powers it has.
verses.hi: मुझसे संक्षेप में सुनो कि वह क्षेत्र क्या है, कैसा है, उसमें क्या बदलाव होते हैं और वह कहाँ से आता है, और क्षेत्रज्ञ कौन है और उसका क्या प्रभाव है।
verses.short: "Let me quickly explain what the body is, how it changes, and who the self is."
verses.notes: What will Krishna explain? What the field is, its nature, its changes, its origin, and who the knower is and his powers. Why 'briefly'? These are deep topics; he gives the essence.

verses.en: Sages have sung of this in many ways, in various hymns, and it is clearly set out with reasoning in the verses of the Brahma Sutras.
verses.hi: ऋषियों ने इसे कई तरह से, अलग-अलग छंदों में गाया है, और ब्रह्मसूत्र के तर्क भरे पदों में भी इसे साफ़ तय किया गया है।
verses.short: Sages have explained this in many ways, through hymns and solid logic.
verses.notes: Is this teaching new? No. Sages have described it in many ways, in hymns and in the Brahma Sutras. Why mention this? To show the teaching is supported by long tradition and reason.

verses.en: The great elements, ego, intellect and the unseen nature, the ten senses and the mind, and the five sense objects,
verses.hi: पाँच महाभूत, अहंकार, बुद्धि और अव्यक्त प्रकृति, दस इंद्रियाँ और मन, और इंद्रियों के पाँच विषय,
verses.short: The elements, ego, intellect, the senses and what they experience. That's the field.
verses.notes: What makes up the field? The great elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifest, the ten senses, the mind and the five sense objects. Why list these parts? To show that body and mind are all part of nature, not the Self.

verses.en: desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body, awareness and willpower: this, in brief, is the field with its changes.
verses.hi: इच्छा, द्वेष, सुख, दुख, शरीर, चेतना और धैर्य, संक्षेप में यही अपने बदलावों सहित क्षेत्र कहा गया है।
verses.short: Desire, hate, pleasure, pain and awareness are all part of the field, too.
verses.notes: What else belongs to the field? Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body, awareness and steadiness. Even emotions are part of the field? Yes. They are changes in nature, observed by the Self.

verses.en: Humility, honesty, non-violence, patience, straightforwardness, serving the teacher, cleanliness, steadiness and self-control,
verses.hi: विनम्रता, दिखावा न करना, अहिंसा, सहनशीलता, सरलता, गुरु की सेवा, पवित्रता, स्थिरता और आत्म-संयम,
verses.short: Real wisdom looks like humility, no showing off, non-violence, patience, honesty and respect for teachers.
verses.notes: What is true knowledge? Humility, honesty, non-violence, patience, sincerity, serving the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control. Why call qualities 'knowledge'? Real wisdom shows in how you live, not just what you know.

verses.en: detachment from sense objects, absence of ego, and seeing clearly the pain and flaws of birth, death, old age and sickness,
verses.hi: इंद्रियों के विषयों से वैराग्य, अहंकार न होना, और जन्म, मृत्यु, बुढ़ापे और बीमारी के दुख और दोषों को साफ़ देखना,
verses.short: Not chasing sense pleasures, no ego, and seeing clearly that birth, ageing and illness bring pain.
verses.notes: What more marks of knowledge are given? Detachment from sense objects, no ego, and seeing the pain in birth, death, old age and disease. Why reflect on suffering? It loosens attachment to passing things.

verses.en: non-attachment, not clinging to children, spouse, home and the like, and staying even-minded whether wanted or unwanted things happen,
verses.hi: आसक्ति न होना, बच्चों, पत्नी, घर आदि से चिपके न रहना, और मनचाहा या अनचाहा होने पर हमेशा मन को सम रखना,
verses.short: Not clinging to people and stuff, and staying balanced whether things go your way or not.
verses.notes: Does this mean not loving family? No. It means not clinging possessively to children, spouse or home. What is 'even-mindedness'? Staying balanced whether things go your way or not.

verses.en: unwavering devotion to me through undivided yoga, seeking quiet places and not enjoying crowds,
verses.hi: अनन्य योग से मुझमें अटल भक्ति, एकांत जगह में रहना और भीड़ में मन न लगना,
verses.short: Steady devotion, enjoying solitude, and not needing the crowd's approval.
verses.notes: What does devotion have to do with knowledge? Unwavering devotion to the Divine is itself a mark of knowledge. Why prefer quiet places? They help the mind turn inward.

verses.en: constant focus on knowledge of the self and seeing the purpose of knowing the truth: this is called knowledge. Everything opposite to it is ignorance.
verses.hi: आत्मा के ज्ञान में लगातार लगे रहना और तत्त्व-ज्ञान के उद्देश्य को देखना, इसे ज्ञान कहते हैं। इसके उलट जो कुछ है, वह अज्ञान है।
verses.short: Keep reflecting on who you really are and searching for truth. That's wisdom. The rest is ignorance.
verses.notes: What is the final mark of knowledge? Constant focus on self-knowledge and seeing the purpose of truth. What is ignorance? Everything opposite to these qualities.

verses.en: I will tell you what is to be known, knowing which one gains immortality. It is the beginningless Supreme, which is said to be neither being nor non-being.
verses.hi: अब मैं तुम्हें बताता हूँ कि जानने योग्य क्या है, जिसे जानकर अमरता मिलती है। वह अनादि परम ब्रह्म है, जिसे न सत् कहा जाता है, न असत्।
verses.short: Now, what's worth knowing: the eternal truth. Know it and you become immortal.
verses.notes: What is 'that which is to be known'? The beginningless Supreme Brahman, beyond being and non-being. What does knowing it bring? Immortality.

verses.en: Its hands and feet are everywhere, its eyes, heads and faces are everywhere, its ears are everywhere. It stands in the world, enveloping everything.
verses.hi: उसके हाथ-पैर हर जगह हैं, आँखें, सिर और मुख हर जगह हैं, कान हर जगह हैं। वह संसार में सबको घेरकर स्थित है।
verses.short: It has hands, feet, eyes and ears everywhere. It covers everything.
verses.notes: How is Brahman described? With hands, feet, eyes, heads, mouths and ears everywhere, pervading all. What does this image mean? The Supreme acts and perceives through every being.

verses.en: It shines through the functions of all the senses, yet is free of all senses. Unattached, it supports all. Beyond the qualities of nature, it still experiences them.
verses.hi: वह सब इंद्रियों के गुणों से झलकता है, फिर भी सब इंद्रियों से रहित है। अनासक्त होकर भी सबको धारण करता है। गुणों से परे होकर भी गुणों का अनुभव करता है।
verses.short: It powers the senses without having senses. It supports all but clings to nothing.
verses.notes: How can Brahman have senses and no senses? It shines through all senses but has none of its own; it supports all but is unattached. Why such paradoxes? The infinite can't be captured by ordinary logic.

verses.en: It is outside and inside all beings, unmoving and moving. Because it is subtle, it can't be grasped. It is far away and also near.
verses.hi: वह सब प्राणियों के बाहर भी है और भीतर भी, अचल भी है और चल भी। सूक्ष्म होने के कारण वह समझ में नहीं आता। वह दूर भी है और पास भी।
verses.short: It's inside and outside everything, still yet moving, far away yet really close.
verses.notes: Where is the Supreme? Inside and outside all beings, moving and unmoving, far and very near. Why is it hard to know? It's too subtle to be grasped by the senses.

verses.en: Undivided, it seems divided among beings. Know it as the one who sustains beings, who absorbs them and who creates them.
verses.hi: बँटा न होकर भी वह प्राणियों में बँटा हुआ-सा दिखता है। उसे प्राणियों का पालने वाला, उन्हें निगलने वाला और पैदा करने वाला जानो।
verses.short: It's one, but seems divided among beings. It creates, sustains and absorbs everything.
verses.notes: Is the Supreme divided? No. It is undivided, but seems divided among beings. What roles does it play? It sustains, absorbs and creates all beings.

verses.en: It is the light of all lights and is said to be beyond darkness. It is knowledge, what is to be known and the goal of knowledge, seated in the heart of all.
verses.hi: वह सब ज्योतियों की भी ज्योति है और अंधकार से परे कहा जाता है। वह ज्ञान है, जानने योग्य है और ज्ञान से पाने योग्य है, और सबके हृदय में स्थित है।
verses.short: It's the light behind all lights, beyond darkness, and it lives in every heart.
verses.notes: What is the 'light of lights'? The Supreme, which lights up everything and is beyond darkness. Where does it live? In the heart of all.

verses.en: So I have briefly described the field, knowledge and what is to be known. My devotee who understands this becomes worthy of my state of being.
verses.hi: इस तरह मैंने संक्षेप में क्षेत्र, ज्ञान और जानने योग्य के बारे में बताया। मेरा भक्त इसे समझकर मेरे स्वरूप को पाने के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.short: That's the field, wisdom and the truth, in short. Understand it and you're ready for me.
verses.notes: What has Krishna summed up? The field, knowledge and what is to be known. What happens to the devotee who understands this? They become fit to reach his state.

verses.en: Know that nature and spirit are both without beginning. And know that all changes and qualities are born from nature.
verses.hi: जानो कि प्रकृति और पुरुष दोनों ही अनादि हैं। और सारे बदलाव और गुण प्रकृति से ही पैदा होते हैं।
verses.short: Nature and the soul both have no beginning. All changes and qualities come from nature.
verses.notes: What are Prakriti and Purusha? Nature and spirit. Both are without beginning. Where do changes and qualities come from? From nature.

verses.en: Nature is said to be the cause of body, senses and action. Spirit is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.
verses.hi: शरीर, इंद्रियों और कर्म के होने का कारण प्रकृति कही जाती है। सुख-दुख के अनुभव का कारण पुरुष कहा जाता है।
verses.short: Nature does the doing. The soul is what experiences pleasure and pain.
verses.notes: What does nature do? It's the cause of the body, the senses and all action. What does the spirit do? It experiences pleasure and pain.

verses.en: Spirit, living in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature. Its attachment to these qualities is the cause of birth in good and bad wombs.
verses.hi: प्रकृति में स्थित पुरुष प्रकृति से पैदा हुए गुणों को भोगता है। इन गुणों से उसका लगाव ही अच्छी-बुरी योनियों में जन्म का कारण है।
verses.short: The soul gets attached to nature's qualities, and that attachment decides the next birth.
verses.notes: Why is the soul born again and again? Because of its attachment to the qualities of nature. What decides good or bad births? Which qualities it clings to.

verses.en: The Supreme Spirit in this body is also called the witness, the one who permits, the supporter, the experiencer, the great Lord and the highest self.
verses.hi: इस शरीर में स्थित परम पुरुष को साक्षी, अनुमति देने वाला, धारण करने वाला, भोगने वाला, महेश्वर और परमात्मा भी कहा जाता है।
verses.short: The soul in you is the witness, the supporter, the experiencer, the supreme self.
verses.notes: What is the Supreme Self in the body called? The witness, approver, supporter, experiencer, great Lord and Supreme Self. What does 'witness' mean? It watches everything without being changed.

verses.en: Whoever understands spirit, and nature with its qualities, in this way is not born again, however they may be living.
verses.hi: जो इस तरह पुरुष को और गुणों सहित प्रकृति को जान लेता है, वह किसी भी तरह रहते हुए भी फिर जन्म नहीं लेता।
verses.short: Understand the soul and nature properly, and you won't be reborn, whatever your situation.
verses.notes: What happens to one who understands nature and spirit? They are not reborn, however they live. Why? They no longer confuse themselves with the body.

verses.en: Some see the self within themselves through meditation, some through the path of knowledge, and others through the path of action.
verses.hi: कुछ लोग ध्यान से अपने भीतर आत्मा को देखते हैं, कुछ ज्ञान-योग से, और कुछ कर्म-योग से।
verses.short: Some find the self through meditation, some through knowledge, some through selfless work.
verses.notes: How do people find the Self? Some through meditation, some through knowledge and some through selfless action. Is one way enough? Yes. Each sincere path can lead there.

verses.en: Others, not knowing this themselves, worship by hearing from others. They too, devoted to what they hear, go beyond death.
verses.hi: और कुछ लोग इसे खुद न जानकर दूसरों से सुनकर उपासना करते हैं। सुनी हुई बात पर चलने वाले वे भी मृत्यु को पार कर जाते हैं।
verses.short: Others just listen to the wise and follow with faith. They get there too.
verses.notes: What about those who don't know these paths? They hear from others and worship with faith. Do they succeed? Yes. Even they cross beyond death.

verses.en: Arjuna, know that whatever exists, moving or unmoving, comes from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
verses.hi: हे भरतश्रेष्ठ, जो कुछ भी चर या अचर पैदा होता है, उसे क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ के मेल से पैदा हुआ जानो।
verses.short: Everything that's born, moving or still, comes from body and soul coming together.
verses.notes: How does anything come into being? Through the union of the field and its knower: matter and consciousness. Does this apply to everything? Yes, to all moving and unmoving beings.

verses.en: Whoever sees the Supreme Lord present equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishable, truly sees.
verses.hi: जो परमेश्वर को सब प्राणियों में एक समान स्थित, और नाशवानों में अविनाशी रूप में देखता है, वही सच में देखता है।
verses.short: Whoever sees the same eternal divine in every being, even as bodies die, truly sees.
verses.notes: Who truly sees? The one who sees the Supreme Lord equally in all beings, undying among the dying. What does this change? It removes the sense that anyone is less than you.

verses.en: Seeing the same Lord present everywhere, one does not harm the self by the self, and so reaches the highest goal.
verses.hi: हर जगह एक ही ईश्वर को समान रूप से स्थित देखने वाला खुद से खुद को चोट नहीं पहुँचाता, और इसलिए परम गति पाता है।
verses.short: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, you stop hurting yourself and reach the highest.
verses.notes: Why doesn't such a person harm themselves? Seeing the Lord everywhere, they don't hurt others, and so don't hurt their own Self. Where do they reach? The highest goal.

verses.en: Whoever sees that all actions are done by nature alone, and that the self is not the doer, truly sees.
verses.hi: जो देखता है कि सारे कर्म प्रकृति ही करती है, और आत्मा करने वाली नहीं है, वही सच में देखता है।
verses.short: Whoever sees that nature does the acting, not the soul, truly sees.
verses.notes: What else does the wise person see? That nature performs all actions, and the Self is not the doer. Why does this matter? It ends the ego of 'I did this.'

verses.en: When one sees the variety of beings as resting in the One, and spreading out from that One alone, one reaches the Supreme.
verses.hi: जब कोई प्राणियों की अलग-अलग अवस्थाओं को एक में स्थित, और उसी एक से फैलता हुआ देखता है, तब वह ब्रह्म को पा लेता है।
verses.short: When you see all the variety coming from one source, you've found the ultimate.
verses.notes: When does one attain Brahman? When they see the variety of beings resting in the One and spreading from it. What is this vision? Unity behind all diversity.

verses.en: Being without beginning and beyond the qualities, this imperishable highest self, though living in the body, Arjuna, neither acts nor is stained.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, अनादि और गुणों से परे होने के कारण यह अविनाशी परमात्मा शरीर में रहते हुए भी न कुछ करता है, न लिप्त होता है।
verses.short: The supreme self lives in the body but never changes, never acts and is never stained.
verses.notes: Does the Self act or get tainted? No. Though in the body, it neither acts nor is touched. Why? It is beginningless and beyond the qualities of nature.

verses.en: Just as space, though present everywhere, is not stained because it is so subtle, the self present throughout the body is not stained.
verses.hi: जैसे हर जगह फैला आकाश सूक्ष्म होने के कारण लिप्त नहीं होता, वैसे ही पूरे शरीर में स्थित आत्मा भी लिप्त नहीं होती।
verses.short: Like space is everywhere but nothing sticks to it, the soul isn't stained by the body.
verses.notes: What does the space example mean? Space is everywhere but nothing sticks to it. The Self in the body is the same. Why space? It's the subtlest element, touching all yet untouched.

verses.en: Just as the one sun lights up this whole world, Arjuna, the knower of the field lights up the whole field.
verses.hi: हे भारत, जैसे एक ही सूरज इस पूरे संसार को रोशन करता है, वैसे ही क्षेत्रज्ञ पूरे क्षेत्र को रोशन करता है।
verses.short: Like one sun lights up the whole world, the soul lights up the whole body.
verses.notes: What does the sun example mean? As one sun lights the whole world, the Self lights up the whole body with awareness. What does it teach? Awareness is the light by which everything is known.

verses.en: Those who see with the eye of wisdom the difference between the field and its knower, and how beings are freed from nature, reach the Supreme.
verses.hi: जो ज्ञान की आँख से क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञ का अंतर, और प्राणियों के प्रकृति से छूटने का तरीका जान लेते हैं, वे परम को पाते हैं।
verses.short: See the difference between body and soul clearly, and how to break free, and you reach the supreme.
verses.notes: What is the result of this knowledge? Those who see the difference between body and Self, and how to be free of nature, reach the Supreme. What is the 'eye of knowledge'? Inner insight that sees beyond appearances.

verses.en: Krishna said: I will tell you again the highest of all knowledge. Knowing it, all the sages went from here to supreme perfection.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: मैं तुम्हें फिर से सब ज्ञानों में उत्तम परम ज्ञान बताता हूँ, जिसे जानकर सब मुनि यहाँ से परम सिद्धि को पा गए।
verses.short: Krishna: "Here's the highest knowledge again. Sages who knew this reached perfection."
verses.notes: What will Krishna teach now? The highest knowledge, by which sages have reached perfection. What is this chapter about? The three gunas, the forces of nature that shape us.

verses.en: Those who take refuge in this knowledge and come to share my nature are not born at creation and are not troubled at dissolution.
verses.hi: इस ज्ञान का सहारा लेकर जो मेरे स्वरूप को पा लेते हैं, वे न सृष्टि के समय जन्म लेते हैं, न प्रलय के समय दुखी होते हैं।
verses.short: Those who get this become like me. They're not reborn or shaken at the end of the world.
verses.notes: What happens to those who take refuge in this knowledge? They share the Divine's nature and aren't reborn or troubled at dissolution. Why is this significant? It means complete freedom.

verses.en: Great nature is my womb. In it I place the seed, and from it all beings are born, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे भारत, महान प्रकृति मेरी योनि है। उसमें मैं बीज रखता हूँ, और उसी से सब प्राणी पैदा होते हैं।
verses.short: Nature is like the womb of the universe, and I plant the seed. That's how all life begins.
verses.notes: How does creation begin? Krishna places the seed in great nature, and all beings are born from it. What is 'great Brahman' here? Prakriti, the womb of all creation.

verses.en: Arjuna, whatever forms are born in any womb, great nature is their womb and I am the father who gives the seed.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, सब योनियों में जो भी रूप पैदा होते हैं, उन सबकी योनि महान प्रकृति है और बीज देने वाला पिता मैं हूँ।
verses.short: Every life form comes from nature as the mother, and I'm the father.
verses.notes: Who are the mother and father of all beings? Nature is the mother; Krishna is the seed-giving father. What does this mean for us? All beings share the same divine parents.

verses.en: Goodness, passion and dullness are the qualities born of nature. They bind the eternal soul to the body, mighty Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे महाबाहु, सत्त्व, रज और तम, प्रकृति से पैदा हुए ये तीन गुण अविनाशी आत्मा को शरीर में बाँधते हैं।
verses.short: Three energies, goodness, passion and inertia, keep the soul tied to the body.
verses.notes: What are the three gunas? Sattva (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (inertia). What do they do? They bind the eternal soul to the body.

verses.en: Of these, goodness, being pure, gives light and health. It binds through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, sinless Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे निष्पाप, इनमें सत्त्व निर्मल होने से प्रकाश देने वाला और विकार रहित है। यह सुख और ज्ञान की आसक्ति से बाँधता है।
verses.short: Goodness is clean and bright, but even it can trap you through attachment to happiness and knowledge.
verses.notes: How does sattva bind? Through attachment to happiness and knowledge. Isn't sattva good? Yes, it's pure and bright, but even good things can become attachments.

verses.en: Know that passion is full of desire, born from craving and attachment. It binds the soul through attachment to action, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, रजोगुण को राग से भरा, तृष्णा और आसक्ति से पैदा हुआ जानो। यह आत्मा को कर्म की आसक्ति से बाँधता है।
verses.short: Passion comes from craving and attachment, and it hooks you on constant activity. Hustle-culture energy.
verses.notes: What is rajas? Passion born of craving and attachment. How does it bind? Through attachment to action and its results.

verses.en: Know that dullness is born of ignorance and confuses all beings. It binds through carelessness, laziness and sleep, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे भारत, तमोगुण को अज्ञान से पैदा हुआ और सब प्राणियों को भ्रमित करने वाला जानो। यह लापरवाही, आलस और नींद से बाँधता है।
verses.short: Inertia comes from ignorance and traps you with laziness, carelessness and too much sleep.
verses.notes: What is tamas? Inertia born of ignorance that confuses all beings. How does it bind? Through carelessness, laziness and too much sleep.

verses.en: Goodness ties you to happiness, passion to action, Arjuna, while dullness covers knowledge and ties you to carelessness.
verses.hi: हे भारत, सत्त्व सुख में लगाता है, रज कर्म में, और तम ज्ञान को ढककर लापरवाही में लगाता है।
verses.short: Goodness chains you to happiness, passion to work, and inertia to carelessness.
verses.notes: What does each guna attach us to? Sattva to happiness, rajas to action, tamas to carelessness. How does tamas work? It covers wisdom.

verses.en: Sometimes goodness rises by overpowering passion and dullness, Arjuna. Sometimes passion rises over goodness and dullness, and sometimes dullness over goodness and passion.
verses.hi: हे भारत, कभी रज और तम को दबाकर सत्त्व बढ़ता है, कभी सत्त्व और तम को दबाकर रज, और कभी सत्त्व और रज को दबाकर तम।
verses.short: These three compete constantly. Sometimes one wins, sometimes another. Your mood is the scoreboard.
verses.notes: Are the gunas always balanced? No. One rises by overpowering the other two. What does this mean for us? Our moods and tendencies keep shifting.

verses.en: When the light of knowledge shines through all the gates of the body, know that goodness has grown strong.
verses.hi: जब इस शरीर के सब दरवाज़ों में ज्ञान का प्रकाश फैलता है, तब जानो कि सत्त्व बढ़ा हुआ है।
verses.short: When clarity and understanding shine through all your senses, goodness is in charge.
verses.notes: How do I know sattva is strong? When the light of knowledge shines through all the senses. What does that feel like? Clarity, calm and understanding.

verses.en: Greed, restless activity, taking on new projects, unease and craving arise when passion grows strong, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे भरतश्रेष्ठ, रजोगुण बढ़ने पर लालच, लगातार भागदौड़, नए-नए काम शुरू करना, बेचैनी और लालसा पैदा होती है।
verses.short: Greed, restlessness, taking on too much and constant craving: that's passion in charge.
verses.notes: What are the signs of rajas? Greed, constant activity, restlessness and craving. Is activity bad? Not in itself; restless, driven activity is the sign.

verses.en: Darkness, inactivity, carelessness and confusion arise when dullness grows strong, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे कुरुनंदन, तमोगुण बढ़ने पर अंधेरा, कुछ न करना, लापरवाही और भ्रम पैदा होते हैं।
verses.short: Darkness, laziness, carelessness and confusion: that's inertia in charge.
verses.notes: What are the signs of tamas? Darkness, inactivity, carelessness and confusion. How can we recognise it? When the mind feels foggy and lazy.

verses.en: If a person dies when goodness is strong, they reach the pure worlds of those who know the highest.
verses.hi: जब सत्त्व बढ़ा हो और उस समय व्यक्ति मरे, तो वह उत्तम ज्ञानियों के निर्मल लोकों को पाता है।
verses.short: Leave the world in a state of goodness and you go to the higher, purer realms.
verses.notes: What if one dies when sattva dominates? They go to the pure worlds of the wise. What is the lesson? The quality we live in shapes where we go.

verses.en: Dying in passion, one is born among those attached to action. Dying in dullness, one is born in the wombs of the ignorant.
verses.hi: रजोगुण में मरने वाला कर्म में आसक्त लोगों के बीच जन्म लेता है, और तमोगुण में मरने वाला मूर्ख योनियों में जन्म लेता है।
verses.short: Leave in passion and you're born among workaholics. Leave in inertia and you're born into dullness.
verses.notes: What if one dies in rajas? They are born among people attached to action. And in tamas? They are born among the dull and ignorant.

verses.en: The result of good action is said to be pure and full of goodness. The result of passion is pain, and the result of dullness is ignorance.
verses.hi: भले कर्म से शुद्ध और सात्त्विक फल मिलता है। रजोगुण से किए काम का नतीजा दुख होता है, और तमोगुण से किए काम का नतीजा नासमझी।
verses.short: Good deeds lead to purity, passion leads to pain, and inertia leads to ignorance.
verses.notes: What are the fruits of each guna? Good action brings purity; rajas brings pain; tamas brings ignorance. What can we learn? Our results reflect the quality behind our actions.

verses.en: From goodness comes knowledge, from passion comes greed, and from dullness come carelessness, confusion and ignorance.
verses.hi: सत्त्व से ज्ञान पैदा होता है, रज से लालच, और तम से लापरवाही, भ्रम और अज्ञान।
verses.short: Goodness brings wisdom, passion brings greed, inertia brings carelessness and confusion.
verses.notes: What comes from each guna? Knowledge from sattva, greed from rajas, and carelessness and confusion from tamas. How can we use this? Notice what you're feeling to see which guna is active.

verses.en: Those rooted in goodness rise upwards, those in passion stay in the middle, and those in dullness, living by the lowest quality, sink downwards.
verses.hi: सत्त्व में स्थित लोग ऊपर जाते हैं, रजोगुणी बीच में रहते हैं, और सबसे निचले गुण में जीने वाले तमोगुणी नीचे जाते हैं।
verses.short: Live in goodness and you rise. Live in passion and you stay stuck. Live in inertia and you sink.
verses.notes: Where do people of each guna go? Sattvic people rise, rajasic stay in the middle, tamasic sink. Is this fixed forever? No. We can shift our tendencies through effort.

verses.en: When the seer sees no doer other than the qualities, and knows what lies beyond the qualities, they reach my state of being.
verses.hi: जब देखने वाला गुणों के सिवा किसी और को करने वाला नहीं देखता, और गुणों से परे को जान लेता है, तब वह मेरे स्वरूप को पाता है।
verses.short: See that these three energies are behind every action and know what's beyond them. Then you reach me.
verses.notes: When does one reach Krishna's state? When they see that only the gunas act, and know what lies beyond them. What does this insight remove? The false sense of being the doer.
