verses.en: Going beyond these three qualities, which give rise to the body, the soul is freed from birth, death, old age and sorrow, and tastes immortality.
verses.hi: शरीर को पैदा करने वाले इन तीन गुणों से ऊपर उठकर आत्मा जन्म, मृत्यु, बुढ़ापे और दुख से छूटकर अमरता पाती है।
verses.short: Rise above all three and you're free from birth, death, ageing and pain.
verses.notes: What happens when one goes beyond the gunas? Freedom from birth, death, old age and sorrow. What is attained? Immortality.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Lord, what are the signs of someone who has gone beyond these three qualities? How do they behave, and how do they go beyond them?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे प्रभु, इन तीन गुणों से परे गए व्यक्ति की क्या पहचान है? उसका आचरण कैसा होता है, और वह इन गुणों से कैसे पार होता है?
verses.short: Arjuna: "How do I spot someone who's gone beyond all three? How do they act?"
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask? How to recognise someone beyond the gunas, how they behave and how they got there. Why is this useful? A clear picture helps us aim for it.

verses.en: Krishna said: Arjuna, such a person does not resent light, activity or confusion when they arise, nor long for them when they fade.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: हे पांडव, जब प्रकाश, सक्रियता या भ्रम आते हैं तो वह उनसे नफ़रत नहीं करता, और जब चले जाते हैं तो उनकी चाह नहीं रखता।
verses.short: They don't resent clarity, busyness or confusion when it comes, and don't miss it when it goes.
verses.notes: How does such a person relate to the gunas? They don't resent clarity, activity or confusion when present, nor long for them when gone. What is the key? Non-reaction to inner states.

verses.en: Sitting as if neutral, not shaken by the qualities, knowing that it is just the qualities at work, they stay steady and don't waver.
verses.hi: जो उदासीन की तरह बैठा रहता है, गुणों से विचलित नहीं होता, और यह जानकर कि गुण ही बरत रहे हैं, स्थिर रहता है और डगमगाता नहीं,
verses.short: They sit back like an observer. "Oh, it's just the energies doing their thing." Unshaken.
verses.notes: How do they stay? Like a neutral observer, unshaken, knowing 'the gunas are just doing their work.' Can we practise this? Yes. Watch moods come and go without being swept away.

verses.en: The same in pain and pleasure, centred in themselves, seeing a lump of earth, a stone and gold as equal, the same towards the pleasant and the unpleasant, steady, the same in blame and praise,
verses.hi: जो सुख-दुख में एक जैसा, अपने आप में स्थित, मिट्टी, पत्थर और सोने को समान मानने वाला, प्रिय-अप्रिय में एक जैसा, धीर, और निंदा-प्रशंसा में समान है,
verses.short: Same in pleasure and pain. Dirt, stone and gold look the same to them. Calm with praise or blame.
verses.notes: How do they view pleasure and pain? Equally, resting in the Self, seeing gold and earth as the same. And praise and blame? Also equally; they stay steady.

verses.en: the same in honour and insult, the same towards friend and foe, and having given up all self-driven projects: such a person is said to have gone beyond the qualities.
verses.hi: जो मान-अपमान में समान, मित्र और शत्रु के पक्ष में समान है, और जिसने स्वार्थ के सारे काम छोड़ दिए हैं, वह गुणों से परे कहलाता है।
verses.short: Same in honour and insult, with friends and enemies, not chasing ego projects. They're beyond the energies.
verses.notes: What else marks them? Same in honour and insult, same to friend and foe, free of selfish projects. Is this indifference? No. It's freedom from being controlled by outer events.

verses.en: And whoever serves me with unwavering devotion goes beyond these qualities and becomes fit to be one with the Supreme.
verses.hi: और जो अटल भक्ति-योग से मेरी सेवा करता है, वह इन गुणों को पार करके ब्रह्म बनने के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.short: Those who love and serve me steadily rise above all three and reach the ultimate.
verses.notes: How does one go beyond the gunas? Through unwavering devotion to Krishna. Why devotion? Love for the Divine lifts you above nature's pull.

verses.en: For I am the foundation of the Supreme, of the immortal and imperishable, of eternal dharma and of perfect happiness.
verses.hi: क्योंकि ब्रह्म का, अविनाशी अमृत का, सनातन धर्म का और परम सुख का आधार मैं ही हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the foundation of the ultimate: eternal, unchanging truth and complete bliss.
verses.notes: What does Krishna say he is the basis of? Brahman, immortality, eternal dharma and perfect bliss. What does this tell us? Reaching him means reaching all of these.

verses.en: Krishna said: They speak of an eternal sacred fig tree with roots above and branches below. Its leaves are the Vedic hymns. Whoever knows this tree knows the Vedas.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: एक अविनाशी पीपल के पेड़ की बात कही जाती है, जिसकी जड़ें ऊपर और शाखाएँ नीचे हैं। वेद के मंत्र इसके पत्ते हैं। जो इसे जानता है, वही वेद जानता है।
verses.short: Life is like an upside-down tree, roots in the divine, branches spreading down into the world. Understand it and you get it all.
verses.notes: What is the upside-down tree? The world, pictured as an ashvattha tree with roots above in the Divine and branches spreading below. Why are its leaves the Vedas? Scriptures nourish and protect the tree of life, like leaves.

verses.en: Its branches spread below and above, nourished by the qualities, with sense objects as their buds. Below, its roots stretch out, tying people to action in the human world.
verses.hi: इसकी शाखाएँ नीचे और ऊपर फैली हैं, गुणों से पोषित हैं और विषय इनकी कोंपलें हैं। नीचे इसकी जड़ें फैली हैं जो मनुष्य-लोक में कर्मों से बाँधती हैं।
verses.short: Its branches grow on our moods, its buds are sense pleasures, and its roots keep pulling us into action.
verses.notes: How do the branches grow? Fed by the gunas, with sense objects as buds, spreading up and down. What are the roots below? Our actions and desires, which tie us to the human world.

verses.en: Its real form can't be seen here, nor its end, its beginning or its foundation. Cutting down this deep-rooted tree with the strong axe of detachment,
verses.hi: यहाँ इसका असली रूप नहीं दिखता, न इसका अंत, न आदि, न आधार। गहरी जड़ों वाले इस पीपल को वैराग्य की मज़बूत कुल्हाड़ी से काटकर,
verses.short: You can't see where it starts or ends. Cut through it with the strong axe of detachment.
verses.notes: Why can't we see the tree's form? Its beginning, end and base aren't visible from inside it. How do we cut it? With the strong axe of detachment.

verses.en: one should seek that place from which, once reached, no one returns, thinking: "I take refuge in that original Being from whom this ancient flow of creation came."
verses.hi: उस पद को खोजना चाहिए जहाँ पहुँचकर कोई वापस नहीं लौटता, यह सोचते हुए: "मैं उस आदि पुरुष की शरण लेता हूँ जिससे यह पुरानी सृष्टि की धारा निकली है।"
verses.short: Then search for the place you never come back from, and take refuge in the original source.
verses.notes: What should one seek after cutting the tree? The goal from which there's no return: the Primal Person. How should we approach him? By taking refuge in him, the source of all.

verses.en: Free from pride and confusion, having conquered the flaw of attachment, always focused on the self, with desires gone and free from the opposites of pleasure and pain, the wise reach that eternal state.
verses.hi: जो घमंड और मोह से मुक्त हैं, आसक्ति के दोष को जीत चुके हैं, हमेशा आत्मा में लगे हैं, जिनकी इच्छाएँ मिट गई हैं और जो सुख-दुख के द्वंद्वों से छूट गए हैं, वे ज्ञानी उस अविनाशी पद को पाते हैं।
verses.short: No ego, no clinging, focused on the self, free from cravings and highs and lows. That's how you get there.
verses.notes: Who reaches the eternal goal? Those free from pride and delusion, who have conquered attachment and desire. What else marks them? They are free from pairs of opposites and always devoted to the Self.

verses.en: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire lights it up. Those who reach it never return. That is my supreme home.
verses.hi: उसे न सूरज रोशन करता है, न चाँद, न आग। जहाँ पहुँचकर लोग वापस नहीं लौटते, वही मेरा परम धाम है।
verses.short: My home isn't lit by sun, moon or fire. Reach it and you never come back.
verses.notes: What lights up Krishna's abode? Not the sun, moon or fire. It is self-luminous. What happens to those who reach it? They don't return.

verses.en: An eternal part of me becomes the living soul in the world of the living. It draws to itself the mind and the five senses, which rest in nature.
verses.hi: जीव-लोक में मेरा ही सनातन अंश जीवात्मा बनता है। वह प्रकृति में स्थित मन और पाँच इंद्रियों को अपनी ओर खींचता है।
verses.short: Every soul is a forever part of me. In this world it gets pulled by the mind and senses.
verses.notes: What is the individual soul? An eternal part of Krishna, living in the world. What does it draw to itself? The mind and five senses, which belong to nature.

verses.en: When the soul, the master of the body, takes on a body and when it leaves one, it carries these along, as the wind carries scents from flowers.
verses.hi: जब शरीर का स्वामी आत्मा कोई शरीर पाता है और जब उसे छोड़ता है, तो इन्हें साथ ले जाता है, जैसे हवा फूलों से खुशबू ले जाती है।
verses.short: When the soul switches bodies, it carries the mind and senses along, like wind carries a scent.
verses.notes: How does the soul move between bodies? Like wind carrying fragrance from flowers, it carries the mind and senses to a new body. What does the image suggest? Our tendencies travel with us.

verses.en: Using the ears, eyes, touch, taste, smell and the mind, it experiences the objects of the senses.
verses.hi: कान, आँख, त्वचा, जीभ, नाक और मन का सहारा लेकर वह इंद्रियों के विषयों का अनुभव करता है।
verses.short: Through ears, eyes, skin, tongue, nose and mind, the soul experiences the world.
verses.notes: How does the soul experience the world? Through the ear, eye, touch, taste, smell and mind. Is the soul the senses? No. It uses them, like a person using tools.

verses.en: The deluded don't see the soul leaving, staying or experiencing through the qualities. Those with the eye of wisdom see it.
verses.hi: शरीर छोड़ते, उसमें रहते या गुणों से जुड़कर भोगते हुए आत्मा को मूर्ख नहीं देख पाते। ज्ञान की आँख वाले ही उसे देखते हैं।
verses.short: Confused people don't notice the soul coming, staying or leaving. People with insight do.
verses.notes: Why don't most people see the soul? The deluded don't notice it leaving, staying or experiencing. Who sees it? Those with the eye of wisdom.

verses.en: Yogis who strive see it present within themselves. But those who are not pure in heart and lack understanding don't see it, even when they try.
verses.hi: कोशिश करने वाले योगी इसे अपने भीतर स्थित देखते हैं। पर जिनका मन शुद्ध नहीं और समझ नहीं है, वे कोशिश करके भी इसे नहीं देख पाते।
verses.short: Dedicated yogis see the soul within themselves. Effort without a clear mind doesn't get you there.
verses.notes: Who sees the Self within? Yogis who strive sincerely. Why do some fail despite trying? Their minds are not yet purified.

verses.en: The light in the sun that brightens the whole world, the light in the moon and the light in fire: know that light to be mine.
verses.hi: सूरज में जो तेज पूरे जगत को रोशन करता है, और जो तेज चाँद में और आग में है, उस तेज को मेरा ही जानो।
verses.short: The light of the sun, the moon and fire that lights up the world? That's me.
verses.notes: Whose light is in the sun, moon and fire? Krishna's. What does this teach? All light comes from one source.

verses.en: Entering the earth, I hold up all beings with my energy. Becoming the moon, full of juice, I nourish all plants.
verses.hi: धरती में समाकर मैं अपनी ऊर्जा से सब प्राणियों को धारण करता हूँ, और रस से भरा चंद्रमा बनकर सब वनस्पतियों को पोषण देता हूँ।
verses.short: I hold the earth together and support all life. I'm the nourishment in every plant.
verses.notes: How does Krishna support life? He enters the earth to hold up beings, and as the moon's essence he nourishes plants. What is Soma here? The life-giving essence that feeds all plants.

verses.en: Becoming the digestive fire in the bodies of living beings, joined with the incoming and outgoing breath, I digest the four kinds of food.
verses.hi: प्राणियों के शरीर में वैश्वानर अग्नि बनकर, प्राण और अपान से जुड़कर, मैं चार तरह के भोजन को पचाता हूँ।
verses.short: I'm the fire of digestion inside you, working with your breath to process everything you eat.
verses.notes: How is Krishna present in our bodies? As the digestive fire, working with the breath to digest food. What does this show? The Divine is present even in everyday body functions.

verses.en: I am seated in everyone's heart. From me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I am what all the Vedas seek to know. I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
verses.hi: मैं सबके हृदय में बसा हूँ। मुझसे ही याददाश्त, ज्ञान और उनका खो जाना होता है। सब वेदों से जानने योग्य मैं ही हूँ। वेदांत का रचयिता और वेदों को जानने वाला भी मैं हूँ।
verses.short: I'm in every heart. Memory, knowledge and forgetting come from me. Every scripture points to me.
verses.notes: Where is Krishna in us? Seated in every heart. Memory, knowledge and forgetting come from him. What is the goal of all scripture? To know him.

verses.en: There are two kinds of beings in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. All living beings are perishable; the unchanging one is called imperishable.
verses.hi: इस संसार में दो तरह के पुरुष हैं, नाशवान और अविनाशी। सब प्राणी नाशवान हैं, और जो अटल है उसे अविनाशी कहते हैं।
verses.short: There are two kinds of beings: those that perish and the one that doesn't.
verses.notes: What are the two kinds of beings? The perishable (all beings) and the imperishable (the unchanging soul). What does 'perishable' mean here? Bodies and forms that change and end.

verses.en: But there is another, the highest Being, called the Supreme Self, the unchanging Lord who enters the three worlds and sustains them.
verses.hi: पर उत्तम पुरुष इनसे अलग है, जिसे परमात्मा कहते हैं। वह अविनाशी ईश्वर तीनों लोकों में समाकर उनका पालन करता है।
verses.short: Beyond both is the Supreme Self, who enters and sustains all three worlds.
verses.notes: Who is beyond both? The Supreme Person, called the Paramatma, who pervades and supports the three worlds. What makes him different? He is the unchanging Lord over both.

verses.en: Because I am beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable, I am known in the world and in the Vedas as the Supreme Person.
verses.hi: क्योंकि मैं नाशवान से परे हूँ और अविनाशी से भी उत्तम हूँ, इसलिए संसार और वेदों में पुरुषोत्तम के नाम से प्रसिद्ध हूँ।
verses.short: I'm beyond the perishable and higher than the imperishable. That's why I'm called the Supreme Person.
verses.notes: Why is Krishna called Purushottama? Because he is beyond the perishable and higher than the imperishable. What does the name mean? The Supreme Person.

verses.en: Whoever, free from confusion, knows me as the Supreme Person knows everything and worships me with their whole being, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे भारत, जो भ्रम से मुक्त होकर मुझे पुरुषोत्तम जानता है, वह सब कुछ जानता है और पूरे मन से मुझे भजता है।
verses.short: Whoever knows me this way, without confusion, knows everything and loves me fully.
verses.notes: What happens to one who knows Krishna as the Supreme? They know everything worth knowing and worship him with their whole being. Why 'with their whole being'? True knowing naturally becomes complete devotion.

verses.en: So I have taught you this most secret teaching, sinless Arjuna. Understanding it, a person becomes wise and has done all that needs doing.
verses.hi: हे निष्पाप भारत, इस तरह मैंने तुम्हें यह सबसे गुप्त शास्त्र बताया। इसे समझकर इंसान बुद्धिमान और कृतार्थ हो जाता है।
verses.short: That's the deepest secret. Understand it and you're truly wise, and your life's work is done.
verses.notes: How does Krishna describe this teaching? As the most secret teaching. What does understanding it bring? Wisdom and the fulfilment of life's purpose.

verses.en: Krishna said: Fearlessness, a pure heart, steadiness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scripture, discipline and honesty,
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: निडरता, मन की शुद्धता, ज्ञान और योग में स्थिरता, दान, इंद्रियों पर काबू, यज्ञ, शास्त्रों का अध्ययन, तप और सरलता,
verses.short: Divine qualities: fearlessness, a clean heart, steady practice, generosity, self-control, study and honesty.
verses.notes: What divine qualities are listed first? Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadiness in knowledge, charity, self-control, worship, study, austerity and honesty. Why start with fearlessness? Many good qualities need courage to grow.

verses.en: non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, letting go, calm, not gossiping, kindness to all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty and steadiness,
verses.hi: अहिंसा, सच बोलना, क्रोध न करना, त्याग, शांति, चुगली न करना, सब प्राणियों पर दया, लालच न होना, कोमलता, लज्जा और चंचलता न होना,
verses.short: Non-violence, truth, no anger, letting go, peace, no gossip, kindness to all, no greed, gentleness.
verses.notes: What more divine qualities are named? Non-violence, truth, no anger, renunciation, peace, no backbiting, compassion, no greed, gentleness and modesty. Which is most practical today? Not speaking ill of others is a simple daily start.

verses.en: vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, not bearing grudges and not being arrogant: these belong to someone born with a divine nature, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे भारत, तेज, क्षमा, धैर्य, पवित्रता, किसी से वैर न रखना और घमंड न करना, ये दैवी स्वभाव लेकर जन्मे व्यक्ति के गुण हैं।
verses.short: Energy, forgiveness, courage, purity, no hate and no big ego. These are signs of a divine nature.
verses.notes: What are the last divine qualities? Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, no hatred and no excessive pride. Who has these qualities? Those born with a divine nature.

verses.en: Hypocrisy, arrogance, pride, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to someone born with a demonic nature, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, पाखंड, घमंड, अभिमान, क्रोध, कठोरता और अज्ञान, ये आसुरी स्वभाव लेकर जन्मे व्यक्ति के लक्षण हैं।
verses.short: Showing off, arrogance, ego, anger, rudeness and ignorance are signs of a toxic nature.
verses.notes: What are demonic qualities? Hypocrisy, arrogance, pride, anger, harshness and ignorance. Is anyone purely one type? Most of us have a mix; the point is which ones we grow.

verses.en: The divine nature leads to freedom, and the demonic nature leads to bondage. Don't worry, Arjuna, you were born with a divine nature.
verses.hi: दैवी स्वभाव मुक्ति की ओर ले जाता है और आसुरी स्वभाव बंधन की ओर। हे पांडव, चिंता मत करो, तुम दैवी स्वभाव लेकर जन्मे हो।
verses.short: Divine qualities set you free; toxic ones trap you. Relax, Arjuna, you've got the good kind.
verses.notes: Where do divine and demonic qualities lead? Divine ones to freedom, demonic ones to bondage. What does Krishna tell Arjuna? Don't worry, you were born with divine qualities.

verses.en: There are two kinds of beings in this world, the divine and the demonic. I have described the divine at length. Now hear about the demonic, Arjuna.
verses.hi: इस संसार में दो तरह के प्राणी हैं, दैवी और आसुरी। दैवी स्वभाव के बारे में मैंने विस्तार से बताया। हे पार्थ, अब आसुरी के बारे में सुनो।
verses.short: There are two types of people: divine and toxic. You've heard about the divine. Now the other side.
verses.notes: How many types of beings are there? Two: the divine and the demonic. Why describe the demonic in detail? So we can recognise and avoid these traits.

verses.en: People of demonic nature don't know what to do and what not to do. There is no cleanliness, no good conduct and no truth in them.
verses.hi: आसुरी स्वभाव वाले लोग नहीं जानते कि क्या करना चाहिए और क्या नहीं। उनमें न पवित्रता होती है, न अच्छा आचरण, न सच्चाई।
verses.short: Toxic people don't know what to do or what to avoid. No integrity, no discipline, no truth.
verses.notes: What don't demonic people understand? What to do and what not to do. What do they lack? Purity, good conduct and truth.

verses.en: They say the world is unreal, has no foundation and no God, and is born only from attraction. What else, they ask, causes it but desire?
verses.hi: वे कहते हैं कि यह संसार झूठा है, इसका कोई आधार नहीं, कोई ईश्वर नहीं, और यह बस आकर्षण से पैदा हुआ है। इच्छा के सिवा इसका और क्या कारण है?
verses.short: They say: "Nothing's real, there's no God, life is random and it's all about desire."
verses.notes: What do demonic people believe? That the world has no truth, no basis and no God, and exists only for desire. Why does this view lead to harm? Without any higher value, selfishness rules.

verses.en: Holding this view, these lost souls of little understanding and cruel actions rise up as enemies of the world, bent on its destruction.
verses.hi: इस सोच को पकड़कर, खोई हुई आत्मा वाले, कम समझ वाले और क्रूर कर्म करने वाले ये लोग दुनिया के दुश्मन बनकर उसके नाश के लिए उठ खड़े होते हैं।
verses.short: With that mindset they lose themselves and do harmful things that damage the world.
verses.notes: What do people with this view do? They act cruelly and harm the world. What is the root cause? A lost inner compass and small understanding.

verses.en: Driven by desires that can never be filled, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, holding wrong ideas out of confusion, they act with impure intentions.
verses.hi: कभी न भरने वाली इच्छाओं के सहारे, पाखंड, अभिमान और घमंड से भरे, मोह से गलत धारणाएँ पकड़कर, वे अपवित्र इरादों से काम करते हैं।
verses.short: Endless desires, shady money, ego and showing off. That's how they live.
verses.notes: What drives them? Endless desires, hypocrisy, pride and arrogance. What do they hold on to? False ideas and impure goals.

verses.en: Gripped by endless worries that last until death, treating enjoyment of desires as the highest goal, they are sure that this is all there is.
verses.hi: मरते दम तक चलने वाली अनगिनत चिंताओं से घिरे, इच्छाओं के भोग को ही सबसे बड़ा लक्ष्य मानकर, वे पक्का मान लेते हैं कि बस यही सब कुछ है।
verses.short: They worry endlessly until death, and believe pleasure is the only point of life.
verses.notes: What is their main concern? Endless worries until death, believing pleasure is everything. What is the result? A restless, anxious life.

verses.en: Bound by hundreds of chains of hope, given over to desire and anger, they try to pile up wealth by unfair means to feed their pleasures.
verses.hi: आशा की सैकड़ों रस्सियों से बँधे, इच्छा और क्रोध में डूबे, वे अपने भोगों के लिए गलत तरीकों से धन जमा करने की कोशिश करते हैं।
verses.short: Trapped by a hundred hopes, ruled by desire and anger, they grab money any way they can.
verses.notes: What binds them? Hundreds of hopes, desire and anger. How do they get wealth? By unfair means, just to satisfy cravings.

verses.en: "I got this today; I'll fulfil that wish next. This is mine, and that wealth will be mine too.
verses.hi: "आज मैंने यह पा लिया, अब वह इच्छा पूरी करूँगा। यह मेरा है, और वह धन भी मेरा हो जाएगा।
verses.short: "I got this today, I'll get that tomorrow. This is mine, and that'll be mine too." Never enough.
verses.notes: How do they think? 'I got this today, I'll get that next. This wealth is mine, more will be mine.' What does this show? A mind that is never satisfied.

verses.en: I have killed that enemy, and I'll kill the others too. I am the boss, I enjoy life, I am successful, powerful and happy.
verses.hi: उस दुश्मन को मैंने मार दिया, और बाकियों को भी मारूँगा। मैं ही मालिक हूँ, मैं ही भोगने वाला हूँ, मैं सफल, ताकतवर और सुखी हूँ।
verses.short: "I destroyed that rival, I'll take down the rest. I'm the boss, I'm winning, I'm powerful."
verses.notes: What else do they say? 'I defeated that enemy and will defeat others. I'm the master, I'm successful, strong and happy.' What's wrong with this? It's pure ego, with no humility or care for others.

verses.en: I am rich and well-born. Who else is like me? I'll perform rituals, give charity and have a great time." So they think, deluded by ignorance.
verses.hi: मैं अमीर हूँ और ऊँचे कुल का हूँ। मेरे जैसा और कौन है? मैं यज्ञ करूँगा, दान दूँगा और मज़े करूँगा।" अज्ञान से भ्रमित लोग ऐसा सोचते हैं।
verses.short: "I'm rich and well-connected. Who's like me? I'll donate and party." Clout chasing, ancient edition.
verses.notes: How do they see themselves? 'I'm rich and high-born. Who is like me? I'll give, I'll celebrate.' Why call this delusion? Even their charity is about showing off.

verses.en: Confused by many thoughts, caught in a web of delusion and addicted to pleasures, they fall into a foul hell.
verses.hi: तरह-तरह के विचारों में भटके, मोह के जाल में फँसे और भोगों में डूबे वे लोग गंदे नरक में गिरते हैं।
verses.short: Lost in a hundred thoughts, stuck in a web of illusion, hooked on pleasure, they fall hard.
verses.notes: What happens to them? Confused by many thoughts and caught in delusion, they fall into misery. What is the 'net'? The tangle of desires that traps the mind.

verses.en: Full of self-importance, stubborn, drunk on wealth and pride, they perform rituals in name only, for show, without following the proper way.
verses.hi: खुद को बड़ा मानने वाले, अकड़ू, धन और मान के नशे में चूर, वे दिखावे के लिए, बिना विधि के, केवल नाम के यज्ञ करते हैं।
verses.short: Full of themselves and drunk on money and pride, they do good deeds only for show.
verses.notes: How do they perform worship? Only for show, full of pride, not according to scripture. What is the lesson? Outer religion without inner sincerity is empty.

verses.en: Clinging to ego, force, arrogance, desire and anger, these spiteful people hate me, who live in their own bodies and in the bodies of others.
verses.hi: अहंकार, बल, घमंड, इच्छा और क्रोध का सहारा लेने वाले ये दोष निकालने वाले लोग अपने और दूसरों के शरीर में रहने वाले मुझसे नफ़रत करते हैं।
verses.short: Driven by ego, power, pride, lust and anger, they end up hating the divine in themselves and others.
verses.notes: Whom do they hate? The Divine who lives in their own bodies and in others. What fuels this hatred? Ego, force, pride, desire and anger.

verses.en: These hateful, cruel and lowest of people, I keep throwing into demonic wombs in the cycle of rebirth.
verses.hi: इन नफ़रत करने वाले, क्रूर, अशुभ और नीच लोगों को मैं संसार में बार-बार आसुरी योनियों में डालता हूँ।
verses.short: Cruel, hateful people keep getting pulled back into toxic cycles. What you give, you get.
verses.notes: What happens to the cruel and hateful? They are thrown again and again into lower births. Is this punishment? It's the natural result of their own actions.

verses.en: Falling into demonic wombs birth after birth, these deluded people never reach me, Arjuna, and sink to the lowest state.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, जन्म-जन्म आसुरी योनियों में पड़कर ये मूर्ख लोग मुझे कभी नहीं पाते और सबसे नीची गति में चले जाते हैं।
verses.short: Life after life they sink lower, never reaching me.
verses.notes: Do they ever improve? Not while they reject the Divine; they sink lower birth after birth. Is there hope? Yes. Krishna says elsewhere that turning to him can change anyone.

verses.en: There are three gates to hell that destroy the self: desire, anger and greed. So let go of these three.
verses.hi: नरक के तीन दरवाज़े हैं जो आत्मा का नाश करते हैं: काम, क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को छोड़ देना चाहिए।
verses.short: Lust, anger and greed: the three doors to self-destruction. Close all three.
verses.notes: What are the three gates to hell? Desire, anger and greed. Why should we drop them? They destroy the self.

verses.en: A person freed from these three gates of darkness, Arjuna, does what is good for the self and then reaches the highest goal.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, अंधकार के इन तीन दरवाज़ों से छूटा व्यक्ति अपने भले का आचरण करता है और फिर परम गति पाता है।
verses.short: Escape those three and you start working for your own real good, and you reach the highest.
verses.notes: What happens to one free of these three? They act for their own true good and reach the highest goal. Is it possible to be free? Yes, with awareness and effort.

verses.en: Whoever ignores the guidance of scripture and acts on impulse reaches neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal.
verses.hi: जो शास्त्र के बताए तरीके को छोड़कर अपनी मनमर्ज़ी से चलता है, उसे न सिद्धि मिलती है, न सुख, न परम गति।
verses.short: Ignore all guidance and just follow your cravings? You get no success, no happiness and no freedom.
verses.notes: What happens to those who ignore scripture and follow whims? They don't find perfection, happiness or the highest goal. Why? Acting from desire alone leads nowhere lasting.

verses.en: So let scripture be your guide in deciding what to do and what not to do. Knowing what scripture teaches, you should do your work here.
verses.hi: इसलिए क्या करना है और क्या नहीं, यह तय करने में शास्त्र को अपना पैमाना बनाओ। शास्त्र की बताई बात जानकर यहाँ अपना कर्म करो।
verses.short: So let wisdom be your guide on what to do and what not to do, and then act.
verses.notes: How do we decide right and wrong? Let scripture be the guide. Why scripture? It holds tested wisdom beyond personal desires.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Krishna, what about those who ignore the rules of scripture but worship with faith? Is their state one of goodness, passion or dullness?
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे कृष्ण, जो लोग शास्त्र की विधि छोड़कर श्रद्धा से पूजा करते हैं, उनकी स्थिति कैसी है? सात्त्विक, राजसिक या तामसिक?
verses.short: Arjuna: "What about people who skip the rules but still have faith? What kind of faith is that?"
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask? What about those who worship with faith but don't follow scripture? Is their faith sattvic, rajasic or tamasic? Why ask this? Many sincere people don't know the rules. Arjuna wants to know where they stand.

verses.en: Krishna said: The faith of embodied beings, born of their nature, is of three kinds: of goodness, of passion and of dullness. Hear about it.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: शरीरधारियों की श्रद्धा, जो उनके स्वभाव से पैदा होती है, तीन तरह की होती है: सात्त्विक, राजसिक और तामसिक। इसके बारे में सुनो।
verses.short: Krishna: "Faith comes in three types, based on your nature: pure, passionate or dark."
verses.notes: What are the three kinds of faith? Sattvic, rajasic and tamasic, based on one's nature. Where does faith come from? From a person's inborn tendencies.

verses.en: Everyone's faith matches their inner nature, Arjuna. A person is made of their faith. Whatever their faith is, that is who they are.
verses.hi: हे भारत, हर किसी की श्रद्धा उसके अंतर्मन के अनुसार होती है। इंसान श्रद्धा से बना है। जिसकी जैसी श्रद्धा है, वह वैसा ही है।
verses.short: You are what you believe in. Your faith shapes who you become.
verses.notes: What does 'a person is made of faith' mean? What you deeply believe shapes who you are. How can we use this? Choose what you put your faith in carefully.

verses.en: People of goodness worship the gods. People of passion worship yakshas and rakshasas. People of dullness worship ghosts and spirits.
verses.hi: सात्त्विक लोग देवताओं की पूजा करते हैं, राजसिक लोग यक्षों और राक्षसों की, और तामसिक लोग प्रेतों और भूतों की।
verses.short: Pure people worship the divine, passionate people chase power, dark-minded people worship ghosts and spirits.
verses.notes: Whom does each type worship? Sattvic people worship the gods, rajasic people worship power-spirits, tamasic people worship ghosts. What does this show? Our nature shapes what we turn to.

verses.en: Those who practise harsh austerities not taught by scripture, full of hypocrisy and ego, driven by desire, attachment and force,
verses.hi: जो लोग शास्त्र में न बताए गए कठोर तप करते हैं, पाखंड और अहंकार से भरे, और इच्छा, आसक्ति और ज़िद के ज़ोर से चलते हैं,
verses.short: Some people do extreme self-punishment just to show off, driven by ego and desire.
verses.notes: What kind of austerity does Krishna reject? Harsh self-punishment not taught by scripture, done out of pride and desire. Why reject it? It harms instead of purifying.

verses.en: who mindlessly torture the elements of their body and me living within it: know that they have a demonic resolve.
verses.hi: जो नासमझी में अपने शरीर के तत्त्वों को और उसके भीतर रहने वाले मुझे भी कष्ट देते हैं, उन्हें आसुरी निश्चय वाला जानो।
verses.short: Hurting your own body isn't spiritual. It hurts the divine in you too. That's a toxic mindset.
verses.notes: Whom does such austerity torment? The body's elements and Krishna who lives within. What is the lesson? Spiritual life doesn't mean hurting your body.

verses.en: Even the food people like is of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, austerity and charity. Hear how they differ.
verses.hi: लोगों को पसंद आने वाला भोजन भी तीन तरह का होता है, और वैसे ही यज्ञ, तप और दान भी। इनके अंतर के बारे में सुनो।
verses.short: Even food comes in three types. So does worship, discipline and giving. Let's break it down.
verses.notes: What else comes in three types? Food, sacrifice, austerity and charity. Why does this matter? Daily choices reflect and shape our nature.

verses.en: Foods that increase life, clarity, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction, that are juicy, wholesome, nourishing and pleasant, are liked by people of goodness.
verses.hi: जो भोजन उम्र, बुद्धि, ताकत, सेहत, सुख और प्रसन्नता बढ़ाता है, और रसीला, चिकना, टिकाऊ और मन को भाने वाला होता है, वह सात्त्विक लोगों को प्रिय है।
verses.short: Pure food: fresh, nourishing, wholesome, satisfying. It boosts health, energy, focus and happiness.
verses.notes: What is sattvic food? Food that is wholesome, juicy, nourishing and pleasing, and supports long life, strength and joy. How does it affect the mind? It keeps it clear and calm.

verses.en: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and burning are liked by people of passion. They cause pain, grief and illness.
verses.hi: कड़वा, खट्टा, नमकीन, बहुत गरम, तीखा, रूखा और जलन पैदा करने वाला भोजन राजसिक लोगों को प्रिय है। यह दुख, शोक और रोग देता है।
verses.short: Passionate food: too spicy, salty, sour or hot. Tastes intense, leaves you uncomfortable and unwell.
verses.notes: What is rajasic food? Very bitter, sour, salty, hot, spicy, dry or burning food. What does it cause? Pain, grief and disease.

verses.en: Food that is stale, tasteless, smelly, left over, half-eaten and impure is liked by people of dullness.
verses.hi: बासी, बेस्वाद, बदबूदार, रखा हुआ, जूठा और अपवित्र भोजन तामसिक लोगों को प्रिय है।
verses.short: Dark food: stale, leftover, tasteless, rotten. Junk that drags you down.
verses.notes: What is tamasic food? Stale, tasteless, spoiled, leftover or impure food. What does it do? It makes the mind dull.

verses.en: A sacrifice done as the rules direct, by people who want no reward, with the mind set on the thought "this is my duty", is of goodness.
verses.hi: जो यज्ञ विधि के अनुसार, फल की इच्छा न रखने वाले लोग, "यह करना ही चाहिए" यह सोचकर मन लगाकर करते हैं, वह सात्त्विक है।
verses.short: Pure worship is done because it's right, without expecting anything back.
verses.notes: What is a sattvic offering? One made as duty, without wanting anything back, as scripture guides. What makes it pure? The selfless motive.

verses.en: But a sacrifice done with an eye on the reward, or just for show, know that to be of passion, Arjuna.
verses.hi: पर हे भरतश्रेष्ठ, जो यज्ञ फल को ध्यान में रखकर या केवल दिखावे के लिए किया जाता है, उसे राजसिक जानो।
verses.short: Worship done for rewards or to show off is the passionate kind.
verses.notes: What is a rajasic offering? One done for rewards or to show off. How can we spot it? When we care more about recognition than the act itself.

verses.en: A sacrifice done without proper method, without sharing food, without sacred chants, without gifts to the priests and without faith is called a sacrifice of dullness.
verses.hi: जो यज्ञ बिना विधि के, बिना अन्न बाँटे, बिना मंत्र के, बिना दक्षिणा के और बिना श्रद्धा के किया जाता है, उसे तामसिक कहते हैं।
verses.short: Worship with no faith, no care, no sincerity and no giving is the dark kind.
verses.notes: What is a tamasic offering? One without guidance, without sharing food, without mantras, without gifts to priests and without faith. What is missing most? Faith and sincerity.

verses.en: Honouring the gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise, along with cleanliness, honesty, self-restraint and non-violence, is called discipline of the body.
verses.hi: देवताओं, ब्राह्मणों, गुरुओं और ज्ञानियों का सम्मान, पवित्रता, सरलता, ब्रह्मचर्य और अहिंसा को शरीर का तप कहते हैं।
verses.short: Discipline of the body: respecting teachers and elders, staying clean, honest, self-controlled and non-violent.
verses.notes: What is austerity of the body? Honouring the divine, teachers and the wise, along with cleanliness, simplicity, self-control and non-violence. Is this about hardship? No. It's about disciplined, respectful living.

verses.en: Speech that doesn't upset others and is true, pleasant and helpful, along with regular study of scripture, is called discipline of speech.
verses.hi: ऐसी वाणी जो किसी को परेशान न करे, सच्ची, प्यारी और भली हो, और शास्त्रों का नियमित अध्ययन, इसे वाणी का तप कहते हैं।
verses.short: Discipline of speech: saying what's true, kind and helpful, without hurting anyone.
verses.notes: What is austerity of speech? Words that are true, kind and helpful, and that don't upset others, plus regular study. Can this be practised daily? Yes. Every conversation is a chance.

verses.en: Peace of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control and purity of intention are called discipline of the mind.
verses.hi: मन की प्रसन्नता, सौम्यता, मौन, आत्म-संयम और भावों की शुद्धता को मन का तप कहते हैं।
verses.short: Discipline of the mind: calm, kind, quiet, self-controlled and pure thoughts.
verses.notes: What is austerity of the mind? Calm, kindness, silence, self-control and pure intentions. Why is it hardest? The mind is the hardest thing to discipline.

verses.en: This threefold discipline, practised with deep faith by people who are steady and want no reward, is said to be of goodness.
verses.hi: जब यह तीन तरह का तप पूरी श्रद्धा से, फल की इच्छा न रखने वाले स्थिर लोग करते हैं, तो उसे सात्त्विक कहते हैं।
verses.short: All three done with faith and no expectations? That's the purest discipline.
verses.notes: When is austerity sattvic? When done with deep faith, without wanting rewards. What ties all three together? A selfless heart.

verses.en: Discipline practised to gain respect, honour and worship, or just for show, is said here to be of passion. It is unstable and doesn't last.
verses.hi: जो तप सम्मान, मान और पूजा पाने के लिए या दिखावे के लिए किया जाता है, उसे यहाँ राजसिक कहा गया है। वह अस्थिर और नाशवान है।
verses.short: Discipline done for likes, respect and praise is the passionate kind. It doesn't last.
verses.notes: When is austerity rajasic? When done for respect, praise or show. What happens to it? It is unstable and short-lived.

verses.en: Discipline practised out of foolish stubbornness, by torturing oneself or to harm others, is said to be of dullness.
verses.hi: जो तप मूर्खतापूर्ण ज़िद से, खुद को कष्ट देकर या दूसरों का नुकसान करने के लिए किया जाता है, उसे तामसिक कहते हैं।
verses.short: Discipline that's self-torture or meant to harm others is the dark kind.
verses.notes: When is austerity tamasic? When done out of confusion, with self-torture or to harm others. What's the warning? Discipline without wisdom can become destructive.

verses.en: A gift given because it is right to give, to someone who can't repay it, at the right place and time, to a worthy person, is of goodness.
verses.hi: जो दान यह सोचकर दिया जाए कि देना ही चाहिए, ऐसे व्यक्ति को जो बदले में कुछ न कर सके, सही जगह, सही समय पर और योग्य व्यक्ति को, वह सात्त्विक है।
verses.short: Giving because it's right, to someone who deserves it, at the right time, expecting nothing back. That's pure giving.
verses.notes: What is sattvic giving? Giving as a duty, at the right time and place, to a worthy person, expecting nothing back. Why expect nothing? Giving with strings attached is a deal, not charity.

verses.en: But a gift given expecting something back, or aiming for a reward, or given unwillingly, is of passion.
verses.hi: पर जो दान बदले में कुछ पाने के लिए, या फल की चाह में, या मन मारकर दिया जाता है, वह राजसिक है।
verses.short: Giving to get something back, or giving reluctantly, is the passionate kind.
verses.notes: What is rajasic giving? Giving to get something back, for a reward, or reluctantly. How can we tell? If we feel resentful or keep score.

verses.en: A gift given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy people, without respect or with contempt, is of dullness.
verses.hi: जो दान गलत जगह और समय पर, अयोग्य लोगों को, बिना सम्मान के या अपमान के साथ दिया जाता है, वह तामसिक है।
verses.short: Giving at the wrong time, to the wrong person, with disrespect, is the dark kind.
verses.notes: What is tamasic giving? Giving at the wrong place or time, to the wrong person, without respect or with contempt. What's the lesson? How you give matters as much as what you give.

verses.en: "Om Tat Sat" is said to be the threefold name of the Supreme. By it, the priests, the Vedas and sacrifices were created in the beginning.
verses.hi: "ॐ तत् सत्" ब्रह्म का तीन तरह का नाम कहा गया है। इसी से शुरुआत में ब्राह्मण, वेद और यज्ञ रचे गए।
verses.short: "Om Tat Sat": three sacred words that point to the ultimate truth.
verses.notes: What does 'Om Tat Sat' mean? It is the threefold name of Brahman, used to sanctify actions. Where did it come from? It was the basis of priests, the Vedas and sacrifice from the beginning.

verses.en: So those who follow the Vedas always begin acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity, as the scriptures direct, by saying "Om".
verses.hi: इसलिए वेद मानने वाले लोग शास्त्र की विधि से यज्ञ, दान और तप के काम हमेशा "ॐ" बोलकर शुरू करते हैं।
verses.short: That's why the wise begin every sacred act by saying "Om".
verses.notes: Why say Om before acts? Those who follow the Vedas begin sacrifice, charity and austerity with Om. What does it do? It connects the act to the Divine.

verses.en: Saying "Tat", seekers of freedom perform acts of sacrifice, austerity and various kinds of charity without seeking any reward.
verses.hi: "तत्" बोलकर मोक्ष चाहने वाले लोग बिना फल की इच्छा के यज्ञ, तप और तरह-तरह के दान के काम करते हैं।
verses.short: Seekers say "Tat" and act without wanting rewards. It means: this is for the divine, not me.
verses.notes: What does 'Tat' signify? Acts done without seeking rewards, by those seeking liberation. What is the spirit behind it? 'This is for That,' for the Divine, not for me.

verses.en: The word "Sat" is used to mean reality and goodness. It is also used for any praiseworthy action, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, "सत्" शब्द सच्चाई और भलाई के अर्थ में इस्तेमाल होता है, और अच्छे कर्म के लिए भी "सत्" शब्द लगाया जाता है।
verses.short: "Sat" means truth and goodness. Any good deed is called Sat.
verses.notes: What does 'Sat' mean? Reality and goodness. It is also used for any auspicious act. Why use it? To mark actions as true and good.

verses.en: Steadiness in sacrifice, austerity and charity is also called "Sat", and so is any action done for that purpose.
verses.hi: यज्ञ, तप और दान में डटे रहना भी "सत्" कहलाता है, और इन्हीं के लिए जो काम किया जाए, उसे भी "सत्" नाम दिया जाता है।
verses.short: Staying committed to worship, discipline and giving is Sat too. So is any work done for that purpose.
verses.notes: What else is called 'Sat'? Steadiness in sacrifice, austerity and charity, and any action done for the Divine. What does this show? Dedicated action itself becomes sacred.

verses.en: Whatever is offered, given or practised as discipline without faith is called "asat", unreal, Arjuna. It is of no use here or hereafter.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, बिना श्रद्धा के जो हवन, दान, तप या कोई और कर्म किया जाता है, उसे "असत्" कहते हैं। उसका न यहाँ कोई लाभ है, न मरने के बाद।
verses.short: Anything done without faith, even if it looks spiritual, is empty. Faith is what makes it count.
verses.notes: What happens to acts done without faith? They are called 'asat': unreal, with no value here or hereafter. What is the lesson? Faith gives meaning to every action.

verses.en: Arjuna said: Mighty Krishna, I want to understand the true meaning of renunciation and of letting go, and how they differ.
verses.hi: अर्जुन ने कहा: हे महाबाहु कृष्ण, मुझे संन्यास का सार भी समझाइए और त्याग का भी, और यह भी कि दोनों में फ़र्क क्या है।
verses.short: Arjuna: "What's the real difference between renouncing and letting go?" The final chapter begins.
verses.notes: What does Arjuna ask in the final chapter? The true meaning of sannyasa (renunciation) and tyaga (letting go), and how they differ. Why ask this now? It ties together everything Krishna has taught about action.

verses.en: Krishna said: The wise say renunciation means giving up actions done out of desire. The insightful say letting go means giving up the results of all actions.
verses.hi: श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा: ज्ञानी लोग इच्छा से किए जाने वाले कर्मों को छोड़ना संन्यास कहते हैं। समझदार लोग सब कर्मों के फल को छोड़ना त्याग कहते हैं।
verses.short: Renouncing means dropping selfish actions. Letting go means doing your work but dropping the attachment to results.
verses.notes: What is the difference between sannyasa and tyaga? Sannyasa is giving up desire-driven actions; tyaga is giving up the fruits of all actions. Which does Krishna prefer? Tyaga: keep acting, but let go of results.

verses.en: Some thinkers say all action should be given up as flawed. Others say acts of sacrifice, charity and discipline should never be given up.
verses.hi: कुछ विचारक कहते हैं कि कर्म दोष भरा है, इसलिए उसे छोड़ देना चाहिए। दूसरे कहते हैं कि यज्ञ, दान और तप के कर्म कभी नहीं छोड़ने चाहिए।
verses.short: Some say quit all action. Others say keep doing good things like charity and discipline.
verses.notes: What do different sages say? Some say all action should be dropped as flawed; others say sacrifice, charity and austerity should never be dropped. Why mention both views? To set up Krishna's own clear answer.

verses.en: Hear my conclusion about letting go, best of the Bharatas. Letting go is said to be of three kinds, tiger among men.
verses.hi: हे भरतश्रेष्ठ, त्याग के बारे में मेरा निश्चय सुनो। हे पुरुषसिंह, त्याग तीन तरह का बताया गया है।
verses.short: Krishna: "Here's my final take. Letting go comes in three types."
verses.notes: What does Krishna say about tyaga? It comes in three kinds, and he will give his final view. Why three kinds? They match the three gunas.

verses.en: Acts of sacrifice, charity and discipline should not be given up; they should be done. Sacrifice, charity and discipline purify even the wise.
verses.hi: यज्ञ, दान और तप के कर्म नहीं छोड़ने चाहिए, उन्हें करना ही चाहिए। यज्ञ, दान और तप ज्ञानियों को भी पवित्र करते हैं।
verses.short: Worship, charity and discipline shouldn't be dropped. They purify even wise people.
verses.notes: Should sacrifice, charity and austerity be given up? No. They should be done because they purify even the wise. Why do they matter? They keep the heart clean.

verses.en: But even these actions should be done giving up attachment and results. This, Arjuna, is my firm and final view.
verses.hi: पर हे पार्थ, ये कर्म भी आसक्ति और फल छोड़कर ही करने चाहिए। यही मेरा पक्का और उत्तम मत है।
verses.short: But even these should be done without attachment or expecting results. That's my final answer.
verses.notes: What is Krishna's final view? Do these acts, but without attachment and without wanting results. Why is this the 'best' view? It keeps both the good of action and the freedom of detachment.

verses.en: Giving up a duty that is yours to do is not right. Abandoning it out of confusion is called letting go in dullness.
verses.hi: अपने तय कर्तव्य को छोड़ना ठीक नहीं है। मोह के कारण उसे छोड़ देना तामसिक त्याग कहलाता है।
verses.short: Ditching your duties out of confusion? That's the lazy, dark kind of quitting.
verses.notes: What is tamasic renunciation? Dropping one's duty out of confusion. Why is it wrong? It's avoidance, not true letting go.

verses.en: Someone who gives up an action because it is painful or out of fear of physical strain makes a passionate kind of letting go and doesn't gain its reward.
verses.hi: जो कर्म को दुख भरा मानकर या शरीर के कष्ट के डर से छोड़ देता है, वह राजसिक त्याग करता है और उसे त्याग का फल नहीं मिलता।
verses.short: Quitting because something's hard or uncomfortable? That's the restless kind, and it gets you nothing.
verses.notes: What is rajasic renunciation? Dropping duties because they are hard or painful. Does it bring results? No. It brings none of the benefits of real renunciation.

verses.en: When a required action is done simply because it should be done, Arjuna, giving up attachment and the result, that letting go is of goodness.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, जब तय कर्म केवल यह सोचकर किया जाता है कि यह करना ही है, और आसक्ति व फल छोड़ दिए जाते हैं, तो वह सात्त्विक त्याग है।
verses.short: Doing your duty fully while letting go of attachment and results? That's the pure kind.
verses.notes: What is sattvic renunciation? Doing your duty because it should be done, letting go of attachment and results. What makes it pure? Doing the work fully while giving up the ego's claim.

verses.en: Someone who lets go in goodness, intelligent and free from doubt, neither dislikes unpleasant work nor clings to pleasant work.
verses.hi: सत्त्व से भरा, समझदार और संदेह से मुक्त त्यागी न अप्रिय काम से नफ़रत करता है, न प्रिय काम से चिपकता है।
verses.short: A truly wise person doesn't avoid unpleasant work or cling to pleasant work. No doubts, just clarity.
verses.notes: How does a true renunciate treat unpleasant work? Without hating it, and doesn't cling to pleasant work either. What marks them? Clarity, wisdom and freedom from doubt.

verses.en: It is impossible for an embodied being to give up action completely. But whoever gives up the results of action is called one who has truly let go.
verses.hi: शरीरधारी के लिए कर्मों को पूरी तरह छोड़ना संभव नहीं है। पर जो कर्म-फल का त्याग करता है, उसी को त्यागी कहा जाता है।
verses.short: You can't stop acting while you have a body. Real letting go means letting go of results.
verses.notes: Can anyone give up action completely? No one with a body can. Who is the true renunciate then? The one who gives up the fruits of action.

verses.en: For those who haven't let go, the results of action, pleasant, unpleasant and mixed, come after death. But never for those who have renounced.
verses.hi: जो त्यागी नहीं हैं, उन्हें मरने के बाद कर्म का अच्छा, बुरा और मिला-जुला, तीन तरह का फल मिलता है। पर संन्यासियों को कभी नहीं।
verses.short: If you cling to results, you get good, bad or mixed karma. Let go and none of it sticks.
verses.notes: What results do non-renunciates get? Pleasant, unpleasant or mixed, after death. And true renunciates? None. They are free.

verses.en: Learn from me, mighty Arjuna, the five causes for the completion of all actions, as described in the philosophy of Sankhya.
verses.hi: हे महाबाहु, सांख्य दर्शन में बताए गए, सब कर्मों के पूरे होने के पाँच कारण मुझसे जानो।
verses.short: Every action has five causes. Let me break them down.
verses.notes: What will Krishna explain now? The five causes behind every action. Why does this matter? It shows we're not the only cause of what happens.

verses.en: The body, the doer, the various instruments, the many different efforts, and fifth, the divine factor.
verses.hi: शरीर, करने वाला, तरह-तरह के साधन, अलग-अलग तरह की कोशिशें, और पाँचवाँ दैव।
verses.short: The body, the doer, the senses, the various efforts, and divine will. Five factors behind every action.
verses.notes: What are the five causes of action? The body, the doer, the senses, the various energies, and the Divine (fate). What is the takeaway? Many factors work together in every action.

verses.en: Whatever action a person begins with body, speech or mind, right or wrong, these five are its causes.
verses.hi: इंसान शरीर, वाणी या मन से जो भी कर्म शुरू करता है, सही हो या गलत, उसके यही पाँच कारण हैं।
verses.short: Whatever you do with body, words or mind, right or wrong, these five are behind it.
verses.notes: Do these five causes apply to all actions? Yes, to everything done by body, speech or mind, right or wrong. What does that mean? No action happens by the ego alone.

verses.en: This being so, whoever sees the self alone as the doer, with an untrained mind, doesn't see clearly and is misguided.
verses.hi: ऐसा होने पर भी जो अधूरी समझ के कारण केवल आत्मा को करने वाला मानता है, वह गलत सोच वाला सही नहीं देखता।
verses.short: So thinking "I alone did this" is a limited view. You're only one of five factors.
verses.notes: What mistake do the unwise make? They see themselves alone as the doer. Why is this wrong? It ignores the other causes and inflates the ego.

verses.en: Someone free from the sense of "I am doing this", whose understanding is not stained, does not really kill even if they kill these people, and is not bound.
verses.hi: जिसमें "मैं करता हूँ" का भाव नहीं है और जिसकी बुद्धि लिप्त नहीं होती, वह इन लोगों को मारकर भी असल में नहीं मारता और न बँधता है।
verses.short: Someone with no "I did it" ego and a clean mind isn't bound by their actions.
verses.notes: How can someone act and not be bound? When free from 'I am the doer' and with an untainted mind, even great acts don't bind. Is this permission to do anything? No. Such a person, free of ego, naturally acts rightly.

verses.en: Knowledge, the object of knowledge and the knower are the three things that drive action. The instrument, the act and the doer are the three parts of action.
verses.hi: ज्ञान, जानने योग्य और जानने वाला, ये तीन कर्म के प्रेरक हैं। साधन, कर्म और करने वाला, ये तीन कर्म के अंग हैं।
verses.short: Knowledge, the thing known and the knower drive action. The tool, the act and the doer make it happen.
verses.notes: What drives action? Knowledge, the thing known and the knower. What makes up action? The instrument, the act and the doer.

verses.en: Knowledge, action and the doer are each said to be of three kinds, according to the qualities, in the study of the qualities. Hear about them as they are.
verses.hi: गुणों के शास्त्र में ज्ञान, कर्म और करने वाले को गुणों के अनुसार तीन-तीन तरह का बताया गया है। उन्हें भी ठीक-ठीक सुनो।
verses.short: Knowledge, action and the doer each come in three types too. Here's how.
verses.notes: What will Krishna classify next? Knowledge, action and the doer, each in three types by the gunas. Why classify? It helps us see which quality guides us.

verses.en: Knowledge by which one sees one unchanging reality in all beings, undivided in the divided, know that as knowledge of goodness.
verses.hi: जिस ज्ञान से व्यक्ति सब प्राणियों में एक अविनाशी सत्ता देखता है, बँटे हुओं में अबँटा, उस ज्ञान को सात्त्विक जानो।
verses.short: Pure knowledge sees one unchanging reality in all beings. Unity in diversity.
verses.notes: What is sattvic knowledge? Seeing one unchanging reality in all beings, undivided in the divided. How does it feel? Like unity and connection with everyone.

verses.en: Knowledge that sees all beings as separate, with different natures of their own, know that as knowledge of passion.
verses.hi: जो ज्ञान सब प्राणियों को अलग-अलग, अपने-अपने अलग स्वभाव वाला मानता है, उस ज्ञान को राजसिक जानो।
verses.short: Passionate knowledge sees everyone as totally separate and different. Us versus them.
verses.notes: What is rajasic knowledge? Seeing beings only as separate and different from one another. What does it lead to? Division and comparison.

verses.en: Knowledge that clings to one small thing as if it were everything, without reason, without grasping the truth, and narrow, is said to be of dullness.
verses.hi: जो ज्ञान किसी एक छोटी चीज़ को ही सब कुछ मानकर उसमें चिपका रहता है, बिना तर्क के, बिना सच समझे और संकुचित होता है, उसे तामसिक कहते हैं।
verses.short: Dark knowledge fixates on one small thing as if it's everything. Narrow, illogical, shallow.
verses.notes: What is tamasic knowledge? Clinging to one small thing as if it were everything, without reason or truth. What is an example? Narrow, stubborn thinking that refuses to see the bigger picture.

verses.en: Action that is required, done without attachment, without liking or disliking, by someone who doesn't want the result, is said to be of goodness.
verses.hi: जो तय कर्म बिना आसक्ति के, बिना राग-द्वेष के, फल न चाहने वाले व्यक्ति द्वारा किया जाता है, उसे सात्त्विक कहते हैं।
verses.short: Pure action: doing what's needed, without attachment, likes or dislikes, or wanting rewards.
verses.notes: What is sattvic action? Duty done without attachment, likes or dislikes, and without wanting results. How does it feel? Calm and clean.

verses.en: But action done to fulfil desires, or with ego, and with a lot of strain, is said to be of passion.
verses.hi: पर जो कर्म इच्छाएँ पूरी करने के लिए, या अहंकार के साथ, और बहुत मेहनत से किया जाता है, उसे राजसिक कहते हैं।
verses.short: Passionate action: lots of stress and effort, all to satisfy your ego and desires.
verses.notes: What is rajasic action? Action done with great strain, driven by desire or ego. What's the giveaway? Stress and the need for credit.

verses.en: Action started out of confusion, without regard for consequences, loss, harm to others or one's own ability, is said to be of dullness.
verses.hi: जो कर्म नतीजे, नुकसान, दूसरों को चोट और अपनी क्षमता की परवाह किए बिना, मोह से शुरू किया जाता है, उसे तामसिक कहते हैं।
verses.short: Dark action: done blindly, ignoring consequences, harm to others, and your own limits.
verses.notes: What is tamasic action? Action begun in confusion, without thinking about consequences, harm or ability. What's the lesson? Think before you act.

verses.en: A doer free from attachment, without ego, full of resolve and enthusiasm, and unchanged by success or failure, is said to be of goodness.
verses.hi: जो करने वाला आसक्ति से मुक्त है, अहंकार की बात नहीं करता, धैर्य और उत्साह से भरा है, और सफलता-असफलता में नहीं बदलता, वह सात्त्विक कहलाता है।
verses.short: A pure doer: no attachment, no bragging, steady, enthusiastic, unbothered by success or failure.
verses.notes: What is a sattvic doer? Unattached, humble, steady and enthusiastic, unchanged by success or failure. Is this a good role model? Yes. It describes a balanced, effective person.

verses.en: A doer who is attached, wants the results, is greedy, harmful and impure, and swings between joy and grief, is said to be of passion.
verses.hi: जो करने वाला आसक्त है, फल चाहता है, लालची, हिंसक और अपवित्र है, और खुशी-गम में डूबता-उतराता है, वह राजसिक कहलाता है।
verses.short: A passionate doer: attached, result-obsessed, greedy, harmful, and on an emotional rollercoaster.
verses.notes: What is a rajasic doer? Passionate, eager for results, greedy, harmful, impure and swayed by joy and sorrow. What drives them? Wanting the outcome.

verses.en: A doer who is undisciplined, crude, stubborn, deceitful, spiteful, lazy, gloomy and always putting things off is said to be of dullness.
verses.hi: जो करने वाला अनुशासनहीन, असभ्य, अकड़ू, धोखेबाज़, दूसरों का काम बिगाड़ने वाला, आलसी, उदास और काम टालने वाला है, वह तामसिक कहलाता है।
verses.short: A dark doer: careless, stubborn, dishonest, lazy, gloomy and always procrastinating.
verses.notes: What is a tamasic doer? Undisciplined, crude, stubborn, deceitful, lazy, gloomy and procrastinating. Can someone change? Yes. Recognising these traits is the first step.

verses.en: Now hear, Arjuna, about the three kinds of understanding and of resolve, according to the qualities, explained fully and one by one.
verses.hi: हे धनंजय, अब गुणों के अनुसार बुद्धि और धृति के तीन-तीन प्रकार पूरी तरह और अलग-अलग सुनो।
verses.short: Now the three types of intellect and willpower.
verses.notes: What's explained next? The three kinds of intellect and determination. Why do these matter? They guide every decision we make.

verses.en: Understanding that knows when to act and when to stop, what should and shouldn't be done, what to fear and what not to fear, and what binds and what frees, is of goodness, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, जो बुद्धि जानती है कि कब कर्म करना है और कब रुकना है, क्या करना चाहिए और क्या नहीं, किससे डरना है और किससे नहीं, और क्या बाँधता है और क्या मुक्त करता है, वह सात्त्विक है।
verses.short: Pure intellect knows what to do and avoid, when to fear and when not, what binds and what frees.
verses.notes: What is sattvic intellect? It knows when to act and when to step back, what to do and avoid, what to fear and what not to, what binds and what frees. What is it, in short? Clear judgment.

verses.en: Understanding that gets right and wrong, and what should and shouldn't be done, mixed up, is of passion, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, जिस बुद्धि से धर्म-अधर्म और करने-न करने योग्य बातें ठीक से समझ नहीं आतीं, वह राजसिक है।
verses.short: Passionate intellect gets confused between right and wrong, what to do and what not to do.
verses.notes: What is rajasic intellect? It mixes up right and wrong, what to do and what not to do. Why? Desire clouds its judgment.

verses.en: Understanding that, covered by darkness, takes wrong to be right and sees everything backwards, is of dullness, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, जो बुद्धि अंधकार से ढकी होकर अधर्म को धर्म मानती है और हर चीज़ को उल्टा देखती है, वह तामसिक है।
verses.short: Dark intellect sees wrong as right and flips every value upside down.
verses.notes: What is tamasic intellect? Wrapped in darkness, it sees wrong as right and turns everything upside down. What's the danger? It can justify anything.

verses.en: The unwavering resolve, held through yoga, by which one steadies the workings of the mind, breath and senses, is of goodness, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, योग से टिकी जिस अटल धृति से व्यक्ति मन, प्राण और इंद्रियों के कामों को थामे रखता है, वह सात्त्विक है।
verses.short: Pure willpower keeps your mind, breath and senses steady through practice. Unshakeable focus.
verses.notes: What is sattvic determination? Steady control over mind, breath and senses through yoga. How does it feel? Calm, firm, unwavering.

verses.en: The resolve by which one holds on to duty, pleasure and wealth, wanting the results out of attachment, is of passion, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, जिस धृति से व्यक्ति आसक्ति के कारण फल चाहते हुए धर्म, काम और अर्थ को पकड़े रहता है, हे पार्थ, वह राजसिक है।
verses.short: Passionate willpower holds tight to duty, desire and wealth, but only for what you'll get out of it.
verses.notes: What is rajasic determination? Holding on to duty, pleasure and wealth with attachment, wanting results. What is the difference from sattvic? It is persistent, but for selfish ends.

verses.en: The resolve by which a foolish person won't let go of sleep, fear, grief, gloom and arrogance is of dullness, Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ, जिस धृति से मूर्ख व्यक्ति नींद, डर, शोक, उदासी और घमंड को नहीं छोड़ता, वह तामसिक है।
verses.short: Dark willpower is just being stubborn about not giving up sleep, fear, sadness and ego.
verses.notes: What is tamasic determination? Stubbornly clinging to sleep, fear, grief, depression and arrogance. Is that really 'determination'? Yes, but in the wrong direction: stubbornly staying stuck.

verses.en: Now hear from me, Arjuna, about the three kinds of happiness. There is a happiness that one comes to enjoy through practice, in which sorrow comes to an end,
verses.hi: हे भरतश्रेष्ठ, अब मुझसे तीन तरह के सुख के बारे में सुनो। एक सुख ऐसा है जिसमें व्यक्ति अभ्यास से रमता है और जिसमें दुखों का अंत हो जाता है,
verses.short: Now the three kinds of happiness. Real joy builds with practice and ends your pain.
verses.notes: What is the next topic? The three kinds of happiness. What does real happiness do? It grows with practice and ends sorrow.

verses.en: which feels like poison at first but like nectar in the end, born from a clear understanding of the self. That happiness is said to be of goodness.
verses.hi: जो शुरू में ज़हर जैसा लगता है पर अंत में अमृत जैसा होता है, और आत्मा की साफ़ समझ से पैदा होता है। वह सुख सात्त्विक कहा गया है।
verses.short: Pure happiness feels like medicine at first but becomes nectar. It comes from a calm, clear mind.
verses.notes: What is sattvic happiness? Like poison at first but like nectar in the end, born from a clear mind. What is an example? Discipline, study or exercise: hard at first, rewarding later.

verses.en: Happiness from contact between the senses and their objects, which feels like nectar at first but like poison in the end, is said to be of passion.
verses.hi: इंद्रियों और विषयों के मेल से मिलने वाला सुख, जो शुरू में अमृत जैसा पर अंत में ज़हर जैसा होता है, राजसिक कहा गया है।
verses.short: Passionate happiness feels like nectar at first but turns into poison. Instant gratification, long-term regret.
verses.notes: What is rajasic happiness? Like nectar at first but like poison in the end, from the senses meeting objects. What is an example? Binge-watching or junk food: fun now, regret later.

verses.en: Happiness that deludes the self from beginning to end, arising from sleep, laziness and carelessness, is said to be of dullness.
verses.hi: जो सुख शुरू से अंत तक आत्मा को भ्रम में रखता है और नींद, आलस और लापरवाही से पैदा होता है, उसे तामसिक कहते हैं।
verses.short: Dark happiness comes from oversleeping, laziness and carelessness. It fools you from start to finish.
verses.notes: What is tamasic happiness? Delusion from start to finish, coming from sleep, laziness and carelessness. Why is it the lowest? It never brings clarity at any stage.

verses.en: There is no being on earth, or among the gods in heaven, that is free from these three qualities born of nature.
verses.hi: धरती पर या स्वर्ग में देवताओं में भी ऐसा कोई प्राणी नहीं है जो प्रकृति से पैदा हुए इन तीन गुणों से मुक्त हो।
verses.short: No one, on earth or in heaven, is free from these three energies.
verses.notes: Is anyone free of the gunas? No being on earth or in heaven is free from these three. What does that mean? Everyone works with these forces; the goal is to rise above them.

verses.en: Arjuna, the work of priests, warriors, merchants and labourers is divided according to the qualities born of their own nature.
verses.hi: हे परंतप, ब्राह्मणों, क्षत्रियों, वैश्यों और शूद्रों के कर्म उनके स्वभाव से पैदा हुए गुणों के अनुसार बाँटे गए हैं।
verses.short: People's roles in society are meant to match their natural qualities, not their birth.
verses.notes: How are duties divided? According to qualities born of one's nature, not merely by birth. What is the point? Work should suit one's nature.

verses.en: Calm, self-control, discipline, purity, patience, honesty, knowledge, wisdom and faith are the natural work of a priest.
verses.hi: शांति, इंद्रियों पर काबू, तप, पवित्रता, क्षमा, सरलता, ज्ञान, विज्ञान और आस्था, ये ब्राह्मण के स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं।
verses.short: Thinkers and teachers by nature: calm, disciplined, pure, patient, honest, wise and full of faith.
verses.notes: What qualities suit a teacher or priest by nature? Calm, self-control, austerity, purity, patience, honesty, knowledge, wisdom and faith. Are these only for priests? No. They are good qualities anyone can grow.

verses.en: Courage, vigour, determination, skill, not running from battle, generosity and leadership are the natural work of a warrior.
verses.hi: वीरता, तेज, धैर्य, कुशलता, युद्ध से न भागना, दान और नेतृत्व, ये क्षत्रिय के स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं।
verses.short: Leaders and protectors by nature: brave, energetic, steady, skilled, generous and never running from a fight.
verses.notes: What qualities suit a leader or warrior? Courage, vigour, steadiness, skill, not fleeing battle, generosity and leadership. Why mention this to Arjuna? These are his natural qualities, so fighting for right fits him.

verses.en: Farming, caring for cattle and trade are the natural work of a merchant. Work that serves others is the natural work of a labourer.
verses.hi: खेती, गौ-पालन और व्यापार वैश्य के स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं। सेवा वाला काम शूद्र का स्वाभाविक कर्म है।
verses.short: Builders, farmers and traders by nature create wealth. Those who love serving keep everything running.
verses.notes: What work suits other natures? Farming, cattle care and trade suit some; service suits others. Is one work better than another? The next verses say perfection comes from doing your own work well.

verses.en: Each person who is devoted to their own work reaches perfection. Hear how someone devoted to their own work finds perfection.
verses.hi: अपने-अपने कर्म में लगा इंसान सिद्धि पाता है। अपने कर्म में लगा व्यक्ति सिद्धि कैसे पाता है, वह सुनो।
verses.short: Dedicate yourself to your own natural work and you reach perfection. Here's how.
verses.notes: How does one reach perfection? By being devoted to one's own work. Is any work spiritual? Yes, when done with devotion.

verses.en: By worshipping, through their own work, the one from whom all beings come and by whom all this is pervaded, a person finds perfection.
verses.hi: जिससे सब प्राणी पैदा होते हैं और जिससे यह सब व्याप्त है, अपने कर्म से उसकी पूजा करके इंसान सिद्धि पाता है।
verses.short: Do your own work as worship of the one who created everything, and you'll reach perfection.
verses.notes: How does work become worship? By offering your work to the One from whom all beings arise. What is the result? Perfection, through everyday duties.

verses.en: It is better to do your own duty imperfectly than someone else's duty well. Doing the work set by your own nature, you incur no sin.
verses.hi: दूसरे का धर्म अच्छी तरह निभाने से अपना धर्म अधूरे ढंग से निभाना बेहतर है। अपने स्वभाव से तय कर्म करने वाले को पाप नहीं लगता।
verses.short: Your own path done imperfectly beats someone else's done perfectly. Doing your own thing keeps you clean.
verses.notes: Why is one's own duty better? Even imperfect, it suits your nature and doesn't lead to wrong. Is this repeated from Chapter 3? Yes. Krishna repeats it because it's so important.

verses.en: Arjuna, don't give up the work you were born to, even if it has flaws. Every undertaking is covered by some flaw, as fire is by smoke.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, अपने स्वाभाविक कर्म को, उसमें दोष हो तब भी, नहीं छोड़ना चाहिए। हर काम में कोई न कोई दोष ऐसे होता है जैसे आग में धुआँ।
verses.short: Don't quit your work just because it's imperfect. Every effort has some flaw, like fire has smoke.
verses.notes: Should we leave work because it has flaws? No. All work has flaws, like fire has smoke. What is the lesson? Perfect work doesn't exist; do yours anyway.

verses.en: Someone whose mind is unattached everywhere, who has mastered themselves and is free from craving, reaches through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.
verses.hi: जिसकी बुद्धि कहीं आसक्त नहीं, जिसने खुद को जीत लिया है और जो लालसा से मुक्त है, वह संन्यास से नैष्कर्म्य की परम सिद्धि पाता है।
verses.short: Unattached, self-controlled, free from craving. Through letting go, you reach the ultimate freedom.
verses.notes: What is the highest perfection? Freedom from action's bondage, reached through detachment, self-control and freedom from craving. How is it reached? Through renunciation in the true sense.

verses.en: Learn from me briefly, Arjuna, how one who has reached perfection reaches the Supreme, the highest goal of knowledge.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, मुझसे संक्षेप में जानो कि सिद्धि पाया हुआ व्यक्ति ब्रह्म को कैसे पाता है, जो ज्ञान की परम निष्ठा है।
verses.short: Here's the short version of how a perfected person reaches the ultimate.
verses.notes: What will Krishna explain now? How a perfected person reaches Brahman, the peak of knowledge. Why 'briefly'? He's summing up the path.

verses.en: Joined with a pure understanding, steadying oneself with resolve, letting go of sound and other sense objects, and setting aside attraction and aversion,
verses.hi: शुद्ध बुद्धि से जुड़कर, धैर्य से खुद को वश में करके, शब्द आदि विषयों को छोड़कर और राग-द्वेष को दूर करके,
verses.short: A clear mind, steady self-control, stepping back from distractions, and dropping love-hate drama.
verses.notes: What qualities lead to Brahman? A pure mind, firm self-control, letting go of sense pleasures, and dropping attraction and aversion. Where does it start? With a purified intellect.

verses.en: living in solitude, eating lightly, controlling speech, body and mind, always devoted to meditation and rooted in detachment,
verses.hi: एकांत में रहकर, हल्का भोजन करके, वाणी, शरीर और मन को वश में रखकर, हमेशा ध्यान-योग में लगकर और वैराग्य का सहारा लेकर,
verses.short: Enjoying solitude, eating light, controlling body, speech and mind, meditating, staying detached.
verses.notes: How does the seeker live? In solitude, eating lightly, controlling speech, body and mind, meditating and detached. Is this for everyone? It's the ideal; anyone can take small steps toward it.

verses.en: giving up ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, free from "mine" and at peace, one becomes fit to be one with the Supreme.
verses.hi: अहंकार, बल, घमंड, काम, क्रोध और संग्रह को छोड़कर, "मेरेपन" से मुक्त और शांत व्यक्ति ब्रह्म बनने के योग्य हो जाता है।
verses.short: Dropping ego, power trips, pride, lust, anger and hoarding. No "mine". Total peace.
verses.notes: What must be dropped? Ego, force, pride, desire, anger and possessiveness. What remains? Peace, and readiness for oneness with Brahman.

verses.en: One with the Supreme and serene, such a person neither grieves nor craves. Seeing all beings as equal, they gain supreme devotion to me.
verses.hi: ब्रह्म में स्थित और प्रसन्न मन वाला व्यक्ति न शोक करता है, न कुछ चाहता है। सब प्राणियों में समान भाव रखकर वह मेरी परम भक्ति पाता है।
verses.short: At peace, without grief or craving, seeing everyone as equal, you find the highest love for me.
verses.notes: What is the state of oneness like? Serene, without grief or craving, seeing all beings equally. What follows? Supreme devotion to Krishna.

verses.en: Through devotion they come to know who and what I truly am. Then, knowing me truly, they enter into me.
verses.hi: भक्ति से वह मुझे सच में जानता है कि मैं कौन हूँ और कितना हूँ। फिर मुझे सच में जानकर वह मुझमें समा जाता है।
verses.short: Through that love you truly know who I am. And knowing me, you become one with me.
verses.notes: How does one truly know Krishna? Through devotion: who he is and what he is. What happens then? They enter into him.

verses.en: Even while always doing all kinds of work, someone who takes refuge in me reaches by my grace the eternal, unchanging home.
verses.hi: मेरी शरण लेने वाला व्यक्ति हमेशा सब तरह के कर्म करते हुए भी मेरी कृपा से सनातन, अविनाशी पद को पाता है।
verses.short: Keep doing your work while trusting me, and by my grace you reach the eternal home.
verses.notes: Can one reach the goal while working? Yes. Taking refuge in Krishna while doing all work, one reaches the eternal by his grace. What role does grace play? It completes what effort begins.

verses.en: Mentally offering all your actions to me, making me your goal and relying on steady understanding, always keep your mind on me.
verses.hi: मन से सारे कर्म मुझे अर्पित करके, मुझे लक्ष्य मानकर और बुद्धि-योग का सहारा लेकर, हमेशा मुझमें मन लगाए रखो।
verses.short: Mentally hand over all your actions to me, make me your goal, and keep your thoughts on me.
verses.notes: What does Krishna ask Arjuna? Offer all actions to him in your mind, make him your goal and keep your mind on him. What is 'buddhi yoga'? The yoga of a steady, devoted intellect.

verses.en: With your mind on me, you will cross every obstacle by my grace. But if out of ego you don't listen, you will be lost.
verses.hi: मुझमें मन लगाकर तुम मेरी कृपा से हर मुश्किल पार कर जाओगे। पर अगर अहंकार के कारण नहीं सुनोगे, तो नष्ट हो जाओगे।
verses.short: Keep me in mind and you'll get through every obstacle. Ignore me out of ego and you'll struggle.
verses.notes: What will happen if Arjuna keeps his mind on Krishna? By grace, he'll overcome all obstacles. And if he doesn't listen? Out of ego, he will be lost.

verses.en: If, relying on ego, you think "I will not fight," your decision is pointless. Your own nature will push you into it.
verses.hi: अगर तुम अहंकार के भरोसे सोचते हो कि "मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा," तो तुम्हारा यह निश्चय बेकार है। तुम्हारी प्रकृति तुम्हें इसमें लगा देगी।
verses.short: "I won't fight"? Your ego is talking. Your own nature will push you to act anyway.
verses.notes: What if Arjuna says 'I won't fight'? His resolve will fail. His own nature will push him to act. What does this teach? We can't escape our nature by force of will.

verses.en: Arjuna, bound by your own work born of your nature, what you don't want to do out of confusion, you will do anyway, even against your will.
verses.hi: हे कौन्तेय, अपने स्वभाव से पैदा हुए कर्म से बँधे तुम, जो मोह के कारण नहीं करना चाहते, वह मजबूर होकर भी करोगे।
verses.short: What you refuse to do out of confusion, your nature will make you do anyway.
verses.notes: Why will Arjuna act anyway? His own nature and duty will compel him, even against his wish. So why choose consciously? Acting with understanding is better than being dragged by nature.

verses.en: The Lord lives in the heart of all beings, Arjuna, moving them all by his power as if they were mounted on a machine.
verses.hi: हे अर्जुन, ईश्वर सब प्राणियों के हृदय में रहता है और अपनी माया से सब प्राणियों को ऐसे घुमाता है जैसे वे किसी यंत्र पर चढ़े हों।
verses.short: The divine lives in every heart and moves all beings, like riders on a wheel.
verses.notes: Where is the Lord? In the heart of every being, moving them as if on a machine by his power. What does this mean for us? The Divine is always within, guiding life.

verses.en: Take refuge in him alone with your whole being, Arjuna. By his grace you will reach supreme peace and the eternal home.
verses.hi: हे भारत, पूरे मन से उसी की शरण में जाओ। उसकी कृपा से तुम परम शांति और सनातन धाम पाओगे।
verses.short: Turn to the divine with everything you've got. By that grace you'll find supreme peace.
verses.notes: What does Krishna advise? Take refuge in the Lord with your whole being. What comes from that? Supreme peace and the eternal home, by his grace.

verses.en: So I have given you this knowledge, the most secret of secrets. Think it over fully, and then do as you choose.
verses.hi: इस तरह मैंने तुम्हें यह रहस्यों से भी गहरा रहस्य वाला ज्ञान बताया। इस पर पूरी तरह विचार करो, फिर जैसा चाहो वैसा करो।
verses.short: That's the deepest wisdom. Think it through fully, then do what you choose. Your call.
verses.notes: Does Krishna force Arjuna? No. He says: reflect on all this fully, then do as you wish. Why give the choice? Real change comes from understanding, not orders.

verses.en: Hear again my supreme word, the most secret of all. You are deeply loved by me, so I will tell you what is good for you.
verses.hi: सबसे गहरे रहस्य वाला मेरा परम वचन फिर से सुनो। तुम मुझे बहुत प्रिय हो, इसलिए मैं तुम्हारे भले की बात कहूँगा।
verses.short: "Listen to my most secret message once more. I'm telling you because I care about you deeply."
verses.notes: Why does Krishna speak again? Because Arjuna is very dear to him, he shares the most secret teaching. What is it for? Arjuna's good.

verses.en: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me and bow to me. You will come to me, I promise you truly, because you are dear to me.
verses.hi: मुझमें मन लगाओ, मेरे भक्त बनो, मेरी पूजा करो और मुझे प्रणाम करो। तुम मुझे ही पाओगे, मैं तुमसे सच्चा वादा करता हूँ, क्योंकि तुम मुझे प्रिय हो।
verses.short: Keep your mind on me, love me, honour me, bow to me. You'll come to me. That's my promise.
verses.notes: What is Krishna's promise? Think of him, be devoted, worship and bow, and you will surely come to him. Why does he promise? 'Because you are dear to me.'
